title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
summary: This paper explores token compression techniques for Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) to reduce input token cost during inference. The research addresses the high cost of visual tokens when Omni-LLMs process audio, video, and text jointly.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning Model for Cross-Modality Super-Resolution in Fluorescence Microscopy
summary: This research introduces a physics-informed deep learning model for cross-modality super-resolution in fluorescence microscopy. The model aims to generate high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while ensuring consistency with optical image formation principles.

title: Learning-based Seam Correspondence Reconstruction in Sewing Patterns
summary: This paper presents a graph-based learning framework for reconstructing two-level stitching information in digital sewing patterns. The method aims to automate seam correspondence reconstruction, which is crucial for 3D modeling and typically requires labor-intensive expert specification.

title: DART: A Degradation-Aware Recurrent Transformer for Archival Film Restoration
summary: This research introduces DART, a Degradation-Aware Recurrent Transformer, for archival film restoration. The model addresses compound degradations in historical footage like scratches, blur, and flicker, without relying on clean reference videos.

title: Stokes-Informed Diffusion for Robust Linear Polarization Estimation
summary: This research proposes a Stokes-Informed Diffusion method for robust linear polarization estimation from a single RGB image. The technique aims to extract polarization cues, useful for applications like material detection, without requiring dedicated hardware.

title: HERMES: Heterogeneous Edge-Relational Multi-Head Embedded SSM Attention for Traffic Conflict Prediction at Signalized Intersections
summary: This paper introduces HERMES, a Heterogeneous Edge-Relational Multi-Head Embedded SSM Attention model, for predicting traffic conflicts at signalized intersections. The method aims to better represent complex multi-agent interactions for proactive traffic safety assessment.

title: PhysCoRe: Physics-Corrected Residual World Models for Material-Aware Deformable Dynamics
summary: This research presents PhysCoRe, Physics-Corrected Residual World Models, to predict the dynamics of deformable objects during robotic manipulation. The model aims to improve generalization and accuracy by incorporating physical corrections into learned material-aware dynamics.

title: Scalable Low-Cost Laboratory Automation: A Digital Twin-Integrated Robotic Platform for Autonomous Liquid Handling (RAINBOTTM)
summary: This work introduces RAINBOT™, a low-cost, openly reproducible robotic platform integrated with a digital twin for autonomous liquid handling in laboratories. The system aims to address the high cost and proprietary nature of commercial lab automation.

title: Safe and Scalable Multi-Drone Payload Transport via CBF-based Reinforcement Learning with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
summary: This research proposes a method for safe and scalable multi-drone payload transport using CBF-based Reinforcement Learning and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. The approach tackles the complex dynamics of coupled drones, cables, and payloads for applications like logistics.

title: FELT: Generating Tactile Signals from Vision for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation
summary: This research introduces FELT, a method for generating tactile signals from visual input to facilitate visuo-tactile manipulation in robotics. The approach aims to overcome the scarcity of tactile data needed for learning robust manipulation policies.

title: Self-Supervised Bio-Inspired Robotic Trajectory Planning with Obstacle Avoidance
summary: This paper explores self-supervised, bio-inspired methods for robotic trajectory planning that incorporate obstacle avoidance. The research aims to generate collision-free and efficient robot trajectories in complex environments, addressing the computational expense of traditional planners.

title: Emergent Compositional Skills in Mixture-of-Experts VLAs
summary: This research investigates how Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can learn emergent compositional robot policies from expert demonstrations. The study focuses on whether such systems can implicitly decompose complex tasks.

title: Robostral Navigate
summary: Robostral Navigate proposes a navigation system designed to generalize across various robot embodiments and minimize sensor assumptions for scalable deployment. It aims to reduce reliance on specific hardware like depth sensors or pre-built maps.

title: URF: A Unified Robot Control-Policy Framework for Stable Contact Aware Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces URF, a Unified Robot Control-Policy Framework, for stable contact-aware manipulation. It addresses challenges in separating high-level learned policies from low-level controllers, especially in rigid contact scenarios, to ensure stable robot interaction.

title: Distributed Model-Based Diffusion For Scalable Multi-Robot Trajectory Optimization
summary: This research proposes Distributed Model-Based Diffusion for scalable trajectory optimization in multi-robot systems. The method addresses the challenges of navigating complex, non-convex environments, extending a promising optimization paradigm from single-robot applications.

title: TableVerse: A Large-scale Tabletop Dataset with Real-world Grounded Layouts for Generalizable Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces TableVerse, a large-scale tabletop dataset featuring real-world grounded layouts, designed to support the development of generalizable robotic manipulation policies. It aims to provide high-fidelity scene data to overcome limitations of synthetic data generation.

title: ZONDA: Zero-shot Object Navigation with Dynamic Avoidance in Multi-floor Environments
summary: This research proposes ZONDA, a zero-shot object navigation system with dynamic avoidance for robots in multi-floor environments. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by accounting for cross-floor topologies and dynamic obstacles like pedestrians.

title: A Real-Time Generalized Nash Equilibrium Framework for Interaction-Aware Autonomous Driving in Mixed Traffic
summary: This paper introduces a real-time Generalized Nash Equilibrium framework for interaction-aware autonomous driving in mixed-traffic environments. The framework addresses the complex challenge of safe and efficient navigation for Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) alongside human drivers.

title: GuidedAttention: Interpretable and Correctable Visual Attention for OOD-Robust Robot Manipulation via Imitation Learning
summary: Proposes GuidedAttention, a visuomotor imitation learning framework that provides interpretable and correctable visual attention for out-of-distribution robust robot manipulation.

title: Human-Inspired Framework for Robotic Craniotomy: Integrating Multimodal Fusion and Adaptive Trajectory Adjustment
summary: Introduces a human-inspired framework for robotic craniotomy that integrates multimodal data fusion and adaptive trajectory adjustment to improve safety and compensate for intraoperative errors.

title: RL-MACRO: A Cybernetic Closed-Loop Intelligence Framework for Multimodal Adaptive Robotic Craniotomy
summary: Presents RL-MACRO, a cybernetic closed-loop intelligence framework for multimodal adaptive robotic craniotomy that continuously regulates tool-tissue interactions for safety and efficiency.

title: FORGE-plus: Force-Budgeted Recovery for Contact-Rich Assembly with a Frozen LLM Supervisor
summary: Introduces FORGE-plus, a two-layer framework for force-budgeted recovery in contact-rich robotic assembly, using force-conditioned reinforcement learning with an LLM supervisor.

title: Factorized Spatio-Temporal Convolutions for Human Pose Estimation from Planar Lidar
summary: Proposes using factorized spatio-temporal convolutions for human pose estimation from planar lidar, enabling safe navigation and socially aware interaction for service robots with limited computational resources.

title: Grasp, Handover, Rotate: Bimanual Object Reorientation via Compositional Diffusion and Energy-Based Optimization
summary: Presents a method for bimanual object reorientation, allowing robots to pick, handover, and rotate objects using compositional diffusion and energy-based optimization.

title: GLAM-SLAM: Real-time Gaussian Large-scale Mapping via Flow Densification and Spatial Decomposition
summary: Introduces GLAM-SLAM, a real-time Gaussian-splatting-based monocular SLAM system for large-scale mapping that reduces GPU memory requirements for long-horizon applications.

title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
summary: Introduces GS-Agent, an agentic system capable of creating dynamic and physically realistic 4D virtual worlds from natural language descriptions using generative simulation.

title: Beyond Episodic Evaluation: Memory Architectural Bottlenecks in Sequential Embodied Question Answering
summary: Explores memory architectural bottlenecks in sequential embodied question answering, highlighting the need for robots to accumulate, retain, and selectively reuse information for continuous operation beyond episodic evaluations.

title: Scale Up Strategically: Learning Compositional Generalization via Bias-Aware Evaluation and Data Collection for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Presents a diagnostic framework to improve compositional generalization in robotic manipulation by addressing biases in evaluation and data collection, allowing robots to better follow diverse instructions.

title: AXIS: A Growable Community-Driven Data Engine for Scalable Robot Manipulation
summary: Introduces AXIS, a growable community-driven data engine designed to provide diverse and high-quality demonstration data for scalable robot manipulation learning.

title: HGeo-TopoMap: Boosting Topological Mapping with Hierarchical Geometric Priors
summary: Presents HGeo-TopoMap, a system that boosts topological mapping for autonomous driving perception systems by leveraging hierarchical geometric priors to identify road information like centerlines and traffic signs.

title: Compact Latent Coordination for Autonomous Vehicles at Unsignalized Intersections
summary: Addresses the challenge of coordinating autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections by proposing a compact latent coordination method for multi-agent reinforcement learning systems.

title: i2Nav-Robot: A Large-Scale Indoor-Outdoor Robot Dataset for Multi-Sensor Fusion Navigation
summary: Introduces i2Nav-Robot, a large-scale indoor-outdoor dataset designed for multi-sensor fusion navigation in autonomous unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) to address limitations in existing navigation datasets.

title: Drive As You Like: Multi-Head Diffusion with Reinforcement Learning for Personalized Driving
summary: Proposes a multi-head diffusion model with reinforcement learning for personalized autonomous driving, aiming to address the limitations of imitation learning in capturing behavioral diversity and user intent.

title: Vision-Language-Policy Model for Dynamic Robot Task Planning
summary: Discusses a vision-language-policy model designed to bridge the gap between natural language commands and autonomous execution for dynamic robot task planning in unstructured environments.

title: TOPReward: Token Probabilities as Hidden Zero-Shot Rewards for Robotics
summary: Introduces TOPReward, a method that uses token probabilities as hidden zero-shot rewards to provide dense, instruction-conditioned feedback for general-purpose robot learning.

title: What Matters for Simulation to Online Reinforcement Learning on Real Robots
summary: Investigates design choices for successful simulation-to-online reinforcement learning on real robots, based on extensive training runs across various robotic platforms.

title: Force-Aware Residual DAgger via Trajectory Editing for Precision Insertion with Impedance Control
summary: Proposes Force-Aware Residual DAgger via Trajectory Editing, a method for improving imitation learning in contact-rich precision insertion tasks using impedance control for robots.

title: VPWEM: Non-Markovian Visuomotor Policy with Working and Episodic Memory
summary: Introduces VPWEM, a non-Markovian visuomotor policy incorporating working and episodic memory to enable robotic control systems to handle tasks requiring long-term memory beyond short-context histories.

title: Is Your Safe Controller Actually Safe? A Critical Review of CBF Tautologies and Hidden Assumptions
summary: This tutorial critically reviews Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and their practical application in ensuring robotic safety, highlighting gaps between mathematical assumptions and real-world construction.

title: Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study
summary: This robustness study compares World Action Models with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robot action planning, investigating which approach generalizes better in real-world scenarios.

title: Enhancing Glass Surface Reconstruction via Depth Prior for Robot Navigation
summary: This paper proposes a training-free framework that leverages depth foundation models to enhance glass surface reconstruction, improving robot navigation by addressing corrupted depth sensor measurements.

title: Q-SpiRL: Quantum Spiking Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Robot Navigation
summary: This paper presents Q-SpiRL, a quantum spiking reinforcement learning framework designed to enable adaptive, obstacle-aware robot navigation with efficient and stable trajectories in dynamic environments.

title: OLIVE: Online Low-Rank Incremental Learning for Efficient Adaptive Exoskeletons
summary: This paper introduces OLIVE (Online Low-Rank Incremental Learning), a method for efficient adaptive control of wearable exoskeleton systems, allowing them to adjust to dynamic environments and user characteristics.

title: DART-VLN: Test-Time Memory Decay and Anti-Loop Regularization for Discrete Vision-Language Navigation
summary: This research addresses inference-time failures in memory-based agents for vision-language navigation, proposing solutions like Test-Time Memory Decay and Anti-Loop Regularization to counter stale historical evidence and inefficient local behaviors.

title: Learning to Navigate Efficiently with Only 0.58M Trainable Parameters
summary: This research explores efficient visual navigation by developing end-to-end policies that require significantly fewer trainable parameters (0.58M) compared to large-scale models, examining how structure can substitute for scale.

title: The Sensation Modulating Network:Haltability as the architectural ground for object-directed phenomenology
summary: This paper proposes the Sensation Modulating Network (SMN), a theoretical model for a cognitive agent where the whole body is organized by opponent dynamics from 'Sensation Modulators' for object-directed phenomenology.

title: 2022 IEEE President K.J. Ray Liu Honored for His Leadership
summary: Unlike many budding engineers, K.J. Ray Liu wasn’t inspired to enter the field by tinkering with electronics or following in the footsteps of a family member. Growing up in Taichung, Taiwan, he answered his government’s call for students to become electrical engineers to help manufacture semiconductors in the 1970s, when the country’s economy was struggling. “Students who were good in math, science, and physics all wanted to be an electrical engineer because that was the top priority of the government,” Liu says. “That’s how I got into engineering. Now Taiwan is a world leader in semiconductors.” K.J. Ray Liu Occupation Retired professor of information technology and a digital signal processing researcher at the University of Maryland in College Park Member grade Fellow Alma maters National Taiwan University; University of Michigan; UCLA But by the time he graduated from university in 1983, semiconductor facilities were still under construction, so there were no jobs available. Instead, he went on to have a successful career as an educator and entrepreneur in the United States. For 31 years, he was a professor of information technology and a digital signal processing researcher at the University of Maryland in College Park until he retired in 2021. Liu was the chairman, CEO, and CTO of Origin Wireless , a startup he founded in Rockville, Md. Origin, which was acquired by ADT in February, pioneers artificial intelligence for wireless sensing and indoor tracking. Liu, an IEEE Fellow, is an active IEEE volunteer who served as the organization’s president in 2022. IEEE honored him with this year’s Haraden Pratt Award for “transformative and impactful leadership.” Liu is credited with increasing the diversity of nominees for IEEE’s Fellow program , which is the highest level of membership. He also led the effort to realign the organization’s regions geographically to ensure more equitable global representation on the IEEE Board of Directors . He received the Pratt honor on 24 April during a ceremony in New York City. The IEEE Foundation sponsored the Board-level award. “More than anything, I share the honor with the volunteers and staff I had the privilege to work alongside,” he says. “Our hard work is fueled by our shared devotion to this professional home we love and care for so much.” Making the switch to signal processing In the 1970s, Taiwan’s policymakers decided to improve the country’s economy by pivoting from making products such as shoes and umbrellas to manufacturing electronics. The industry got its start in 1976 when RCA , a major electronics company at the time, agreed to transfer licensed semiconductor processes to Taiwan’s Industrial Technology Research Institute . ITRI spun off several semiconductor-related companies including the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. TSMC, launched in 1987, is the world’s largest dedicated semiconductor foundry. Liu graduated in 1983 with a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from National Taiwan University , in Taipei. At the time, there were no semiconductor companies to work for, he says. “Nowadays, many of the country’s university graduates go right to TSMC to get a job,” he says. “But back then, there was no real job market. “Most of my classmates—including me—came to the U.S. for graduate studies. Many of us stayed and, over the last three to four decades, contributed to the development of electronic computer communication technology in the U.S.” Liu left Taiwan after a two-year mandatory stint in the Republic of China Armed Forces to attend the University of Michigan , in Ann Arbor, where in 1987 he earned a master’s degree in electrical engineering. “If I can help make IEEE a better professional home for future members, that is something that I can pay back to IEEE.” He went on to earn a Ph.D. in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering in 1990 from the University of California, Los Angeles . His interest in digital signal processing and very-large-scale integration (VLSI) was sparked while at UCLA. Today VLSI powers all modern electronics. “When I was a graduate student, there was no wireless communication. Everybody had a landline,” he explains. VLSI was an important, active research field at the time. “My research interest was digital signal processing,” he says. “One day I saw a book on VLSI signal processing on my professor’s bookshelf. I immediately thought to myself: That is the field I want to pursue. “VLSI is one lane, digital signal processing is the other, and there is a bridge linking the two. I was interested in both areas, so I did my Ph.D. thesis on VLSI signal processing.” After graduating, Liu joined the University of Maryland, where he is credited with establishing its signal processing research program . In addition to teaching, he conducted research on a broad range of signal processing and communication aspects. The topics include bioinformatics, game theory, signal processing algorithms and architectures, and wireless sensing and communications. He has authored more than 10 books and 900 papers, and he holds 250 patents. You can find his research papers in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library . Ambient-sensing trailblazer Liu is considered to be a pioneer in the field of ambient sensing. The technology gathers environmental data and is used in security systems and health-monitoring devices. He came up with the idea, he says, while working on a project in 2009 for the U.S. Navy . He was trying to solve a problem the Navy was having with the wireless communication systems used in its submarines. Because submarines are made of metal, radio waves were unable to penetrate the vessels’ compartments and instead bounced around, creating interference, he says. His solution was to use a relatively unknown concept in physics: time-reversal signal processing . The technique captures waves, such as sound and electromagnetic signals, and sends them back through the same medium in reverse, flipping the signal from last-in to first-out, and re-emits them. “By using time-reversal feed, we could increase the signal-to-noise ratio by four times,” he says. “That improved performance dramatically.” He became fascinated by the physics of time-reversal signal processing, he says, and wondered how he could apply the concept to serve society. After three years of research, he came up with the idea of using wireless sensing applications through ambient radio waves from surrounding Wi-Fi networks. “I learned to turn Wi-Fi networks into sensing networks that decipher our activities,” he says. “We could know everything happening around us—our motions, breathing, heartbeat, even fall detection—without any wearables.” Through the university’s incubator , which encourages faculty to work on projects with an impact on society, he launched Origin in 2013. The company’s Wi-FI and AI sensing technology enables accurate indoor tracking, motion detection, and health monitoring without the need for wearable devices or cameras. Its products, including its remote patient monitoring , received three innovation awards at the 2020 and 2021 Consumer Electronics shows, including one for best innovation. Finding his professional home Liu joined IEEE in 1986 as a graduate student to access its research papers, he says. “If you didn’t join an IEEE society, you didn’t get its journal—which meant that you couldn’t read the most up-to-date research papers,” he says. “So, I joined the IEEE Signal Processing Society . When I attended my first signal processing conference, I knew I had found a professional home. I met many like-minded people, and together, we built a professional home for our members worldwide.” He became an active volunteer, holding top leadership positions including 2012–2013 president of the Signal Processing Society and 2016–2017 director of IEEE Division IX , which covers societies focused on signal processing, data transmission, navigation, and transportation. In 2019 he was vice president of the Technical Activities Board . In 2022 he served as IEEE president and CEO. The three accomplishments during his term he says he is most proud of are increasing the prize money for the IEEE Medal of Honor , overseeing the realignment of IEEE regions , and establishing greater financial transparency. The reason for increasing the prize for IEEE’s highest award—from US $50,000 to $2 million—in 2025, he says, was to underscore the importance of the technologies the IEEE community develops. Those innovations include semiconductors , the Internet , and the GPU . The money for the Medal of Honor now exceeds that of the Nobel Prize , which carries an award of roughly $1 million. “We need the whole world to understand the IEEE community has made the most impact on society in the last century,” Liu says. “Nevertheless, we did not receive the attention and respect we deserved, so we needed to help ourselves. We want the whole world to know what our contributions are.” His next achievement was realigning IEEE’s regions. During the past several years, membership in Region 10 , which covers countries in Asia and the Pacific, has grown from 10 percent of total membership to nearly 40 percent, he says. It is the largest and most populous of IEEE’s geographic areas , but its members were not equitably represented on the Board of Directors. Each region had one representative on the Board. “The region has 40 percent of the members but only makes up 10 percent of the Board,” Liu says. “That didn’t make sense to a lot of us.” The IEEE Board in 2022 approved region realignment. The total number of regions remains at 10, but their organization is changing. Effective 1 January 2028, the six U.S.-based regions will be consolidated into five, and Region 10 will be split into two. IEEE will no longer use the Region 1 designation. The new Region 2 will represent the Northeastern and Eastern U.S. Region 10 will cover North Asia, and the new Region 11 will represent South Asia and the Pacific. Liu also succeeded in leading a movement that persuaded the IEEE Board to invest in a better financial reporting system to have a clearer understanding of the organization’s finances. A more modern system now tracks banking transactions, contracts, expense reports, and other spending. “Now we know exactly where the money comes from and where it is spent,” he says, “so that we can make more informed decisions. “If I can help make IEEE a better professional home for future members, that is something that I can pay back to IEEE,” he adds. “I truly appreciate what IEEE offered me. From student to professor to an established leader, at every stage, it offered me different opportunities to grow. That is why I worked very hard when I was president to make sure everybody realizes it is a professional home for our entire career.”

title: Simple Dutch books versus Sleeping Beauty halfers
summary: The Sleeping Beauty problem is a famous philosophical puzzle. Described by Elga (2000) : Some researchers are going to put you to sleep. During the two days that your sleep will last, they will briefly wake you up either once or twice, depending on the toss of a fair coin (Heads: once; Tails: twice). After each waking, they will put you back to sleep with a drug that makes you forget that waking. When you are first awakened, to what degree ought you believe that the outcome of the coin toss is Heads? Stipulate that Beauty ("you") wakes only on Monday if Heads, and on Monday and Tuesday if Tails. The standard answers are 1/3 and 1/2 for the probability of Heads. Among those who answer 1/2, we ask a follow-up question: "When you are awakened and then learn it is Monday, to what degree ought you believe that the outcome of the coin is Heads?". The standard answers are 2/3 and 1/2. Of those who endorsed 1/2 for the original question, those who answer 2/3 to this follow-up question are "single halfers", and those who answer 1/2 to this follow-up question are "double halfers". Generally, people who answer 1/3 to the original question answer 1/2 to the follow-up question, and are called "thirders". In anthropic theory, SSA (self-sampling assumption) generalizes single-halfing, SIA (self-indication assumption) generalizes thirding, and FNC (fully non-indexical conditioning) generalizes double-halfing. (Where relevant, I assume self-sampling over observer moments, in line with Bostrom's "SSSA", to handle cases of amnesia.) To summarize these theories: A SSA agent assigs probabilities as if it is sampled randomly from all observers in the universe who are in its reference class. (Reference class is a parameter SSA needs, but SIA and FNC don't.) A SIA agent first multiplies its prior probabilities over universes by the universe's number of observers, then (as in SSA) conditions on itself being a random sample from observers in a universe sampled according to this modified prior, and that observer having its observation. A FNC agent conditions its prior over universes on "some observer with my observation exists", and otherwise assumes it is randomly sampled from observers in the universe with that observation. One complication: In practice, FNC will agree with thirding in the Sleeping Beauty problem, because Beauty receives random data upon waking up, and the specific random observation sequence is more likely to exist conditional on Tails, because there are more chances for the sequence to happen. FNC endorses double-halfing in a controlled scenario where Beauty is a brain upload and has the exact same information state upon waking up regardless of Heads+Monday, Tails+Monday, or Tails+Tuesday, and regardless of random data that would vary between runs of the scenario. Charitably to double-halfing, I assume this controlled Sleeping Beauty scenario for the purposes of this post. I explore Dutch book arguments against anthropic theories in the context of Sleeping Beauty. A Dutch book against an agent is a sequence of bets they are offered which leads to a sure loss for them, if they bet according to their probabilities, and linear utility in how much money they end up with. My Dutch books satisfy two strict criteria: (a) the bookie must have no information not had by the agent at the time the bet takes place; (b) the agent's probabilities must strictly favor the sure-loss sequence of bets if they assign probabilities according to the theory; theories with ambiguity about probabilities can resist Dutch books. I will focus mainly on CDT, since CDT agents accept or reject bets straightforwardly according to their betting odds. First, I present simple Dutch book arguments against CDT single-halfing and CDT double-halfing. Second, I argue that CDT thirding is resistant to Dutch books. Third, I discuss EDT. Dutch booking CDT single-halfers This Dutch book offers one bet on Sunday, and one on Monday. It doesn't matter if the coin has already been flipped by the time of the bet on Sunday, provided the bookie does not know the result. Beauty only considers the Monday bet after knowing it is Monday. The Sunday bet is as follows: "-$14 if Heads, +$16 if Tails". A CDT single-halfer accepts, because Heads and Tails are equally likely; the expected value is 1/2(-$14 + $16) = $1. The Monday bet is as follows: "+$11 if Heads, -$19 if Tails". A CDT single-halfer accepts, because they assign 2/3 to Heads once they see it is Monday; the expected value is 2/3 * $11 + 1/3 * -$19 = $1. If the coin is Heads, then the overall payoff is -$14 + $11 = -$3. If the coin is Tails, then the overall payoff is $16 - $19 = -$3. This is a sure loss. (For prior work on Dutch books for CDT single-halfers, see Hitchcock 2004 and Draper and Pust 2008 ; see Briggs 2010 on CDT/EDT divergence.) Dutch booking CDT double-halfers This Dutch book offers two bets. Bet A is offered when Beauty has woken up, and otherwise has no posterior information; we imagine the bookie is woken up and administered amnesia drugs just like Beauty. Upon Tails, bet A is offered twice; we label the Monday A-bet as AM, and the Tuesday A-bet as AT. Bet B is offered on Monday after Beauty has accepted or rejected bet AM, and has been told the day (we imagine the bookie learns the day at the same time as Beauty, and only offers bet B if it is Monday). Importantly, no bets are offered prior to Monday. Bet A is as follows: "+$10 if Heads; -$8 if Tails". The CDT double-halfer accepts, because they assign 50% Heads; the expected value is 1/2 * ($10 - $8) = $1. Bet B is as follows: "-$11 if Heads; +$15 if Tails". The CDT double-halfer accepts, because they assign 1/2 to Heads and 1/2 to Tails upon learning it is Monday; the expected value is 1/2 * (-$11 + $15) = $2. If the coin is Heads, the CDT double-halfer accepts bets AM and B; the overall payoff is $10 - $11 = -$1. If the coin is Tails, then CDT double-halfer accepts bets AM, B, and AT; the overall payoff is -$8 + $15 - $8 = -$1. This is a sure loss. (Hitchcock's 2004 Dutch book also applies to double-halfers, but requires a bet to happen before any awakening, unlike this section's Dutch book. "Anthropics: Full Non-indexical Conditioning (FNC) is inconsistent" (Armstrong 2019) notes diachronic inconsistency of FNC, which this Dutch book exploits.) CDT thirders resist Dutch books To make a positive case for thirding, we examine ex ante optimality arguments for CDT+SIA (which generalizes betting according to thirding odds). A policy is ex ante optimal when it is expected to attain maximal expected utility if adopted ahead of time. "Can rational choice guide us to correct de se beliefs?" (Conitzer 2015) supports CDT+SIA ex ante optimality in additive games. Additive games do not require Beauty to "worry about coordinating her actions with her selves from other awakenings", and include ordinary imperfect-recall betting scenarios. CDT+SIA is ex ante optimal for additive games: "when we restrict our attention to additive games, then a thirder will necessarily maximize her ex ante expected payout, but a halfer in some cases will not (assuming causal decision theory)". In the other direction, all ex ante optimal policies are compatible with CDT+SIA in a wide class of imperfect-recall scenarios, a superset of additive games. See my "In memoryless Cartesian environments, every UDT policy is a CDT+SIA policy" (2016) and prior work ( "On the Interpretation of Decision Problems with Imperfect Recall" , Piccione and Rubinstein, 1997, Proposition 3: "If a behavioral strategy is optimal then it is modified multiself consistent"). Together, these considerations show that CDT+SIA policies are exactly ex ante optimal policies in additive games. Therefore, there are no Dutch books against CDT+SIA in additive games, and even in non-additive games (of the class studied in Piccione 1997), there are ex ante optimal (therefore non-Dutch-bookable) policies compatible with CDT+SIA. "A Dutch Book for CDT thirders" (Korzukhin 2020) presents a non-additive game where CDT+SIA can lose; the scenario does not meet my strict condition (b). Quoting the paper: "if we allow Sleeping Beauty to deliberate dynamically, she will end up in one of two possible stable states: she may converge on rejecting, or she may converge on accepting." Indeed, not every CDT+SIA policy is ex ante optimal in non-additive games. Still, this failure mode pales in comparison to those of CDT+SSA and CDT+FNC, which compel ex ante suboptimal policies even in additive games (such as the situations of the above Dutch books). EDT and Dutch books The Dutch book against CDT single-halfers also works against EDT single-halfers, because the Monday bet is only considered once Beauty is certain that it is Monday. Similar considerations have been noted in the literature; "the reasoning utilized by the evidential decision theorist to evade Hitchcock's [diachronic Dutch book] cannot be employed here" ( Draper and Pust 2008 ). A draft paper ( "Can de se choice be ex ante reasonable in games of imperfect recall? A complete analysis" , Oesterheld and Conitzer, 2024) claims CDT+SSA, EDT+SSA, EDT+SIA, CDT+FNC are all Dutch bookable, but that EDT+FNC is ex ante optimal (and accordingly resistant to Dutch books). This post supports Dutch books for CDT+SSA, CDT+FNC, and EDT+SSA, though I have not checked all claims in the draft paper. I will briefly examine EDT+FNC on this post's Dutch book for double-halfers. An EDT+FNC agent will, when offered bet A, use FNC to assign probability 50% to Heads, and 50% to Tails, with "Tails and Monday" equally probable with "Tails and Tuesday" (both 25%). To simplify, we first suppose bet B is not offered. The agent believes its general policy of whether to accept bet A is uncorrelated with Heads/Tails. Using EDT, the agent estimates that, conditional on accepting bet A as a general policy, the expected payoff is 1/2 * $10 + 1/2 * (-$8 + -$8) = -$3, whereas the expected payoff is $0 conditional on rejecting bet A as a general policy. And the agent's action is good evidence about its general policy for what it does in this very information state. So the agent rejects bet A, and adding bet B into the mix does not change this. The main upshot is that EDT's betting behavior differs from naively betting according to posterior anthropic probabilities, unlike CDT, which matches naive betting behavior. As such, traditional Dutch book analysis must be modified when considering EDT agents. EDT+FNC avoids this post's Dutch book against double-halfers, but only by agreeing with CDT+SIA about which bets to accept. Intuitively, an EDT+FNC agent acts as if it considers the consequences of its information state's action, rather than its body's action. Upon being offered bet A, an EDT+FNC agent can reason that its information state would exist either way the coin went (so its existence tells it nothing about the coin), but that its information state has one embodied occurrence if Heads and two embodied occurrences if Tails; the reason to reject bet A is that the bet's consequences are doubled in the Tails case due to two embodied occurrences each accepting an episode of bet A. "A Dutch book against sleeping beauties who are evidential decision theorists" (Conitzer 2015) argues that EDT is subject to Dutch books in Sleeping Beauty variants due to correlations between actions taken in different information states. Oesterheld and Conitzer (2024) address this by specifying that in their version of EDT, "For all other , we imagine that choosing upon gives no evidence about choice in ". As such, optimality for EDT+FNC requires independence assumptions about the agent's distribution over its policy. Conclusion Decision-theoretic considerations support betting according to CDT+SIA, and against betting according to CDT+SSA and CDT+FNC. How much does this support thirding in Sleeping Beauty, at a philosophical level? First, philosophical problems with SSA (and therefore single-halfing) are well-known; see Bostrom's Paradoxes of the Self-Sampling Assumption . CDT+SSA and EDT+SSA are easily Dutch booked. An important general problem for combining SSA with decision theory is that adding "dummies" (copies of the agent, who receive an observation informing them they are a dummy, and whose actions don't matter) to a situation changes SSA's posterior probabilities (given non-dummy observations), and by default this change causes decision-theoretic problems, since dummy counts do not affect ex ante strategy optimality. Second, while CDT+FNC is easily Dutch booked, EDT+FNC is a serious contender, by the analysis of Oesterheld and Conitzer (2024), though this analysis relies on independence assumptions. Of course, FNC 'thirds' in realistic Sleeping Beauty scenarios (due to random observations), but double-halves in controlled brain upload versions. FNC is non-Bayesian, which is why this post's Dutch book against CDT double-halfers succeeds, even without needing any pre-experimental bets: the update between bet AM and bet B (from learning it is Monday) is non-Bayesian. Standard Dutch book arguments for Bayesian updating would apply under CDT, but EDT agents bet at odds not matching their subjective probabilities. I prefer CDT+SIA to EDT+FNC since it is more theoretically elegant, has more concordance with standard theories of probability such as Bayesianism, and has ex ante optimality results (especially for additive games) that do not depend on strong independence assumptions. Still, EDT+FNC appears to be the strongest alternative anthropic decision theory at the moment, and I don't have a decisive argument against it. Discuss

summary: This paper explores scaling native multimodal pre-training from scratch to overcome the limitations of text-only large language models. The approach aims to develop models with enhanced perception of the physical world through multimodal inputs.

title: Benchmarking Fine-tuning and Retrieval Strategies for a Multimodal Language Model on the NRC Reactor Operator Licensing Examination
summary: This study benchmarks the Gemma 4 31B-IT multimodal language model on the NRC Reactor Operator Licensing Examination to evaluate its capacity for nuclear domain-specific knowledge. It assesses various fine-tuning and retrieval strategies.

title: MEUSLI: a Multilingual Projector for LLM-based ASR and Beyond
summary: This paper introduces MEUSLI, a multilingual projector designed to connect pre-trained speech encoders with large language models for tasks like ASR and spoken question answering. It aims to support more languages than existing systems.

title: Dynamic Commonsense Coordination for Empathetic Response Generation
summary: This research proposes dynamic commonsense coordination to enhance empathetic response generation in large language models. The method aims to improve models' ability to recognize user emotions and generate more appropriate empathetic responses.

title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a multilayer taxonomy for large language models to structure capabilities for evaluation, aiming to improve cross-study comparison and identify gaps in assessment.

title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
summary: This study investigates why large language models' evaluations of creativity sometimes converge with and sometimes diverge from human judgments, using six widely used LLMs across three studies.

title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging
summary: This research presents a method using cross-lingual transfer and LoRA adapter merging to improve biomedical machine translation for low-resource Arabic-script languages, leveraging Arabic and Persian as pivot languages.

title: A Factorial Study of Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Machine Translation using Grammar Books
summary: This study introduces a pipeline that uses large language models to extract information from grammar books to generate synthetic parallel data, aiming to enable machine translation for endangered languages.

title: grapheme-kit: Grapheme-Level Metrics and Text Processing for Multilingual NLP
summary: This paper introduces `grapheme-kit`, an open-source Python library that extends lexical metrics and text processing to the grapheme level, improving accuracy for multilingual Natural Language Processing.

title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
summary: This research proposes "Skill Self-Play," a new method for LLM training that aims to overcome the dilemma between task diversity and verification reliability in interaction-driven self-evolution.

title: From Obligation to Specification: A Survey on Validating EU AI Act Requirements in RE
summary: This survey examines how Requirements Engineering can translate obligations from the EU AI Act into testable and verifiable requirements for organizations developing AI systems.

title: The Hard Decision Layer: Evidence for Committed Inference in Transformers
summary: This research investigates how transformer-based language models commit to predictions during inference in multiple-choice question answering, identifying a "Hard Decision Layer" where answer rankings stabilize.

title: Do VLMs Read or Rewrite? On Transcription Faithfulness in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research demonstrates that Vision-Language Models often "rewrite" imperfect text into more plausible forms rather than faithfully transcribing it, impacting their reliability for document understanding.

title: Progress Reward Modeling for Robotic Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: This comprehensive survey reviews progress reward modeling, a technique that provides intermediate feedback to enhance robotic learning in dynamic environments with large behavior spaces.

title: From Seasonality to Semantics: Benchmarking a Hybrid Probabilistic Forecasting System for Roadblocks in Bolivia
summary: This article benchmarks a hybrid probabilistic forecasting system designed to anticipate roadblocks in Bolivia, a social conflict phenomenon with significant economic impacts.

title: Adversarial Prompts for Acceptance Collapse in Speculative Decoding
summary: This research investigates how adversarial prompts can cause "acceptance collapse" in speculative decoding, a lossless inference acceleration scheme, by exploiting a dynamic token-level alignment vulnerability.

title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
summary: This research explores using level-appropriate embodied conversational agents powered by LLMs to help reduce foreign language anxiety in second language acquisition.

title: Diffusion Models in Medical Image Inpainting: Challenges, Solution Taxonomy, and Future Directions
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive survey on the use of diffusion models for medical image inpainting, outlining current challenges, proposing a solution taxonomy, and discussing future research directions.

title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces MissionBench, a new benchmark for zero-shot, mission-level evaluation of aerial multimodal large language model agents performing long-horizon embodied tasks.

title: Small Vision-Language Models Know When They Are Wrong But Cannot Say So: A Two-Model Study of Stated versus Internal Confidence Under Realistic Image Degradation
summary: This study reveals that small Vision-Language Models often possess reliable internal uncertainty signals when processing degraded images but struggle to explicitly communicate this uncertainty.

title: Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Mode
summary: This paper introduces Nanbeige4.2-3B, a compact 3-billion-parameter model designed with strong agentic capabilities for code, office, and complex tool-use tasks, alongside competitive reasoning abilities.

title: DBA-Bench: A Production-Fidelity Benchmark for LLM-Based Database Operations Agents
summary: This paper introduces DBA-Bench, a new production-fidelity benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based database operations agents, focusing on live-environment interaction and complex observation spaces.

title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
summary: This research investigates how commercial large language models' deployment configurations influence their validation of contested scientific claims and ethnonationalist pseudo-science, highlighting issues of epistemic mediation.

title: When Ethics and Payoffs Diverge: LLM Agents in Morally Charged Social Dilemmas
summary: This paper examines the ethical alignment of large language model agents when facing morally charged social dilemmas, exploring the divergence between their moral judgment and strategic behavior.

title: Interpretable Depression Detection from Social Media Text Using LLM-Derived Embeddings
summary: This research investigates using large language model (LLM) embeddings and traditional machine learning classifiers to accurately and interpretably detect depressive language in social media text for early mental health identification.

title: Learning to Reason for Factuality
summary: This paper explores methods, including online Reinforcement Learning, to improve the factuality and reduce hallucinations in Reasoning Large Language Models (R-LLMs), which often struggle with factual accuracy despite advanced reasoning.

title: MedKGent: A Large Language Model Agent Framework for Constructing Temporally Evolving Medical Knowledge Graph
summary: MedKGent is a Large Language Model agent framework designed to construct and manage temporally evolving medical knowledge graphs, addressing challenges in structuring rapidly expanding medical literature.

title: Maximizing Local Entropy Where It Matters: Prefix-Aware Localized LLM Unlearning
summary: This research proposes prefix-aware localized LLM unlearning to selectively forget sensitive knowledge from large language models while preserving general utility, addressing the limitations of existing global unlearning approaches.

title: What Matters When Building Universal Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Models?
summary: This paper investigates critical design decisions for building universal multilingual Named Entity Recognition (NER) models, analyzing the impact of transformer models, architectures, loss functions, and training datasets.

title: SwiftMem: Fast Agentic Memory via Query-aware Indexing
summary: SwiftMem introduces a fast agentic memory system for LLM agents that uses query-aware indexing to efficiently retrieve relevant information, improving upon existing query-agnostic retrieval methods.

title: Language-Aware Distillation for Multilingual Instruction-Following Speech LLMs with ASR-Only Supervision
summary: This research proposes a language-aware distillation method to train multilingual instruction-following Speech LLMs using only ASR supervision, making them useful for real-world interaction without requiring large, task-specific speech corpora.

title: LMEB: Long-horizon Memory Embedding Benchmark
summary: LMEB is a new benchmark designed to evaluate long-horizon memory embeddings for memory-augmented systems like OpenClaw, addressing the gap in current text embedding benchmarks that do not assess models' ability to handle complex memory retrieval.

title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
summary: WHBench is a targeted evaluation benchmark designed to assess the clinical capabilities of frontier Large Language Models in women's health topics, using 47 expert-crafted scenarios.

title: Can AI Debias the News? LLM Interventions Improve Cross-Partisan Receptivity but LLMs Overestimate Their Own Effectiveness
summary: This study investigates whether LLM-generated interventions can debias news headlines to improve cross-partisan receptivity, finding that while LLMs can help, they tend to overestimate their effectiveness.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: SURE-RAG proposes a method for sufficiency and uncertainty-aware evidence verification in selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), aiming to ensure that retrieved passages not only are relevant but also sufficiently justify the answer.

title: Oxygen-TryOn: Fashion-Native Foundation Model for Any-item Virtual Try-On
summary: Oxygen-TryOn is presented as a unified, fashion-native foundation model specifically designed for any-item virtual try-on, leveraging a dedicated data engine and try-on-specific training.

title: Be Consistent! Enhancing Robust Visual Reasoning in LVLMs with Consistency Constraints
summary: This research aims to enhance robust visual reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by introducing consistency constraints, addressing their vulnerabilities in complex visual reasoning tasks.

title: Risk-Routed Implicit Boundary Refinement for Robust Ultrasound Image Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes a risk-routed implicit boundary refinement method to improve robust ultrasound image segmentation, addressing challenges like speckle noise and low-contrast boundaries in medical imaging.

title: Toward High-Fidelity 3D Point-Cloud Learning for Brain Folding Morphology Prediction Using Trans-Unet
summary: This article introduces Trans-Unet, a novel framework for high-fidelity 3D point-cloud learning aimed at predicting brain folding morphology, addressing challenges in fine-grained surface reconstruction and computational cost.

title: Closing the Loop: Training-Free Revisit Consistency for Autoregressive Generative Rendering
summary: This paper presents a training-free revisit consistency method for autoregressive generative rendering, enhancing conditional video generation models to produce more consistent photorealistic videos from 3D engine renderings over long horizons.

title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes
summary: This research introduces SCALE, a self-supervised constraint-aware layout generation method for fixing design-rule violations in semiconductor manufacturing at advanced nodes, leveraging Large Language Models.

title: Farmland Extent and Visible Boundary Mapping from 1 m NAIP Imagery Using Residual U-Net and Text-Prompted SAM 3 Refinement
summary: This study presents a reproducible workflow for mapping farmland extent and visible boundaries from 1m NAIP imagery, using Residual U-Net and text-prompted SAM 3 for refinement.

title: Learning Adaptive Semantic Gaussian Allocation for 3D Occupancy
summary: This paper introduces a method for learning adaptive semantic Gaussian allocation for 3D occupancy, which provides a compact representation for 3D semantic occupancy prediction by rendering semantic primitives into a voxel volume.

title: ISPCloak: Weaponizing ISP for Optimization-Free Physical Camouflage against Deepfake Detectors
summary: This research introduces ISPCloak, a method that weaponizes Image Signal Processors (ISP) for optimization-free physical camouflage to create adversarial examples against deepfake detectors, exposing a blind spot in current forensic paradigms.

title: Low-Altitude Channel Multipath Prediction via Panoramic Perception and Vision-Language Model
summary: This paper presents a method for low-altitude channel multipath prediction in 6G mobile networks using panoramic perception and vision-language models, improving accuracy over traditional statistical models.

title: TextSLIP: Text Self-Supervised CLIP for Medical Report Generation
summary: This research introduces TextSLIP, a self-supervised CLIP-style model designed to enhance medical vision-language modeling for automated medical report generation by providing more fine-grained semantic understanding.

title: Rethinking Layer-Wise Information Allocation for Vision Foundation Model Adaptation
summary: This study re-evaluates layer-wise information allocation for adapting vision foundation models, focusing on parameter-efficient methods like Visual Prompt Tuning to improve downstream visual recognition.

title: Medical-Checklist: Assessing the Comprehension of Medical Images by Multimodal Models
summary: This paper introduces Medical-Checklist, a new benchmark specifically designed to assess the comprehension of medical images by multimodal AI models in vision-language tasks.

title: Visual Saliency Steering Distillation for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: This research proposes Visual Saliency Steering Distillation as a technique to improve multimodal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, especially in smaller models with limited token budgets.

title: EVL-MCoT: Enhanced Vision-Language Multi-CoT for Harmful Meme Detection
summary: This paper introduces EVL-MCoT, an Enhanced Vision-Language Multi-CoT model, specifically developed for the task of detecting harmful memes by jointly interpreting text and vision.

title: A Smooth Phase-Separation Model for Weak-Boundary Segmentation of Homogeneous Structures
summary: This work presents a smooth phase-separation model for weak-boundary segmentation, addressing challenges in image analysis where adjacent structures have similar intensity distributions.

title: Rethinking Multi-Branch and Cross-Backbone Fusion for Vehicle Re-Identification in the Foundation-Model Era
summary: This empirical study re-examines the effectiveness of multi-branch architectures and CNN-Transformer fusion for vehicle re-identification in the era of foundation models, evaluating their complementary representations.

title: ReCowGnition: A Realistic Biometric Benchmark for Cow Face Recognition
summary: This paper introduces ReCowGnition, a new realistic biometric benchmark for cow face recognition, aiming to advance precision livestock farming through computer vision.

title: Alleviating Regional Shortcuts for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
summary: This research addresses the problem of regional shortcuts in Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL), proposing methods to prevent misclassification of novel-class samples into base classes.

title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
summary: This paper introduces CommandLM, a multimodal large language model designed to generate interpretable, human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles in autonomous driving systems.

title: FAIR: Feature-Augmented Implicit Regularization for AI-generated Fake Image Detection
summary: This paper proposes FAIR (Feature-Augmented Implicit Regularization) to improve the generalization and robustness of AI-generated fake image detection, which currently struggles with unseen domains.

title: Spectral Prior for Reducing Exposure Bias in Diffusion Models
summary: This research proposes a Spectral Prior method to reduce exposure bias in diffusion models, identifying and addressing systematic frequency-dependent discrepancies during iterative sampling.

title: InnoText: A Unified Model for Visual Text Generation and Editing
summary: This paper introduces InnoText, a unified model for visual text generation and editing that leverages diffusion models to achieve high-fidelity synthesis with precise structural regularity and legibility.

title: Projection Pursuit CPCANet for Domain Generalization
summary: This paper introduces Projection Pursuit CPCANet, a new method for Domain Generalization that aims to improve robust representation learning by addressing rank-deficient covariance estimation in existing geometric alignment methods.

title: A Framework for Individual Tree Growth Reconstruction Using Multi-Platform Laser Scanning
summary: This paper outlines a framework for reconstructing individual tree growth using multi-platform laser scanning data, crucial for accurate tree-level forest monitoring and estimating attribute changes in boreal forests.

title: CARDIAG: A Dense Segment Classification Benchmark of Deep Learning Architectures for Coronary Angiography
summary: This work introduces CARDIAG, a dense segment classification benchmark for evaluating deep learning architectures in coronary angiography, aiming to standardize assessment protocols for cardiovascular disease analysis.

title: Visual Relocalization from Sparse Views in Aliased and Low-Texture Environments via Novel View Synthesis
summary: This research presents a method for visual relocalization from sparse views in challenging environments like planetary terrains, utilizing novel view synthesis to overcome low texture and aliasing.

title: dRAE: Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes
summary: This work introduces dRAE, a Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes, designed to discretize high-dimensional visual representations to bridge the gap with language models effectively.

title: JustDepth: Real-Time Radar-Camera Depth Estimation with Single-Scan LiDAR Supervision
summary: This paper introduces JustDepth, a real-time method for radar-camera depth estimation that uses single-scan LiDAR supervision, providing accurate and low-latency depth for autonomous systems.

title: Bowel Obstruction Detection and Localization on Abdominal CT with Deep Learning
summary: This research proposes a deep learning method for automated detection and localization of bowel obstruction on abdominal CT scans to support radiologists.

title: LayoutLite: Token-Level Implicit Layout Analysis for Efficient Document OCR
summary: This paper introduces LayoutLite, a method for token-level implicit layout analysis to enhance the efficiency of end-to-end OCR systems based on vision-language models.

title: Filling Before Advancing: Capability-Gap-Driven Post-Training for Scenario-Specialized Remote Sensing MLLMs
summary: This research proposes a post-training method to enhance remote sensing multimodal large language models (RS-MLLMs) for scenario-specialized Earth observation applications by addressing capability gaps.

title: TRaM-VSR: Importance-Aware Token Routing and Merging for One-Step Diffusion Video Super-Resolution
summary: This paper introduces TRaM-VSR, an importance-aware token routing and merging technique, to improve the computational efficiency of Diffusion Transformer-based video super-resolution models.

title: AgentHOI: Multi-Agent Reasoning for Human-Object-Interaction Video Generation via Implicit Representation Alignment
summary: This research proposes AgentHOI, a multi-agent reasoning framework with implicit representation alignment for generating human-object interaction videos with fine-grained control.

title: RadSight: Towards Perceptually Reliable Multimodal Radiology Image Understanding
summary: This paper introduces RadSight, a method to analyze and improve the perceptual reliability of medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in understanding radiology images.

title: fMRI2Face: A Full-HD fMRI-Video Dataset and Geometry-Guided Neural Decoding Framework for Dynamic Human Face Reconstruction
summary: This research introduces fMRI2Face, a full-HD fMRI-video dataset and a geometry-guided neural decoding framework for reconstructing dynamic human faces from brain activity.

title: Geometric 2D Scene Graph Generation
summary: This research presents a method for Geometric 2D Scene Graph Generation, which helps in understanding how components fit together for tasks like assembly instructions in production and robotics.

title: SLIP: Segmentation with Low-latency Interactive Prompting for 3D Medical Images
summary: This paper introduces SLIP, a method for low-latency interactive segmentation of 3D medical images, enabling efficient annotation through user prompts.

title: Time-Reversed Imaging: A Multimodal Benchmark and Framework for Reconstructing Past Human-Environment Interactions
summary: This research introduces time-reversed imaging, a novel paradigm and multimodal benchmark for reconstructing past human-environment interactions from residual physical imprints.

title: SiPhy: Single-Image Physical Property Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SiPhy, a unified framework for inferring physical properties like mass and stiffness from a single image, which is vital for simulation and embodied AI.

title: Active few-shot segmentation by reinforcing data selection
summary: This research proposes a method for active few-shot segmentation in medical images by reinforcing data selection to improve adaptation performance.

title: Correlation-Aware and Gaussianity-Preserving Robust Latent Angular Watermarking for Diffusion Models
summary: This paper presents a robust latent angular watermarking method for diffusion models that is correlation-aware and Gaussianity-preserving, making it resilient to perturbations.

title: Deformable Triangle Splatting: Flexible Primitives for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
summary: This research introduces Deformable Triangle Splatting, a method utilizing flexible primitives for real-time radiance field rendering to efficiently represent curved and concave structures.

title: Optimal Transport Image Representation and Deep Covariance Alignment (CORAL) for Control Valve Stiction Detection
summary: This research proposes a data-driven method using optimal transport image representation and Deep Covariance Alignment (CORAL) for detecting control valve stiction in industrial processes.

title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
summary: This paper explores learning unified representations for multimodal models using focal loss, aiming for a shared visual token space for both understanding and image generation.

title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
summary: This research introduces SM4RT, a method for learning structured motion geometry to advance 4D dynamic reconstruction from monocular input, moving beyond traditional 3D methods.

title: Pixels for Programs? A Cross-Provider Case Study of Input-Token Accounting for Source Code as Text and Images
summary: This study investigates how commercial APIs account for input tokens when source code is processed as both text and images for vision-language models, analyzing efficiency and cost implications.

title: A Dual Path Framework with Hotspot Guided Fusion for Three Dimensional CT to PET Synthesis in Head and Neck Cancer
summary: This research proposes a dual-path framework with hotspot-guided fusion for synthesizing three-dimensional PET images from CT scans in head and neck cancer, aiding diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Learning Diverse Humanoid Tasks via Synthetic Video Scenarios without Real World Data
summary: This research demonstrates learning diverse tasks for humanoid robots using synthetic video scenarios, reducing the need for real-world data collection for skill acquisition.

title: GRACE: Gradient-Free Robot Action Generation via Combined Diffusion-MPPI Posterior Mean Estimation
summary: This paper introduces GRACE, a method using diffusion policies for gradient-free generation of multimodal robot action sequences, addressing practical safety constraints.

title: Ordered Action Tokens for Visuomotor Policy Learning
summary: This research explores ordered action tokenization for visuomotor policy learning in robots, addressing challenges in discretizing continuous robot actions into tokens for modern policies.

title: Addressing the Orchestration Gap in Generalist Robots via Physical Agency
summary: This paper proposes addressing the orchestration gap in generalist robots by enabling them to reason about and combine perception, planning, and control, moving beyond single learned policies.

title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
summary: StARS is a recommender system-driven approach to generate socially appropriate robot actions in human-robot interaction by modeling inter-subject variability in human preferences.

title: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Probe Guidance in Robotic Ultrasound
summary: This paper presents an action-conditioned world model framework for goal plane probe guidance in robotic ultrasound, aiming to reduce the need for extensive training data in autonomous ultrasound tasks.

title: Adaptive Undulatory Locomotion of Snake-like Robots in Dynamic Viscous Environments via Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research demonstrates how deep reinforcement learning enables adaptive undulatory locomotion for snake-like robots in dynamic viscous environments, overcoming limitations of classical control methods.

title: Mag4D-SLAM Dataset: A Repeated-Traversal Multi-Modal 4D Geomagnetic Dataset for Localization and Mapping
summary: The Mag4D-SLAM Dataset is a multi-modal 4D geomagnetic dataset designed for systematic study of localization and mapping in outdoor robotics, providing infrastructure-free orientation robust to GNSS denial.

title: DB-VIO: Dual-Branch Visual Inertial Odometry with Enhanced Visual-Inertial Representation
summary: DB-VIO introduces a dual-branch visual inertial odometry method with enhanced visual-inertial representation for more accurate 6-DoF motion estimation in mobile robotic systems.

title: Flight-Ready LiDAR-Inertial Odometry for Embedded Drone Platforms
summary: This paper presents a flight-ready LiDAR-inertial odometry system optimized for real-time closed-loop aerial control on embedded drone platforms, addressing the needs of UAV deployment.

title: Safe Learning Predictive Control for Ego-World Robotic Systems
summary: SOWL-MPC proposes a safe learning predictive control strategy for autonomous navigation in shared environments, enabling robotic systems to anticipate and react to surrounding robots' behaviors.

title: Offline Vision-Language Navigation with Geometric Goal Localization for Outdoor Environments
summary: This research explores offline vision-language navigation for autonomous robots in outdoor environments, enabling them to interpret natural-language instructions and localize geometric goals without cloud reliance.

title: Design and Human Evaluation of Tactile Withdrawal Reflexes for a Skin-Covered Robot Arm
summary: This paper investigates artificial nociception for a robot arm with whole-body tactile sensing, designing and evaluating tactile withdrawal reflexes in response to harmful stimulation.

title: A Monolithic Hand with Asymmetric Origami Bending and Dual-chamber Actuators
summary: This research presents a monolithic soft robotic hand featuring asymmetric origami bending and dual-chamber actuators, designed to achieve both compliant interaction and high output performance.

title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
summary: Teachy Mini is a knowledge-based generative social robot developed for personalized tutoring in higher education, powered by large language models, with preliminary evaluation regarding its capabilities.

title: Conformal Constraint Tightening for Chance-Constrained Motion Planning with Unknown Dynamics
summary: This paper introduces conformal constraint tightening for chance-constrained motion planning, an algorithm designed to compute safe control sequences for autonomous robots navigating with unknown dynamics.

title: Robot Learning to Communicate through Projected Visual Abstractions
summary: This research explores how robots can learn to communicate through projected visual abstractions like shadows and silhouettes, expanding their expressive capabilities beyond physical morphology.

title: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
summary: ViTacWorld introduces scaled visuo-tactile world models to improve contact-rich robot manipulation by integrating both visual and tactile sensing data for robust control.

title: Robot-Factored World Models via Robot Rendering
summary: This paper presents robot-factored world models that use robot rendering to predict future observations from robot actions, distinguishing between robot motion and scene response.

title: Constraint-Driven Synthesis of Hyper Petri Nets
summary: This paper addresses the modeling and synthesis of constrained robotic system behaviors using Hyper Petri Nets, focusing on constructing models where system states satisfy given logical constraints.

title: OpenNavMap: Multi-Session Appearance-Based Topometric Mapping for Scalable Visual Navigation
summary: OpenNavMap proposes a multi-session appearance-based topometric mapping method for scalable visual navigation, enabling long-term robot deployment in real-world environments with efficient map maintenance.

title: Adaptive Learned State Estimation based on KalmanNet
summary: This paper introduces Adaptive Multi-modal KalmanNet (AM-KNet), a hybrid state estimator combining Kalman filtering with learned components for improved performance on real-world automotive data.

title: Compliant Non-Prehensile Pushing Manipulation
summary: This research addresses compliant non-prehensile pushing operations with robotic manipulation systems, focusing on ensuring safe interactions in human environments.

title: Stop to Decide: Latency-Aware Proprioceptive Navigation Primitives for Mapping-Free Quadruped Inspection
summary: This study proposes a 'stop-to-decide' cadence for quadruped inspection systems to manage latency in proprioceptive navigation, especially for stair-summit detection.

title: Industrial Dexterity Benchmark: A Hardware-Software Benchmarking Platform for Industrial Dexterous Manipulation
summary: This work presents an 'Industrial Dexterity Benchmark', a hardware-software platform designed to measure and compare dexterous manipulation capabilities in industrial robotics.

title: CorVS+: Correspondence-Driven Association of Video Trajectories and Sensors for Identity-Aware Person Localization in Warehouses
summary: This paper introduces CorVS+, a method for correspondence-driven association of video trajectories and sensors, enabling identity-aware person localization in logistics warehouses to improve productivity.

title: The 3D Mirage: Probing and Taming 3D Hallucinations
summary: This paper examines 'The 3D Mirage', a vulnerability in monocular depth foundation models where they hallucinate illusory 3D structures from ambiguous inputs, and proposes methods to understand and mitigate this issue.

title: Benchmarking the Safety of Large Language Models for Robotic Health Attendant Control
summary: This work introduces a new benchmark and dataset to evaluate the safety of large language models when used as control components for robotic health attendants.

title: SAFE-Pruner: Semantic Attention-Guided Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces SAFE-Pruner, a method for semantic attention-guided future-aware token pruning, designed to achieve efficient real-time inference for vision-language-action models in robotic control.

title: NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation

title: Off-grid data centers aren't the panacea that some AI firms hoped
summary: Local backlash and reliability concerns are challenging the vision of an AI boom built quickly using large off-grid data centers. Why it matters: If giant projects stumble, trillions of dollars in AI investment and the industry's plans to rapidly expand data centers could be at risk. The big picture: In an effort to speed AI development, some companies are building data centers powered mainly by onsite generation rather than waiting years to connect to the electric grid. There are 59 data centers with a combined capacity of about 90 gigawatts that plan to build their own power "behind-the-meter" using sources like gas turbines, generators and fuel cells, according to a report from research firm Cleanview. A smaller subset is trying to run large campuses mostly on behind-the-meter power as a way to move more quickly than the local utility and the grid can. Infrastructure risk analysis firm Occam Edge tracks 12 projects where on-site power is the primary serving supply, representing about 10.6 GW of announced capacity. State of play: Recent hiccups are highlighting the challenges that come with bypassing the grid. Earlier this month, New Mexico's top land official rejected a gas pipeline meant to supply on-site fuel cells for Oracle's 2.5 GW Project Jupiter data center campus, part of Oracle and OpenAI's Stargate initiative. The regulatory setback could contribute to a yearslong delay . A week later, a much smaller off-grid data center in Virginia , saw its on-site gas turbines knocked offline for 24 hours , forcing it to run on dirty backup diesel generators during already bad air quality from the Canadian wildfires. Local residents complained of burning lungs and 60-decibel noise, and a local government official called for new laws to regulate generators. Catch up quick: Chief developers of this off-grid approach include OpenAI, and its partners Oracle and Crusoe, which have worked on OpenAI's Stargate campuses. A Stargate project in Abilene, Texas, developed by Crusoe, reportedly went offline for days at a time due to issues with power and cooling equipment. Another off-grid player is Elon Musk, who rattled the energy world when he built xAI's Colossus 1 using mobile gas turbines in just a few months. While it was initially off-grid, it's now grid-connected and selling compute to Anthropic. Despite a lawsuit from the NAACP over Colossus 1, Musk is now using gas turbines to power Colossus 2 (with compute sold to Google), and earlier this month bought a mobile gas turbine company. What they're saying: Critics argue off-grid data centers could prove slower and more costly to deploy, less reliable to run, and more expensive than expanding the electric grid. "This is a flimsy way to deploy AI," says energy investor Jigar Shah, who predicts much of the bullish off-grid deployment figures won't materialize. Power engineers are worried that off-grid data centers won't meet reliability targets, says Occam Edge founder and CEO Christian Okoye, who compares "Dark Gigawatts" to the "Dark Fiber" of the dotcom bust. "It's a time of desperation," says Josh Wong, founder and CEO of ThinkLabs AI, which helps utilities find more capacity on their current grids. "The [off-grid] business model is bolt-on." Follow the money: Investors are lacking insight into the reliability of off-grid data centers, says Okoye. Investors faced with the uncertainties of off-grid data centers could decide not to underwrite them. S&P Global Ratings recently downgraded Oracle's long-term issuer credit rating to BBB- from BBB, just one step above junk status, due to its massive data center spending, which includes investment in on-site power infrastructure. Trillions of dollars are riding on whether large off-grid data centers can work as advertised, justify their added cost and win local support. What's next: More high-profile problems building and running off-grid data centers could lead to a reckoning that the AI boom will be a lot more grid-powered than many AI companies hoped.
