title: Concept-based Visual Counterfactual Explanations with Diffusion Models
summary: This research introduces concept-based visual counterfactual explanations using diffusion models to determine minimal image changes that flip a vision model's prediction, particularly relevant for safety-critical applications.

title: SeT-Diff: Towards Semantic Foundation Models for HPC Telemetry and Time-Series
summary: This research proposes SeT-Diff, a framework for semantic foundation models to create accurate digital twins for HPC telemetry and time-series data in data centers.

title: Same Question, Different Answers: Evaluating LLM Reliability Beyond Accuracy
summary: This work proposes a method for evaluating large language model reliability by assessing how their answers change when presented with meaning-preserving paraphrases of the same question, moving beyond traditional accuracy metrics.

title: DeepLens Diagnosis Agent: Agentic Workflow Design Lets a Small Reasoning Model Compete with Frontier LLMs
summary: This paper introduces DeepLens Diagnosis Agent, an agentic workflow designed for medical diagnosis that enables smaller reasoning models to achieve performance comparable to frontier LLMs. It structures diagnosis into multiple stages: fact extraction, knowledge consultation, differential analysis, and diagnosis selection.

title: MIITA: Memory-Induced Inference-Time Adaptation for Continual Learning with Small Language Models
summary: MIITA proposes a memory-based method for Small Language Models to achieve continual learning without catastrophic forgetting, by decoupling knowledge from parameter updates during inference-time adaptation. This allows SLMs to adapt to evolving real-world needs in resource-constrained environments.

title: Codifying the Judge: Scalable Evaluation via Program Distillation
summary: This paper introduces program distillation as a scalable and efficient alternative to LLM-as-a-judge for automated evaluation, addressing issues of high cost, latency, and opaque decisions. It focuses on improving the scalability and reliability of AI model assessment.

title: SF-AMS: Strategic Forgetting for Structured Memory in LLM Agent
summary: SF-AMS (Strategic Forgetting for Agent Memory Systems) is a framework proposed to manage long-context dependencies in LLM agents by strategically forgetting redundant information. It aims to maintain compact, high-utility memory for multi-step reasoning processes.

title: Synthetic Scenario Generation for Evaluation of Industry 4.0 Agents
summary: This work presents a method for synthetic scenario generation to create realistic evaluation environments for Industry 4.0 agents. It aims to overcome limitations of existing benchmarks by integrating telemetry, failure modes, and domain standards for industrial agent assessment.

title: Loss-Aware Feature-Map Pruning in Convolutional Neural Networks Using Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: This paper introduces a loss-aware feature-map pruning framework for Convolutional Neural Networks, utilizing multi-armed bandits to reduce model storage and inference costs. The method removes redundant feature maps to improve network efficiency.

title: DSTFView: Multi-View Cloud-Edge Workload Forecasting with Dual-Input Spatio-Temporal-Frequency Modeling
summary: DSTFView proposes a dual-input spatio-temporal-frequency modeling approach for multi-view cloud-edge workload forecasting, designed to support latency-sensitive and reliability-critical edge-side AI inference. It aims to balance multidimensional feature modeling and forecasting efficiency.

title: MedLoCoMo: A Long-Context Multi-Session Medical Dialogue Benchmark for Large Language Models
summary: MedLoCoMo is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models' capabilities in patient-specific clinical reasoning over long-context, multi-session medical dialogues. It assesses how LLMs use, connect, and abstain from information across extended medical interactions.

title: Keyword Matters: Unveiling the Energy Sensitivity of On-Device LLM Prompting
summary: This research investigates the energy sensitivity of on-device LLM prompting, revealing how factors like model compression and runtime acceleration affect energy consumption on mobile and embedded devices. It addresses the fundamental constraint of high energy usage in resource-limited hardware.

title: Reference Feature Atlases for Mechanistic Auditing of Language Models
summary: This paper proposes reference feature atlases, a sparse feature library trained once and reused for new models, to enable more efficient and consistent mechanistic auditing of language models. This method simplifies the process of understanding a new LLM's internal features.

title: SCAIR: Schema-Conditioned Agentic Iterative Reasoning for Enterprise Knowledge Graphs
summary: SCAIR (Schema-Conditioned Agentic Iterative Reasoning) is presented as an agentic system designed to improve Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) for enterprise knowledge graphs. It aims to address the challenges of generalizing agentic approaches to dense, real-world enterprise KGs.

title: Schema-Aware Localisation (SAL): Live Schema Grounding and Hallucination Validation for Oracle NL2SQL
summary: Schema-Aware Localisation (SAL) is introduced as a method for live schema grounding and hallucination validation in Oracle NL2SQL applications. It aims to prevent LLMs from generating invalid SQL by ensuring columns and syntax are correct against the database schema.

title: Too much evidence, too little time: From text to actionable recommendations through multi-objective evidence reasoning
summary: This study proposes a multi-objective evidence reasoning system to process vast amounts of scientific literature for evidence-based clinical decision-making. It aims to efficiently identify, evaluate, and synthesize relevant information to generate actionable recommendations for specialists.

title: Temporal Context Reinstatement Drives Episodic-Like Order Memory in Long-Context Language Models
summary: This research investigates how temporal context reinstatement drives episodic-like order memory in long-context language models, offering insights into their ability to retrieve experiences over extended timescales. It explores computational mechanisms underlying memory in LLMs, drawing parallels to human cognition.

title: cMoLLM at Scale: Horizontal Scaling Laws for Mixture-of-LLMs
summary: This paper investigates horizontal scaling laws for Mixture-of-LLMs (cMoLLM) to address the computational bottlenecks associated with dense Transformers. It aims to improve the efficiency and scalability of large language models, particularly as they approach trillion-parameter regimes.

title: HeraSys: Collaborative Serving of Multiple LLM Workflows via Fine-Grained End-to-End Optimization
summary: HeraSys is a system designed for the collaborative serving of multiple LLM workflows, especially high-concurrency, multi-tenant agentic ones, through fine-grained end-to-end optimization. It aims to improve the efficiency and coordination of complex AI task execution.

title: Multi-Objective Structured Pruning of LLMs for Latency and Model Size Optimization
summary: This paper presents a multi-objective structured pruning method for Large Language Models aimed at optimizing latency and model size. It focuses on enabling efficient deployment of LLMs in embedded and edge computing environments with strict resource constraints.

title: Source-Aware Reranking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Reliability Prior Approach
summary: This work proposes source-aware reranking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that incorporates domain-informed source reliability into the retrieval process. It aims to improve the credibility and accuracy of RAG outputs by considering source provenance beyond semantic similarity.

title: The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents: Harness Choice as a Hidden Variable in Coding-Agent Evaluation
summary: This research examines the "scaffold effect" in coding agent evaluation, highlighting how the choice of harness (tools, context management) acts as a hidden variable influencing leaderboard rankings. It suggests that consistent evaluation of coding agents requires explicit specification of the testing environment.

title: MM-ShiftKV: Decode-Aware Prefill-Stage KV Selection for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: MM-ShiftKV introduces a decode-aware prefill-stage KV selection method for Multimodal Large Language Models to optimize Key-Value caching. This technique aims to significantly reduce the memory footprint, which is a major bottleneck for efficient inference with long context lengths and numerous visual tokens.

title: TriSP: Tri-Signal Structured Pruning for Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces TriSP, a structured pruning method for Large Language Models that reduces memory and compute costs by removing entire structures like attention heads and MLP neurons.

title: ParBench: A Benchmark for Reliable Evaluation of LLM Parallel Code Translation
summary: ParBench is a new benchmark designed to reliably evaluate the performance of Large Language Models and autonomous coding agents in translating parallel code for various accelerator ecosystems.

title: Lexical discovery in unknown environments orchestrated by Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes the Neuro-Symbolic Lexical Discovery (NSLD) framework, enabling populations of LLM-based autonomous agents to develop shared vocabularies for entities in unknown environments.

title: Structure Over Scale: Schema-Constrained Causal Graphs for RAG
summary: This paper introduces schema-constrained causal graphs for GraphRAG, aiming to improve the efficiency and relevance of information extraction by focusing on query-relevant knowledge.

title: xMIx: High-Performance Serving-Time Platform for Mechanistic Interpretability Apps
summary: xMIx is a high-performance serving-time platform designed to deploy mechanistic interpretability applications in production, enabling analysis and intervention in AI inference computations for tasks like jailbreak detection.

title: An Agentic Orchestration of Atomistic Simulations
summary: This paper presents an agent-based system embedded within the URSA framework that automates the design and execution of complex, multi-step atomistic simulations for materials design.

title: HyCE-RAG: Hypergraph Chain-of-Evidence Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering
summary: HyCE-RAG is a new method for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that uses hypergraphs and a chain-of-evidence approach to improve multi-hop question answering and provide explainable reasoning.

title: Differencing the Diffusion Trajectory toward Uncertain Components for Time Series Forecasting
summary: This research adapts diffusion models for probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a method to differentiate the diffusion trajectory toward uncertain future components, addressing the asymmetry between past and future data.

title: Chart Deception in Vision-Language Models: From Vulnerability to Mitigation
summary: This paper investigates how deceptive design choices in charts can mislead Vision-Language Models, identifying their vulnerability and proposing mitigation strategies to improve their reliable interpretation of visual data.

title: DeepLook: Deeper Thinking with Lookahead
summary: DeepLook is a method that improves large language model reasoning efficiency by optimizing compute allocation during inference-time scaling through a lookahead mechanism, aiming for deeper thinking.

title: Group Preference Collapse in Personalized Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper identifies "group preference collapse" in personalized multimodal large language models, where models lose sensitivity to individual user preferences despite aiming for user-specific responses.

title: Evaluating LLMs as Interpretable Controllers for Dynamical Systems
summary: This research investigates the potential of Large Language Models to function as interpretable controllers for dynamical physical systems, using a dynamic thermal environment as a test case.

title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations
summary: Tokengeist is a method for multi-turn attribution tracing in agentic conversations, designed to identify which tokens from prior turns shaped a language model's subsequent responses and how dependencies propagated.

title: Decentralized Granular Access Control for Agentic AI Systems in Critical Infrastructure
summary: This paper proposes a decentralized granular access control framework for agentic AI systems, designed to address the fundamental security challenges of deploying autonomous agents in critical infrastructure where traditional RBAC models are insufficient.

title: DynaResize: Runtime GPU Reallocation for Disaggregated LLM Post-Training
summary: DynaResize is a runtime GPU reallocation system that dynamically switches GPUs between rollout and training phases during disaggregated LLM post-training, aiming to prevent pipeline bubbles caused by static partitioning.

title: Opti-Q: A Constraint-Based Optimization Framework for Multi-LLM Question Planning
summary: Opti-Q is a constraint-based optimization framework for multi-LLM question planning that implements a plan-before-execute paradigm to manage cost, latency, and energy in budgeted LLM deployments.

title: CHS-SQL: A Text-to-SQL approach based on Confidence-Guided Heuristic Search Schema Linking process
summary: CHS-SQL is a Text-to-SQL approach that utilizes Small Language Models with a confidence-guided heuristic search schema linking process, achieving performance comparable to larger models while using consumer-grade GPUs.

title: TokenMem: Faithful Knowledge Injection for Frozen LLMs
summary: TokenMem is a lightweight memory mechanism designed for frozen Large Language Models that faithfully injects external knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to prevent knowledge conflicts and unpredictable outputs.

title: Masked Distillation: Internalizing the Chain-of-Thought in Language Models
summary: Masked Distillation is a method to internalize Chain-of-Thought reasoning in Large Reasoning Models, reducing inference-time latency, memory usage, and serving costs by eliminating the need for explicit intermediate traces.

title: VlogReward: Learning Multi-Dimensional Evaluation for Vlog Editing
summary: VlogReward is a system designed to learn multi-dimensional evaluation for vlog editing, addressing the challenge of subjective assessment and lack of standardized criteria in automated video creation.

title: Evolving from Lessons: Skill-Augmented Table Graph Reasoning for Operation-wise Table Question Answering
summary: This paper proposes a skill-augmented table graph reasoning method for operation-wise Table Question Answering to improve LLMs' performance on complex table operations. It addresses how LLMs struggle with operations beyond simple lookups.

title: PRESTO: Prefix-Aligned Tree Drafting for Diffusion Speculative Decoding
summary: The paper introduces PRESTO, a Prefix-Aligned Tree Drafting method to enhance speculative decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs). This technique aims to make dLLMs more effective draft models by generating blocks of tokens in a single pass.

title: CallBench: A Benchmark for Dual-Goal Coordination in Phone Call Assistants
summary: This paper presents CallBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the dual-goal coordination capabilities of phone call assistants. It addresses the challenge of systems needing to manage multiple implicit and explicit goals in interactive conversations.

title: Fast Cross-Scenario Adaptation of CSI Models via Channel Conditional Parameter Generation
summary: This research proposes a method for fast cross-scenario adaptation of Channel State Information (CSI) models in Massive MIMO systems using channel conditional parameter generation. The technique aims to mitigate performance degradation of CSI models in unseen environments.

title: TRACE: Business Rule-Grounded Reasoning Curriculum for Knowledge-Preserving Parametric Tool Retrieval in Enterprise LLMs
summary: TRACE introduces a business rule-grounded reasoning curriculum for enterprise LLMs to improve parametric tool retrieval. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that destroy tool knowledge during training.

title: CRAFT: Learn the Schema, Execute the Plan
summary: CRAFT is a method for enterprise coding agents that streamlines the translation of natural-language requests into executable code over proprietary APIs and schemas. It addresses the overhead caused by injecting exhaustive documentation into prompts for agent execution.

title: Reason Before You Retrieve: Agentic Planning for Multi-modal RAG
summary: This paper introduces Agentic Planning for Multi-modal RAG to improve answering image-text queries by first reasoning about the retrieval target. This approach aims to address challenges arising from direct retrieval over flat evidence spaces.

title: DocHRL: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cost-Optimised Document Classification
summary: DocHRL introduces a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for cost-optimized document classification, aiming to efficiently allocate computational and human resources based on document complexity. It optimizes the sequence of models applied to different document types.

title: Extracting Algorithms in Pre-trained LLMs: A Case on Hidden Markov Models
summary: This research investigates and attempts to extract the underlying algorithms within pre-trained LLMs that enable them to predict observations from Hidden Markov Models via in-context learning. It seeks to understand the mechanisms behind this capability.

title: PTStore (Prefix Tensor Store): Distributed Prefix Caching and Replication for High Throughput Inference Serving
summary: PTStore (Prefix Tensor Store) is a system designed for distributed prefix caching and replication to accelerate high-throughput LLM inference serving. It reduces latency by distributing and replicating reusable KV cache prefixes.

title: STAIF: A Stage-wise Optimization for Complex Instruction Following
summary: STAIF introduces a stage-wise optimization method for large language models to improve their ability to follow complex instructions with multiple explicit constraints. It aims to address the shortcomings of existing alignment methods in satisfying individual constraints.

title: ARdena: Scenario-driven control of real-time LLM agents
summary: ARdena presents a method for scenario-driven control of real-time LLM agents, addressing the challenge of reliably managing their behavior in interactive environments. It offers an alternative to model fine-tuning for adaptive control.

title: KG2Code: Bridging Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models via Executable Code for Question Answering
summary: KG2Code is a research method that bridges knowledge graphs and large language models for question answering by generating executable code. This integration aims to enhance LLM performance on knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: Semalith v1.4: A Calibrated 184M Safety Classifier Achieving State-of-the-Art Prompt-Injection Detection at 44x Fewer Parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B
summary: Semalith v1.4 is a new 184M-parameter safety classifier model designed for detecting prompt injection and ensuring regulatory compliance in LLM deployments. It achieves state-of-the-art prompt-injection detection with significantly fewer parameters than comparable models.

title: CORVUS: Context Optimization and Reduction Via Underlying Synchronization for LLM Coding Agents
summary: CORVUS is a method for context optimization and reduction in LLM coding agents that addresses issues with conventional append-only trajectory architectures. It aims to improve multi-step decision-making by optimizing how agents manage reasoning and tool calls.

title: CausalGate: Causal Importance Distillation for Transformer Module Pruning
summary: CausalGate introduces a method for Transformer module pruning using causal importance distillation, aiming to improve adaptive inference for large language models. It addresses limitations of existing correlation-based metrics by focusing on vital structural computations.

title: Progress-conditioned Group Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
summary: This paper proposes Progress-conditioned Group Policy Optimization as a method to train LLM agents more effectively on long-horizon agentic tasks. It aims to overcome sampling imbalance issues encountered in traditional group-based policy optimization for sparse rewards.

title: QFedPolyp: A Communication- and Inference-Efficient Federated Learning Framework for Polyp Segmentation
summary: QFedPolyp is a communication- and inference-efficient federated learning framework developed for automatic polyp segmentation in medical imaging. It aims to preserve data privacy while reducing communication costs in distributed deep learning for healthcare.

title: Learning to Access Computation: Accessibility Plasticity as a Principle of Adaptive Intelligence
summary: This paper explores "Accessibility Plasticity" as a principle of adaptive intelligence, proposing a novel way for neural networks to learn to access and modify their computational structures beyond just parameter changes. It aims to distinguish computational capability from accessibility.

title: Hierarchical Grading in Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Graded Large Language Models (GLLMs), an algebraic framework that equips transformer representation spaces with a grading. This framework propagates weighted scalar actions through embeddings, self-attention, and the training objective.

title: An Integrated Deep Learning and Statistical Framework for Whole-Network Gene--Environment Association with Leaf Vascular Architecture
summary: This item presents an integrated deep learning and statistical framework for analyzing gene-environment associations with leaf vascular architecture. It applies AI methods to quantify and study complex biological patterns in plant science.

title: Beyond Shapley: An Influence-Based Data Auditing Pipeline for LLM Alignment and Evaluation
summary: This item introduces an influence-based data auditing pipeline, named 'Beyond Shapley', for evaluating and aligning Large Language Models (LLMs). It aims to address data quality issues, structural contradictions, and annotation errors in LLM training datasets.

title: DomainPilot: Domain-Level Loss-Guided Two-Stage Data Mixture Optimization for Efficient Language Model Fine-Tuning
summary: This item introduces 'DomainPilot', a method for domain-level loss-guided two-stage data mixture optimization for efficient language model fine-tuning. It addresses limitations in dynamic data scheduling for large-scale pretraining and supervised fine-tuning of LLMs.

title: Dementia Etiology Diagnosis via Collaborative Meta Knowledge Enhancement
summary: This item explores using collaborative meta knowledge enhancement with AI for diagnosing dementia etiology. It addresses the challenge of complex overlapping symptoms among diseases in medical AI diagnosis.

title: Predicting the Outcome of rTMS Depression Therapy using EEG Signals and CNN
summary: This item describes a study predicting the outcome of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) therapy for depression using EEG signals and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). It utilizes time-frequency methods to represent EEG data for analysis.

title: LC-SEPLM: long-range contact-supervised adaptation for sequence-only protein representation learning
summary: This item presents 'LC-SEPLM', a long-range contact-supervised adaptation method for sequence-only protein representation learning. It aims to improve protein language models by explicitly constraining them to learn three-dimensional residue contacts.

title: Multimodal Surface EMG Hand Gesture Recognition Using Query-Based Transformers for Prosthetic Control
summary: This item proposes a multimodal hand gesture recognition system using query-based Transformers for prosthetic control, based on surface electromyography (sEMG). It seeks to overcome scaling challenges in deep learning architectures for increasing numbers of hand movements.

title: What Softmax Throws Away: Mass-Aware Attention for Evidence Accumulation
summary: This item investigates what information softmax discards and proposes 'Mass-Aware Attention' for evidence accumulation in AI models. It explores how models retain prediction-relevant structural information in their internal representations.

title: Optimizing Transformer Neural Network for Real-Time Outlier Detection on FPGAs
summary: This item focuses on optimizing Transformer Neural Networks for real-time outlier detection in financial time series on FPGAs. The research explores efficient inference time for anomaly detection applications.

title: FMOPF: Latent Flow Matching with Constraint-Aware Interaction Priors for AC Optimal Power Flow
summary: This item introduces 'FMOPF', a method using latent flow matching with constraint-aware interaction priors for AC optimal power flow. It aims to accelerate computations for minimum-cost generation dispatch in electricity market operations.

title: Multimodal Domain Generalization for Depression Detection: An Attention-Based BiLSTM Network with Domain-Adversarial Training
summary: This item presents a multimodal domain generalization framework for depression detection using an Attention-Based BiLSTM Network with Domain-Adversarial Training. It addresses the issue of limited generalization in deep learning models for depression due to domain shift.

title: Physically Verifiable Evidence and LLM-Based Reporting for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
summary: This item discusses the concept of physically verifiable evidence and LLM-based reporting for trustworthy bearing fault diagnosis in safety-critical mechanical systems. It aims to ensure that AI predictions can be checked against physical reality.

title: LithoFormer: A Robust Framework for Stratigraphic Inference via Transformers
summary: This item introduces 'LithoFormer', a robust Transformer-based framework for stratigraphic inference from well log data. This framework is crucial for accurate geological characterization in projects like carbon capture and resource extraction.

title: From Hybrid Mechanistic--Data-Driven Modeling Toward Neuro-Symbolic AI: What, Why, and How
summary: This item discusses the progression from hybrid mechanistic-data-driven modeling towards neuro-symbolic AI. It explores the integration of first-principles with learned components in scientific machine learning and process engineering.

title: MEMENTO: Memory-Guided Memetic Code-as-Policy Evolution
summary: This item introduces 'MEMENTO', a system for memory-guided memetic code-as-policy evolution for long-horizon embodied tasks. It focuses on enabling AI agents to develop and refine their policies through executable control programs.

title: Frustratingly Simple Black-Box Adaptation of Language Models via Logit Bias
summary: This item proposes a 'Frustratingly Simple Black-Box Adaptation' method for language models via logit bias. This technique allows organizations to adapt LLMs for domain-specific tasks and privacy concerns without complex fine-tuning.

title: Same Predictions, Different Reasons: The Effect of Quantization on Model Explanations
summary: This item investigates the effect of post-training quantization on model explanations, showing that while predictions might be similar, the underlying reasons can differ. It explores the interpretability of deep learning models optimized for resource-constrained devices.

title: Spatial Prediction of Soil Microplastics and Organic Matter Using Graph Attention Networks
summary: This item presents a graph-based deep learning approach using Graph Attention Networks (GATs) for spatial prediction of soil microplastics and organic matter. This method helps assess ecosystem health and support sustainable land use.

title: Efficient Learning of Truncated Boolean Product Distributions: Influence to the Rescue
summary: This item addresses the efficient learning of truncated Boolean product distributions, a foundational challenge in high-dimensional statistics. It introduces new methods using 'influence' to estimate natural parameters from constrained samples.

title: Hidden Boundary Motion in Transformer Optimization: Function-Space Orthogonalization of Affine Weight and Bias Updates
summary: This item analyzes 'Hidden Boundary Motion' in Transformer optimization, focusing on function-space orthogonalization of affine weight and bias updates. It delves into the fundamental dynamics of how Transformer networks are optimized.

title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
summary: This paper investigates methods for controlling the distribution-specific curvature during fine-tuning of open-weight models to prevent harmful applications while preserving benign adaptability.

title: Verbalized Particle Posterior: Bayesian Inference over Natural Language Hypotheses
summary: This research introduces Verbalized Particle Posterior, a framework applying Bayesian inference to natural language hypotheses evaluated by LLMs, allowing for uncertainty measures.

title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient in Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes
summary: This paper presents a finite-time analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient (NPG) algorithm within the context of finite-horizon Markov Decision Processes, a core component of Reinforcement Learning.

title: Label-free Industrial Fault Detection via Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A System for Run-to-Failure Prognostics
summary: This research proposes a system for label-free industrial fault detection using Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning to address the scarcity of fault labels in real-world settings.

title: Recycling computational processes of dynamic programming for combinatorial optimization problems: a reservoir computing approach
summary: This paper explores a reservoir computing approach for combinatorial optimization problems, focusing on recycling computational processes of dynamic programming to reduce computational cost.

title: All in One: Generative Modeling as Mean-Field Game Design
summary: This research presents Mean-Field Games as a unifying theoretical framework for continuous-time generative modeling, encompassing various prominent models as special cases.

title: Online Policy Evaluation for MDPs with Dynamic UBSR Measures
summary: This paper addresses online policy evaluation for Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with dynamic UBSR measures, a challenge in risk-aware reinforcement learning.

title: MixQuant: Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces MixQuant, an adaptive mixed-precision quantization method for Large Language Models that dynamically adjusts bitwidths to optimize accuracy for varying memory budgets.

title: The Entropic Bound for Transformers: Why Static Rank Fails and Attention-Native Rank Recovers
summary: This research investigates the Entropic Bound for Transformers, proposing a spectral notion of task-intrinsic capacity to understand minimum model requirements and attention-native rank recovery.

title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models
summary: This paper analyzes Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), an architectural component in Language Models like DeepSeek-V2, explaining how it separates content from position and reduces KV-cache.

title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: This research proposes a self-boosting method for Vision-Language Models using noisy student on-policy self-distillation to improve post-training efficiency and reduce reliance on human data.

title: Diffusion-Guided Search via Exponential Tilting (DiffTilt): An Application to Falsification of Safety-Critical Systems
summary: This paper introduces Diffusion-Guided Search via Exponential Tilting (DiffTilt), a method for discovering rare safety-critical failures in autonomous and cyber-physical systems.

title: Foundation Models and Fine-Tuning: Toward a New Generation of Models for Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper explores the application of foundation models and fine-tuning techniques to develop a new generation of models for zero-shot time series forecasting.

title: In-Context Learning as Implicit Policy Gradient
summary: This research provides a theoretical explanation for in-context learning in Large Language Models, interpreting it as an implicit policy gradient.

title: Wrong Design Intent Is Worse Than None: A Derangement-Control Diagnosis of Header Conditioning in CAD Program Completion
summary: This research evaluates the effectiveness of header conditioning in fine-tuned code LLMs for parametric CAD generation, assessing whether models genuinely leverage design intent information.

title: Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: This paper proposes a domain-prior-regularized graph modeling approach for improved anomaly detection in multivariate sensor time series within cyber-physical systems.

title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models
summary: This research provides an end-to-end generalization analysis of score-based diffusion models, linking finite-sample learning, network parameterization, and numerical discretization to generative quality.

title: Context-Aware Concept Distillation for Trustworthy Flood Prediction
summary: This paper introduces Context-Aware Concept Distillation to enhance the trustworthiness and interpretability of Deep Learning models used for flood prediction.

title: StageGuard: Physiologically Constrained Sleep Staging
summary: This research presents StageGuard, a deep learning model for automated sleep staging that incorporates physiological constraints to achieve higher accuracy and consistency in hypnograms.

title: Explaining GAND: A Resource on Gender-Ambiguous Natural Data & Contrastive Attribution
summary: This paper addresses gender bias in machine translation by introducing GAND (Gender-Ambiguous Natural Data) and a contrastive attribution method to analyze and explain translation biases.

title: MioFFAn: an Annotation Software for Formula Formalization with LLM Automation Capabilities
summary: This research introduces MioFFAn, an annotation software that uses LLM automation to create high-quality datasets for formalizing mathematical expressions in scientific literature, addressing data scarcity.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Reviewer Guideline Design on LLM-Based Automated Peer Review
summary: This study evaluates how different reviewer guideline designs impact the effectiveness of LLM-based automated peer review systems, aiming to improve their performance.

title: Learning When to Reason for Text-to-SQL via SFT and DPO
summary: This paper presents methods using SFT and DPO to teach Text-to-SQL models when to engage in complex reasoning, reducing inference overhead for simpler queries.

title: Between Suppression and Collapse: Evaluating Narrative Unlearning with LENS
summary: This paper introduces LENS (Level-based Evaluation of Narrative Suppression), a new contextualization-based method to evaluate the effectiveness of machine unlearning algorithms in suppressing disinformation narratives in LLMs.

title: PatiGonit22K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Solving Complex Bengali MWPs
summary: This work introduces PatiGonit22K, a comprehensive, large-scale annotated dataset for solving complex Bengali Mathematical Word Problems, addressing a resource gap for evaluating natural language understanding.

title: CHiPS: Character Histograms and Positional Signals for Lightweight Authorship Attribution in Romanian Texts
summary: This research proposes CHiPS, a lightweight character-level method for authorship attribution in Romanian texts, analyzing character histograms and positional signals.

title: Simple Language Normalization Wins: Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification for the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge
summary: This research explores simple language normalization techniques to improve cross-lingual speaker verification, specifically addressing the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge.

title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
summary: This paper demonstrates that LLMs can perform 'invisible reasoning' not fully expressed in their Chain-of-Thought outputs, raising concerns for AI safety and interpretability.

title: Toward Automated Detection of Documentation Inconsistencies in Electronic Health Records
summary: This research explores using a two-stage LLM pipeline to automatically detect internal documentation inconsistencies within real-world Electronic Health Records, characterizing its capabilities and limitations.

title: Beyond Direct Answering: Aligning Educational LLMs as Socratic Guides via Heuristic Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces HeuristicEdu, a pipeline using heuristic reinforcement learning to align educational LLMs like Qwen2 to act as Socratic guides rather than direct answerers.

title: Speech Signals Complement LLMs for Predicting Interpersonal Attraction in Speed Dating
summary: This study shows that speech signals can complement LLM predictions from conversation transcripts to improve the accuracy of predicting interpersonal attraction in speed dating.

title: ADAGE: A Language-Agnostic Pipeline for Analogical Reasoning Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces ADAGE, a new language-agnostic pipeline for evaluating analogical reasoning, designed to overcome linguistic artifacts in existing multilingual benchmarks.

title: Attention-Guided Layer Selection for Contrastive Decoding in Large Language Models
summary: This work proposes attention-guided layer selection to enhance contrastive decoding methods like DoLa, improving the factuality of Large Language Models.

title: LoRA for Gender-Inclusive Rewriting and Activation Steering for Counter-Narrative Generation
summary: This paper presents a system utilizing LoRA and activation steering for gender-inclusive rewriting and counter-narrative generation, developed for the LT-EDI 2026 Shared Task.

title: Beyond a Global Norm: Personalizing Toxicity Sensitivity in Language Models Without Retraining
summary: This paper evaluates training-free methods for personalizing toxicity sensitivity in language models, recognizing subjective perceptions of harmful language for improved alignment.

title: IndicTalk: A Large-Scale Persona-Based Multilingual Conversational Corpus for Indic Languages
summary: This work presents IndicTalk, a large-scale, persona-based, multilingual conversational corpus specifically for Indic languages, including code-mixed dialogues, addressing a resource gap for LLMs.

title: Co-Evolving Graph and Text Memory for Training-Free Multi-Hop Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces a method that co-evolves graph and text memory to enable training-free multi-hop question answering, improving upon existing RAG approaches.

title: BHARATI: Morphology-Aware Tokenizers for Classical Indian Languages with Subword Fertility Analysis
summary: This work introduces BHARATI, a new morphology-aware tokenizer for classical Indian languages, designed to overcome the inefficiencies of standard tokenization algorithms for agglutinative languages.

title: IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems
summary: This paper presents IKS-Instruct, a 24,000-example multilingual dataset designed for instruction tuning LLMs on Indian Knowledge Systems, filling a gap in specialized pedagogical datasets.

title: BERT-based Models vs. Large Language Models for Low-Resource Named Entity Recognition: A Comparative Study on Marathi
summary: This comparative study evaluates BERT-based models against Large Language Models for low-resource Named Entity Recognition (NER) on the Marathi language, highlighting the challenges and performance differences.

title: Joint Optimization for Greedy Longest-match Tokenization
summary: This paper extends previous work on subword vocabularies by proposing a joint optimization approach for greedy longest-match tokenization, aiming to improve compression for fast inference.

title: When Activation Oracles Learn Not to Read: Concept-Specific Blind Spots in Fine-Tuned Oracles
summary: This research investigates Activation Oracles, language models designed to interpret internal activations of other models, revealing concept-specific blind spots that emerge during fine-tuning.

title: LA-RL: Label-Aware Self-Reflection for Reinforcement Learning in Information Extraction
summary: This paper introduces LA-RL, a Label-Aware Self-Reflection method for Reinforcement Learning, designed to improve information extraction by aligning reflection-based corrections with structured output requirements of Large Language Models.

title: Reasoning or Memorization: Can LLMs Understand and Generate Chinese Xiehouyu Riddles?
summary: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models demonstrate genuine reasoning or mere memorization when tasked with understanding and generating novel Chinese Xiehouyu (allegorical two-part sayings) riddles.

title: Do LLM Debates Repeat Arguments Differently Across Languages?
summary: This study analyzes LLM debate transcripts using 'prior-argument similarity' to determine if Large Language Models repeat arguments differently across various languages during discussions.

title: Do Small Models Use the Law You Give Them? Context-Injected Fine-Tuning for Legal QA in Bangladesh
summary: This research explores whether small language models effectively utilize provided legal context for Legal QA in Bangladesh, testing if context-injected fine-tuning improves their performance on curated bilingual datasets.

title: Two Regimes of Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness: Behavioral Detection Fails Where Models Are Wrong
summary: This paper identifies two types of unfaithfulness in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) explanations, demonstrating that behavioral detection methods often fail to identify unfaithful reasoning when models produce incorrect answers.

title: Mwando: Leveraging AI to Preserve and Teach shiKomori
summary: This paper presents Mwando, a virtual educational assistant leveraging AI to support the teaching and preservation of shiKomori, covering its four main dialectal variants through a constructed knowledge base.

title: The Cross-Domain Generalization Cost of Offensive Language Detection
summary: This study analyzes the performance degradation of offensive language detection models across different datasets and languages, proposing a systematic methodology to identify the causes of this cross-domain generalization cost.

title: Do Diagrams Help Large Language Models Reason? Evidence from Syllogistic Reasoning
summary: This research investigates whether diagrams can enhance the reasoning abilities of Large Language Models, providing evidence from a study on syllogistic reasoning under various representational conditions.

title: Novel Claim or D\'ej\`a Vu? Rethinking "Contamination-Free'' Dynamic Evaluation for Multimodal Automated Fact-Checking
summary: This paper re-evaluates existing benchmarks for Multimodal Automated Fact-Checking, highlighting the risk of data contamination and proposing a rethinking of 'contamination-free' dynamic evaluation methods.

title: The JEPA Paradox in Language: The Geometry of Linguistic Alternatives
summary: This paper explores the 'JEPA Paradox' in language, investigating why Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are not commonly used as text encoders despite their effectiveness in other modalities.

title: Guiding Language Models to Be More Empathetic: Culturally Sensitive Mental Health Advice Generation Through Human-LLM Collaboration
summary: This research focuses on guiding Large Language Models to generate more empathetic and culturally sensitive mental health advice, particularly for low-resource languages, through human-LLM collaboration and a curated dataset.

title: Language Shapes Instruction Hierarchy Compliance in Multilingual LLMs
summary: This study examines how different languages influence the compliance of multilingual Large Language Models with instruction hierarchies, moving beyond English-centric evaluation approaches.

title: EmoTrace: An Emotion Trajectory-Centered Framework for Psychological Support Dialogue Generation
summary: This paper introduces EmoTrace, an emotion trajectory-centered framework for generating psychological support dialogues using Large Language Models, emphasizing the importance of high-quality corpora for training.

title: An empirical investigation into the properties of standard word embeddings
summary: This empirical investigation delves into the fundamental properties of standard word embeddings, which are crucial components in various Natural Language Processing applications.

title: Formally Verified Synthesizable Floating-Point Data Types in ARCH HDL
summary: This report details the design and formal verification of IEEE-754 binary32 (FP32) and bfloat16 (BF16) floating-point arithmetic for ARCH, a hardware description language intended for generation by language models.

title: Zing: Social Mind for LLMs
summary: This report presents Zing (Zhijing), an integrated framework designed to instill social intelligence in Large Language Models, enabling them to infer mental states, track social relations, and adapt behavior for long-term human interaction.

title: How Context Attribution Handles What the Model Already Knows
summary: This research investigates how context attribution methods for Large Language Models differentiate between information derived from input context and knowledge already present in the model's training data.

title: A Frozen 12B Beats Frontier Models on Verified Work: 100% Accuracy, 0 Tokens, Bit-Exact, Forever
summary: This paper proposes an alternative to retraining large language models by keeping the model frozen and growing a persistent memory of verified solutions alongside it. This approach aims for 100% accuracy and bit-exact output by leveraging an external memory.

title: Indic DiarBench: A Multilingual Joint Diarization and ASR Benchmark for Indian Languages
summary: This work introduces Indic DiarBench, a new multilingual benchmark dataset for speaker diarization and ASR, covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages. The corpus contains 108 hours of multi-speaker audio from various real-world scenarios.

title: Earnings25: A Comprehensive 500-Hour Speech Benchmark for Finance
summary: This paper introduces Earnings25, a 500-hour finance-domain benchmark for evaluating automatic speech recognition (ASR) models on English-language earnings calls. It includes two test sets for comprehensive evaluation under realistic conditions.

title: Understanding Tone-Dependent Inference Cost in Large Language Models
summary: This research examines how prompt tone affects both the accuracy of LLM answers and inference cost, measured by output-token consumption. Experiments were conducted on a MMLU dataset with LLMs prompted in seven different tones to understand these trade-offs.

title: Tag Questions and the Generational Reversal of Sycophancy Across 45 Language Models
summary: This paper investigates how appending tag questions to prompts changes language models' responses, observing a "generational reversal of sycophancy" across 45 models. The study measures this tag effect on 20 decision questions between defensible options.

title: SyRuP: Enhancing System-Prompt Following via Reward-Guided Prediction in LLM Decoding
summary: This paper introduces SyRuP, a method for enhancing LLM adherence to system prompts through reward-guided prediction during decoding. It addresses the challenge of insufficient implicit prompt following for complex or compositional instructions.

title: MoLGE: Mixture of Language Group Experts for Efficient Scaling of Massively Multilingual Speech Recognition
summary: This paper introduces MoLGE (Mixture of Language Group Experts), a method for efficiently scaling massively multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) models. It aims to mitigate the "curse of multilinguality" and maintain robust performance across diverse languages.

title: Pointer-Augmented Autoregressive Generation of Patent Claims with Joint Topology and Content Decoding
summary: This research proposes a pointer-augmented autoregressive generation method with joint topology and content decoding for patent claims. This approach addresses the limitation of standard autoregressive decoders in enforcing hierarchical constraints for complex structured outputs.

title: LLM-Based vs. Lexicon-Based Sentiment Signals for Tail-Risk Detection in Meme Stocks
summary: This paper empirically compares LLM-based and lexicon-based sentiment analysis for extracting market signals from social media to detect tail-risk in meme stocks. It uses Reddit data from r/WallStreetBets to evaluate the effectiveness of these methods.

title: BioSentinel at EXIST 2026: Soft-Label Optimization with XLM-RoBERTa for Sexism Intent Classification in Memes
summary: This paper details the BioSentinel team's participation in the EXIST 2026 Task 2.2 for sexism intent classification in memes. The team utilized soft-label optimization with XLM-RoBERTa to classify communicative intent in a learning-with-disagreement setting.

title: Looking for Affect in Spontaneous Finnish Speech through Linguistic Interpretability
summary: This research investigates affect in spontaneous Finnish speech by exploring the linguistic interpretability of emotional arousal and valence. It aims to clarify the relative contributions of acoustic characteristics and content-related linguistic aspects in the perceptual process.

title: Where Quality Breaks in Compressed Short-Text Generation: Staged Bottleneck Localization
summary: This paper studies where quality breaks in compressed short-text generation, localizing failure points to either the codec discarding information or the latent generator producing weak codes. It emphasizes the importance of separating these failure modes for targeted improvements.

title: StanceFlip: A Comprehensive Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multimodal Conversational Stance Flipping Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces StanceFlip, a comprehensive multi-dimensional benchmark for multimodal conversational stance flipping forecasting. It addresses limitations of existing benchmarks by capturing the dynamic evolution of beliefs and disentangling affective states during stance reversals.

title: A New Role for Relevance: Guiding Corpus Interaction in Agentic Search
summary: This paper proposes a new role for relevance in guiding corpus interaction within agentic search systems. It suggests that direct corpus interaction is needed beyond simple top-k content selection to localize, compose, and verify evidence for complex questions.

title: CAGE: Cognitive Attribution Graphs for Faithful Inline Citation Generation in Long-Form Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces CAGE (Cognitive Attribution Graphs) for generating faithful inline citations in long-form question answering, making LLM outputs verifiable. It addresses the issue of existing systems often attaching insufficient citations by identifying attribution inconsistencies.

title: Accuracy Hides How Language Models Fail: Measuring Failure States Under Matched Output Budgets
summary: This paper introduces a two-layer evaluation framework designed to separate scorer-independent execution evidence from answer correctness, aiming to reveal how language models fail. It argues that traditional accuracy metrics can obscure failure states in LLM performance.

title: INS-ActBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Professional Actuarial Capability of Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces INS-ActBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess the professional actuarial capabilities of large language models. It aims to evaluate LLMs across domain knowledge, numerical reasoning, long-context understanding, and tool use within realistic professional workflows.

title: The Tokenizer Tax: Quantifying and Explaining the Cross-Lingual Cost of Subword Tokenization for Indian Languages
summary: This paper quantifies and explains the "tokenizer tax," a systematic cross-lingual disadvantage for Indian languages in large language models due to English-centric subword tokenizers. It demonstrates how this impacts non-English language processing.

title: DINOv3-MIL: Per-Kidney Multi-Label Tumour and Cyst Detection from Foundation-Model Patch Tokens on KiTS23
summary: This paper describes DINOv3-MIL, a method for per-kidney multi-label tumor and cyst detection using foundation vision models on KiTS23 dataset. It focuses on aggregating patch tokens for volumetric classification and comparing different aggregation strategies.

title: MegaSlide-DiT: Memory-Centric Adaptation and Deformable Local Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces MegaSlide-DiT, a memory-centric adaptation and deformable local attention method for efficient video diffusion models. It addresses the high memory requirements of high-resolution video diffusion by optimizing the Diffusion Transformer architecture.

title: FogDrive: A Multi-Modal Synthetic Driving Dataset for Perception under Graded Fog
summary: This paper introduces FogDrive, a multi-modal synthetic driving dataset designed to address the lack of systematic multi-modal alignments in existing benchmarks for evaluating autonomous driving perception under adverse weather conditions like fog.

title: MIME: Multimodal Interactive Motion Encoder
summary: This research introduces MIME (Multimodal Interactive Motion Encoder), a new model for text-motion representation learning that aligns language with individual and relational dynamics for multi-person interactions in animation, AR/VR, and embodied AI.

title: Histopathological Spectrum-Guided Prostate Stratification via Segmentation-Assisted Diagnostic Transformer
summary: This paper proposes a Segmentation-Assisted Diagnostic Transformer for histopathological spectrum-guided prostate stratification, aiming to provide more precise prostate cancer diagnosis beyond subjective PI-RADS assessments or binary classifications.

title: Visible-Light Imaging Diagnosis of Neutral Particle Emission Tomography in the Tokamak Divertor: An Efficient Transformer-based Surrogate Model
summary: This research focuses on using a Transformer-based surrogate model for visible-light imaging diagnosis of neutral particle emission tomography in the Tokamak Divertor, aiding plasma observation and analysis in nuclear fusion studies.

title: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
summary: This paper presents StepX-Edge, a new on-device UI Vision-Language Model developed through architecture-training-deployment co-design, addressing the balance between accuracy and efficiency for comprehensive UI understanding on end devices.

title: RMS@CC-MMD 2026: Multimodal Misogyny Detection via Geometric Interaction and Multi-View Consensus
summary: This paper introduces GeoMVC (Geometric Interaction and Multi-View Consensus), a method for multimodal misogyny detection in internet memes, addressing the complexities of implicit hateful intent in visual and textual content for automated moderation.

title: scMIR: a vision-language foundation model for single-cell light microscopy image representation
summary: This work introduces scMIR, a vision-language foundation model designed for single-cell light microscopy image representation, aiming to improve high-throughput automated analysis of complex and heterogeneous cell phenotypes.

title: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation with Optimized RetinaNet Architectures for Embedded Automotive Systems
summary: This paper presents an optimized semantic segmentation architecture derived from RetinaNet, designed for real-time perception in embedded automotive systems, addressing compute, memory, and power constraints for advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles.

title: Child-Oriented AIGC Video Risk Reviewing: A Benchmark and Knowledge-Supported Iterative Reasoning Framework
summary: This paper introduces a new benchmark and a Knowledge-Supported Iterative Reasoning Framework for child-oriented AIGC (Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content) video risk reviewing, aiming to assess and mitigate risks in content consumed by children.

title: Visual Token Compression Enhances Robustness of MLLMs
summary: This research demonstrates that visual token pruning can enhance the robustness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), mitigating vulnerabilities such as jailbreak attacks and hallucinations by addressing misaligned vision and language modalities.

title: DAMamba-UNet3D: A Parameter-Efficient Mamba State Space U-Net with Dynamic Adaptive Scan for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes DAMamba-UNet3D, a parameter-efficient Mamba State Space U-Net with a dynamic adaptive scan, specifically designed for 3D medical image segmentation to improve efficiency and global context reasoning.

title: $\gamma$-Bridge: A Look-Parametric Diffusion Bridge
summary: This paper introduces $\gamma$-Bridge, a look-parametric diffusion bridge model, which is a new diffusion denoiser that parameterizes its forward process based on the physical properties of signal degradation, particularly for multiplicative Gamma noise in coherent imaging.

title: An Interactive Vision Language Platform for Cognitive Remediation in Schizophrenia
summary: This paper describes an Interactive Vision Language Platform designed for cognitive remediation in patients with schizophrenia, helping them perform structured tasks involving object manipulation and sequential reasoning to address cognitive deficits.

title: Visual Information Extraction from Documents via Classification-Guided Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This research proposes a method for Visual Information Extraction from documents using Classification-Guided Large Vision-Language Models, aiming to overcome challenges posed by layout variability and real-world impairments in visually rich documents.

title: Structural Preservation Governs Data Augmentation in Deep Learning-Based Laser Speckle Material Classification
summary: This study investigates how structural preservation governs data augmentation in deep learning-based laser speckle material classification, finding that standard augmentation policies are often mismatched to the unique characteristics of coherent imaging.

title: PCA: Persistence-Aware Compression and Aggregation for Fast Video Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces PCA (Persistence-Aware Compression and Aggregation), a training-free technique designed to enhance the efficiency and reasoning capabilities of Video Large Language Models (VLLMs) by addressing redundancy in long-duration video frames.

title: Trustworthy Medical Segmentation: Uncertainty-Aware U-Net Evaluation Under Clinical Image Degradation
summary: This research focuses on Trustworthy Medical Segmentation by presenting an Uncertainty-Aware U-Net Evaluation framework, aiming to assess the reliability of medical image segmentation models under various clinical image degradations.

title: Open Your Model's Eyes: Video and Context-Aware Multimodal Backchannel Prediction
summary: This research introduces a Video and Context-Aware Multimodal Backchannel Prediction model, aiming to improve the prediction of listener states by incorporating crucial visual cues and broader conversational contexts alongside audio and text.

title: Calibration-Free 3D Multi-Camera People Tracking for Indoor Environment
summary: This paper proposes a Calibration-Free 3D Multi-Camera People Tracking method for indoor environments, addressing the bottleneck of manual camera calibration in large-scale dataset generation for 3D tracking systems.

title: Generative Augmentation for EEG Motor Imagery Classification: A Class-Conditional VAE with Cycle-Consistent Decoder Refinement
summary: This research investigates the use of Generative Augmentation for EEG Motor Imagery Classification, employing a Class-Conditional VAE with Cycle-Consistent Decoder Refinement to supply synthetic trials that improve classifier accuracy.

title: Fast Fourier Convolutional GAN for 30 m Clear-Sky Land Surface Temperature Gap-Free Reconstruction
summary: This paper presents a Fast Fourier Convolutional GAN for reconstructing 30-meter clear-sky Land Surface Temperature data, addressing data gaps caused by clouds in satellite-derived measurements.

title: Benchmarking the Domain Gap: Model Selection Instability Under Domain Shift in Video Capsule Endoscopy
summary: This study benchmarks model selection instability under domain shift for video capsule endoscopy classification, using multiple datasets to examine robustness across different acquisition sources and labeling policies.

title: Cortex: Compact Behavior Cloning for Quake with Frozen Visual Features
summary: This research introduces Cortex, a compact behavior cloning policy with 10.98 million parameters, to explore its performance in the visually rich first-person game Quake using a frozen DINOv3 encoder.

title: A Diagnostic Gap Framework for Evaluating Reconstruction Fidelity in Weakly Supervised Mammography
summary: This paper proposes a Diagnostic Gap Framework to evaluate the reconstruction fidelity of weakly supervised pipelines in mammography, providing insight into clinically relevant aspects often missed by standard metrics.

title: AI-generated Images Challenge Visual Trust in High-risk Scenarios
summary: This article discusses how rapid advances in AI-generated images challenge visual trust in high-risk scenarios, eroding the evidentiary value of content in contexts where authenticity impacts public safety and reputation.

title: Post-Operative Glioma Segmentation via Loss Stabilization, Normalization and Subspace Attention
summary: This research presents a method for post-operative glioma segmentation by employing loss stabilization, normalization, and subspace attention, aiming to improve generalization across clinical settings.

title: Cheap Probes Predict Expensive Training in 3D-CT Vision--Language Models
summary: This paper explores using 'cheap probes' to predict the outcomes of expensive training for 3D-CT Vision-Language Models, helping to efficiently select optimal image encoders and token-compression schemes.

title: Hybrid Semantic and Spectral Ensemble for Robust Synthetic Image Source Attribution
summary: This research proposes a Hybrid Semantic and Spectral Ensemble method for robust Synthetic Image Source Attribution, addressing challenges posed by distribution shifts from post-processing operations on images from text-to-image models.

title: ID-V2V: Identity-Preserving Video Restylization
summary: ID-V2V is presented as a novel identity-preserving video restylization capability, enabling flexible visual edits in generative video models while maintaining human identity and performance.

title: Robustifying pathology foundation models via fine-tuning
summary: This study develops a novel fine-tuning recipe to robustify pathology foundation models, improving their performance against scanner and staining variability for better deployment across laboratories.

title: Spatial-IQ: Deconstructing Spatial Intelligence via Hierarchical Capability Tests
summary: Spatial-IQ is introduced as a new set of hierarchical capability tests designed to deconstruct spatial intelligence and evaluate multimodal large language models, aiming to identify underlying causes of performance limitations.

title: AdaKAN: A dual-branch adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold network for medical image segmentation
summary: AdaKAN is introduced as a novel dual-branch adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold network designed to improve medical image segmentation, addressing challenges from anatomical complexity and imaging variability.

title: Small-Pollinator Detection in Cluttered Field Video
summary: This empirical study investigates small-pollinator detection in cluttered field video, focusing on practical challenges like small targets, visual similarity, and occlusion under a single-GPU compute budget.

title: Controlling Embedding Spaces with Text-Conditioned Transformations
summary: This research explores methods for controlling multimodal embedding spaces using text-conditioned transformations, enabling finer manipulation of semantic information stored within these embeddings in models like CLIP.

title: Layering Virtual Try-On
summary: This work presents an advancement in Virtual Try-On (VTON) methods, enabling realistic layering of garments, which is a fundamental real-world fashion task previously challenging for single-layer replacement systems.

title: HALLELUAI: A Hallucination-Aware AI System for Ultra-Realistic Image-to-Video Generation at Scale
summary: HALLELUAI is introduced as a hallucination-aware AI system for ultra-realistic image-to-video generation at scale, providing integrated quality control to moderate and regenerate outputs for high precision.

title: mmSimPrior: Learning Simulation Priors for Data-Efficient Real-World Generalizable Radar-Based Human Motion Reconstruction
summary: This paper introduces mmSimPrior, a method for learning simulation priors to enable data-efficient and generalizable radar-based human motion reconstruction, addressing the high cost of collecting diverse real-world data.

title: Breaking the Synthetic-Real Domain Shortcut for Training-Free Generative Replay-based Class Incremental Learning
summary: This research proposes a training-free generative replay method to overcome the synthetic-real domain shortcut in class-incremental learning, mitigating catastrophic forgetting by synthesizing old data.

title: OmniMate: Open-Ended Real-Time Streaming Audio-Visual Generation for Interactive Avatars
summary: OmniMate is presented as a system for open-ended, real-time streaming audio-visual generation, leveraging diffusion models to create interactive avatars from combined audio and visual inputs.

title: When Less Is More: A Controlled Benchmark of Lightweight CNNs for Satellite Land-Cover Segmentation on DeepGlobe
summary: This study presents a controlled benchmark comparing lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for satellite land-cover segmentation on the DeepGlobe dataset, evaluating their efficiency and accuracy trade-offs.

title: Structured Redundancy Modeling for Efficient Visual Token Pruning in High-Resolution MLLMs
summary: This research proposes a method called Structured Redundancy Modeling to efficiently prune visual tokens in high-resolution Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), addressing latency bottlenecks.

title: Similarity Is Not Logic: Factored Inference for Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a factored inference method for dual-encoder vision-language models (VLMs) to improve their compositional reasoning, addressing limitations in zero-shot retrieval where similarity fails logical constraints.

title: DishSeg24k: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Food Segmentation with Stochastic Expert Decoding
summary: This introduces DishSeg24k, a new large-scale benchmark for food segmentation, along with a stochastic expert decoding method, to better capture the complexity of real-world dining scenes.

title: Inverse Bayesian Inference for Extracting Lesion Dynamics from Longitudinal Spectral CT
summary: This research proposes an inverse Bayesian framework for inferring the dynamical parameters of lesions from longitudinal spectral CT medical images.

title: DispatchRAG: Grounding Emergency Dispatch Decisions in Real-World Protocols from Traffic Accident Video
summary: This paper explores using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground emergency dispatch decisions based on real-world protocols and traffic accident videos.

title: Towards Dual-Brain Minimal Sufficient Representation for Vision-Language Navigation
summary: This research proposes a method for Vision-and-Language Navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE) to learn minimal sufficient representations, aiming to improve agent planning in unseen scenes.

title: Fashion-3DLR: A Controllable 3D Garment Generation Using Pairwise Fashion Elements for Intelligent Design
summary: This work introduces Fashion-3DLR, a controllable 3D garment generation capability that uses pairwise fashion elements to facilitate intelligent design in the digital fashion industry.

title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
summary: This research presents OmniScope, a modality-decoupled token compression method for omnimodal large language models, aiming to improve efficiency by addressing cross-modal salience mismatches.

title: A Replay-Constrained Simulation Framework for Personalization of Powered Knee--Ankle Prosthesis Controllers
summary: This paper proposes a replay-constrained simulation framework for personalizing impedance controllers for powered prosthetic legs, addressing challenges in accommodating individual gait biomechanics.

title: Pose-Aware Modeling to Mitigate Pose-Related Artifacts in Tactile Gloves
summary: This research focuses on using pose-aware modeling to mitigate artifacts in tactile gloves, improving their utility for robotics applications in dexterous manipulation and learning from demonstration.

title: Real2Sim2Real for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation: An AMD ROCm-Based Pipeline
summary: This introduces an AMD ROCm-based Real2Sim2Real pipeline for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, enabling embodied AI agents to act in the real world for manipulation tasks.

title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction
summary: This paper proposes the World-Cognition Model (WCM) to improve human-robot interaction for physical tasks, enhancing robots' ability to interact fluently beyond instruction execution.

title: The Curse of Precision: A Data Scaling Law for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research investigates data scaling laws specifically for high-precision robotic manipulation tasks, exploring the relationship between data and precision in closed-world settings.

title: Low-Latency Turn-Taking via Context-Aware Preface Generation in a Real-World Dialogue Robot
summary: This paper proposes a two-stage incremental framework for a real-world dialogue robot, using context-aware preface generation to achieve low-latency turn-taking in LLM-based dialogue systems.

title: Semantic Semi-Incremental Data-Association-Free Object SLAM
summary: This research proposes a semantic semi-incremental and data-association-free Object SLAM method, leveraging deep learning to address challenges in landmark measurement association.

title: PRISM: Polynomial Representations for Interaction-Structured Motor Control
summary: This paper introduces PRISM, a method using polynomial representations for interaction-structured motor control in robots, allowing policies to better capture physical variables and their interactions.

title: LEACL: LLM-Enhanced Automatic Curriculum Learning for Reinforcement Learning in Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks
summary: This research proposes LLM-Enhanced Automatic Curriculum Learning (LEACL) for reinforcement learning, aiming to solve long-horizon manipulation tasks by progressively training agents.

title: Anticipatory Risk-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Safe Flight Through Dynamic Clutter
summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning approach for safe quadrotor navigation, focusing on anticipatory risk-guidance to enable flight through cluttered and dynamic environments.

title: Towards Ultrafast Depth Sensing Via Active Event-based Stereo Vision
summary: This research proposes a novel paradigm for ultrafast depth sensing using active event-based stereo vision, addressing challenges in fast-motion scenarios for conventional imaging systems.

title: Try Once, Then Optimal: De-Redundified Procedure Memory for Cross-Episode Exploration Amortization
summary: This research introduces a de-redundified procedure memory approach to optimize robot exploration for manipulating objects with hidden internal states, improving efficiency across multiple episodes.

title: LabRobFail: A Benchmark for Robotic Failure Analysis in Chemical Self-driving Laboratories
summary: This paper introduces LabRobFail, a benchmark designed to analyze robotic failures in chemical self-driving laboratories, aiming to improve the reliability of embodied agents in scientific discovery.

title: Hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic for Sparse-Reward Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes a two-level Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning framework to address challenges in sparse-reward long-horizon tasks by separating high-level strategic planning from low-level continuous control.

title: Learning Traversability-Aware Global Planners for Long Horizon Off-Road Navigation
summary: This research focuses on learning traversability-aware global planners to enable long-horizon autonomous navigation for vehicles in challenging off-road environments, utilizing geo-spatial data.

title: $N_0$-VTLA: Scaling Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Model with Latent Tactile Tokens
summary: This paper introduces $N_0$-VTLA, a vision-tactile-language-action foundation model capable of fine-grained contact-rich manipulation, tactile feedback control, and offline policy improvement.

title: $N_0$-TWAM: Scaling Tactile-Native World-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: This research presents $N_0$-TWAM, a tactile-native world-action model designed for contact-rich manipulation that predicts both future vision and future contact, trained at a large scale.

title: A Few Words Go a Long Way: Language Guided Robot Policy Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes ARCHITECT, a framework for language-guided robot policy synthesis that aims to improve the interpretability, adaptability, and correctability of robot manipulation policies derived from vision-language-action models.

title: Memory for Attention: Language-Conditioned Re-Perception with a Vision--Language--Motion Map
summary: This research investigates a robot's ability to use a language-conditioned re-perception mechanism with a Vision-Language-Motion Map to enhance spatial navigation and information recall.

title: Embodied GPT-5.1: Evidence of a World Model?
summary: This exploratory study investigates whether a large multimodal language model, hypothetically GPT-5.1, can effectively serve as a high-level controller for a physical mobile robot despite lacking prior embodiment training.

title: LeapBot-WA: World-Anchor Action Models via Predictive Latent Alignments
summary: This paper introduces LeapBot-WA, a novel approach to World Action Models using predictive latent alignments to improve embodied intelligence by overcoming the bottlenecks of pixel-level video generation.

title: FutureRTC: Real-Time Robot Execution with Anticipatory-Conditioned Action Chunking
summary: This research proposes FutureRTC, a method for real-time robot execution that uses anticipatory-conditioned action chunking to mitigate prediction-execution misalignment in asynchronous Vision-Language-Action policies.

title: WARL: Wrench-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Task-Agnostic Learning in Legged Robots
summary: This study introduces Wrench-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (WARL), a new method designed to enhance the exploration capabilities and motor performance of legged robots by moving beyond joint-space actions.

title: Effective Parameters, Real Behavior: Renormalization for Robotics -- From Infinite Electron Mass to Sim-to-Real Gap
summary: This paper proposes a novel approach for bridging the sim-to-real gap in robotics by applying renormalization, using effective, resolution-dependent parameters to absorb simulator omissions and reproduce real behavior.

title: A Case Study on the Acceptance of a Humanoid Robotic Head Employed in Three Public Spaces
summary: This case study examines the acceptance of a humanoid robotic head in public spaces, detailing its ability to process natural language and generate multimodal, emotionally expressive responses.

title: DeVA: Decoupled Video-Action Model with physical guidance for robot policy learning
summary: This paper introduces DeVA, a Decoupled Video-Action Model that incorporates physical guidance for learning generalizable robot manipulation policies, addressing limitations of current Vision-Language-Action models.

title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim

title: FloAff-Kitchen: Bridging Navigation and Manipulation via Canonical and Progressive Floor Affordance Learning

title: Quality-Adaptive Multi-UAV 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Workload Redistribution
summary: This research presents a method for quality-adaptive 3D reconstruction using multiple UAVs, focusing on efficient and scalable path planning and sparse workload redistribution for aerial platforms.

title: Learning Adaptive Multi-Task Guidance, Navigation, and Control via Hypernetworks
summary: This paper introduces a method for learning adaptive multi-task guidance, navigation, and control policies for autonomous free-flying robots in orbital environments using hypernetworks.

title: PAC-DP: PAC-Bayesian Diffusion Policy Learning
summary: This paper proposes PAC-DP, a PAC-Bayesian Diffusion Policy Learning approach that provides better control over generalization for complex robot manipulation tasks, particularly in finite-data regimes.

title: Continual-RL for Generalization in Autonomous Racing on the RoboRacer Platform

title: ArmnetBench v0.1: Parallel Real-World Evaluation of Manipulation Policies on a Low-Cost Arm Farm

title: {\tau}: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision

title: NEO: NeRF It Once, Edit It Many Times for Continuous Object Manipulation

title: Development of a Handheld Actuation Mechanism for a Tendon-driven Robotically Steered Guidewire

title: Data Pyramid for Embodied Manipulation

title: Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Sensor Selection in Maritime Surveillance

title: Learning-based Hierarchical Tracheal Anatomy Understanding from Sparse Surgical Demonstration Annotations for Ultrasound Robots

title: Physical AI Governance: From Theory to Practice Across Life Cycle
summary: This article discusses the governance of 'Physical AI,' which encompasses embodied systems interacting with the real world. It highlights unique challenges related to real-time safety constraints and continuous dynamic interaction.

title: Actuator-Aware Spatiotemporal Tube Synthesis for Temporal Reach-Avoid-Stay Tasks
