title: The biggest bet in history
summary: Crossposted from canaryinstitute.ai/blog/biggest-bet-in-history . Related posts AGI and the EMH: markets are not expecting aligned or unaligned AI in the next 30 years — Trevor Chow, Basil Halperin, J. Zachary Mazlish. The canonical statement of "interest rates as a revealed-preference indicator of AGI timing"; this piece is the capex-side companion. Power Overwhelming: dissecting the $1.5T AI revenue shortfall — ykevinzhang. Runs the same capex-vs-revenue math from a different angle and reaches a similar "the required growth is enormous" conclusion. Bubble, Bubble, Toil and Trouble — Zvi Mowshowitz. Directly addresses the "is hyperscaler capex a fiber-optic-style bubble" question. DeepSeek Made it Even Harder for US AI Companies to Ever Reach Profitability — Garrison Lovely. The "open-weight competition collapses the quality gap and competes profits away" exit path. The biggest bet in history The amount that's been bet on AI shows that the hyperscalers really believe in AGI soon. A subject of endless speculation is "how much of AI is a bubble?". On the one hand, the techies are saying "do you think the graph is really super-exponential, or just regular-exponential?", while on the other hand, the economists are saying "A total of half a percent increase to GDP, arriving over a decade". Talk is cheap, though... who is putting their money where their mouth is? It turns out, the hyperscalers! There's 5 companies who are building out the infrastructure to make AI happen. They're Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle; I propose we call them "GOMMA" (Nvidia isn't on the list because they aren't placing a bet, they're just the bookie). GOMMA have collectively committed $2.5T to building out the infrastructure to make AGI happen (and half of it has already been spent). In dollar terms, it's the largest capital expenditure in history; in GDP terms nothing comes close except railroads in the 19th century (but railroads took 20 years to get up to speed, whereas these folks have gone all-in on AGI in 4 years). Unlike OpenAI & Anthropic, the hyperscalers can't be all talk: they've committed real money, for real hardware, and if the bet doesn't pay off, then they'll lose out, big-time. How big-time? Let's run the math: to build the datacenters to house the Nvidia chips to train the models to provide intelligence on tap, GOMMA have bought around $2.5T in hardware. The value of that hardware is dropping by the minute, at around 25% a year, which means $1T worth of chips in 2025 is only worth $750B in 2026, and is down by about two-thirds come 2029. In fact the chips melt so fast that by the time the buildout wraps up, roughly $800B of those purchases will have already expired. The working pile is about $1.7T. That pile sheds ~$420B per year just from melting, and then shareholders expect a 15% return on the pile (another $250B), meaning about $670B per year. [1] And they want that in profit . That's the money that AI users pay them above and beyond operating costs, whether that's labs renting compute, companies buying AI services directly, or their own AI-powered products. That's a big number! How could they get that? Basically they're counting on OpenAI and Anthropic to sell subscriptions which companies will pay for, because it saves the companies more on salary than they spend in subscriptions, and then the GOMMA get some fraction of the total "salary savings" (Meta and Google will have their own in-house versions, but still want numbers around these lines). A plausible number might be that they get to keep one-third of all the salary savings. And note that one-third is generous by every historical measurement, [2] quite apart from being the likely cap while open-weight models exist. Since all the SWE in the USA only pull in around $450B/year, [3] they're going to need more than that (because they'd only take in $150B even if every single SWE was replaced with Codex). Well what if instead they were to capture some percentage of the entire economy that AI could help with? Basically, let's take every single job in the economy, figure out which one could be done by AI, see how much folks currently get paid for doing it, and see how much that adds up to. That's a tall order for a blog post, but fortunately we've already done it , and about 59% of USA labor could be augmented by AI; those salaries total about $8.5T per year. In that case, GOMMA's take would only need to amount to about 8% of those salaries to make this a worthwhile bet. Note that this implies massive efficiency gains to the economy. For their one-third slice to equal 8% of those salaries, the total savings (productivity across that share of the workforce) will need to rise by roughly 24%. So they are absolutely serious about this, and are betting heavily that the productivity boost arrives within four years . If they're right, Acemoglu will be eating crow by the end of 2029, since that's about 50x what he estimated the impact of AI would be. [4] Other than tweaking Daron, my primary point is that while OpenAI and Anthropic might be willing to make a big existential bet for a shot at owning the whole future, there's no way the hyperscalers are willing to get stuck holding the bag for them (OK, Google can probably eat the loss, but we'll just all have to watch 2 extra YouTube ads). Each curve shows the annual productivity savings the US economy must deliver, as a function of what share of those savings AI vendors keep as revenue. Base: AI-addressable wages (tasks within current AI cognitive ability, minimal physical requirements, and no regulatory barriers) totaling $8.46T/yr, 59% of the US wage bill. Solid: the full $667B/yr the hardware must earn (depreciation + 15% return). Dashed: mere break-even ($417B/yr, depreciation only). Orange: innovators' typical historical capture rate (Nordhaus 2004); impossible to recover full investment. There's a fairly fine needle to thread, because while the frontier labs are charging dearly, the competition is right behind them and charging almost nothing. The open-weight models are currently selling at a twentieth the frontier price. So folks who are willing to wait 8 months can get almost the same product, but much, much cheaper. So there's no comfortable middle world for GOMMA, where this peters out into solid-but-dependable profits. Either AGI happens and the gap holds (the entire world gets transformed, and they get paid); or governments ban open-weight models, freezing the competition in place (so GOMMA get paid, transformation optional); or the open-weight companies close the capability gap, and the profits get competed away no matter how good AI gets . This happened in the 1990s with fiber-optics; the investors were 100% right about the internet, but lost their shirts anyway. But everyone at GOMMA doing the finance math already knows all of this, so they probably ALSO believe that AGI is coming soon. We've known that the frontier labs have taken this for granted, but it sounds like they've convinced the finance guys at GOMMA as well, which seems a taller order (there's actually one other dynamic, in which they all know someone will lose, and are just hoping it isn't them, but that's another post). One thing is very, very clear: AI might not be transformative, but it's not going to whimper away. If AGI doesn't arrive, then there will be a bust to make "dotcom" look like a fire drill. For the finance-inclined: the $2.45T of cumulative 2024-27 purchases nets out, after depreciation-in-transit, to a surviving capital stock of ~$1.67T; the annual requirement is Jorgenson user cost, (r + delta) x K = (0.15 + 0.25) x $1.67T = ~$667B/yr of gross profit (i.e. before depreciation, which the bar exists to pay). Under more forgiving assumptions (r = 8%, delta = 15%, consistent with used-GPU resale values) the bar falls to roughly $480-500B/yr, and no conclusion here changes anywhere in that band. Capex, depreciation, and the 15% required return (an asset-manager hurdle rate; Vanguard's published range is 10-25%) follow Wachter & Wachter, "What Investment Data Implies about the AI Transition" (NBER Working Paper 35290, 2026: https://www.nber.org/papers/w35290 ), which also documents the railroad and telecom comparisons in the second paragraph. Depreciation-rate evidence and full sensitivity analysis in the linked repo. ↩︎ Historically, innovators keep far less than a third of the value they create. Economy-wide, Nordhaus estimates innovators captured about 2.2% of the total social surplus from innovation (US nonfarm business, 1948-2001), starting from only ~7% initial appropriability and eroding at ~20% per year as competitors imitate ( Schumpeterian Profits in the American Economy , NBER WP 10433, 2004). The friendliest measured benchmark is Mansfield et al. ( QJE 1977): across 17 industrial innovations, the median private rate of return (25%) ran less than half the median social rate (56%). So one-third sits at or above the top of the measured range, which means the 24% productivity requirement derived above is a floor: at historically typical capture rates, the boom required to justify the spending would be far larger. ↩︎ BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics: ~1.9M software developers and adjacent occupations at ~$290B/yr in cash wages; loaded ~1.45x for benefits and employer taxes (BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation) gives ~$420-450B/yr fully-loaded. ↩︎ Acemoglu, "The Simple Macroeconomics of AI" (2024): total factor productivity gains from AI of ~0.5-0.7% cumulatively over ten years , driven by his estimate that only a modest share of tasks are exposed to current AI capabilities at worthwhile cost. The comparison here is a level-vs-level one: ~24% productivity on ~59% of wages is a ~14% economy-wide level effect, against his ~0.5%. If his forecast is right, the biggest capital misallocation in history is currently underway. The two claims cannot both be true, and the revenue numbers between now and 2029 will decide it. ↩︎ Discuss

title: Emergent Sparsity in Frozen Random CNN Feature Extractors for Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research reports the emergent phenomenon of extreme sparsity in fully-connected representations within deep reinforcement learning agents trained with frozen, randomly initialized CNN feature extractors.

title: Meta-Learned Reward Shaping for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: This paper introduces MeRLa (Meta-Learned Reward Shaping) to improve Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) by addressing limitations of static reward models for aligning large language models.

title: Data Fusion and Contrastive Alignment for Unconstrained IR Molecular Structure Elucidation
summary: This research proposes data fusion and contrastive alignment methods for unconstrained IR molecular structure elucidation, aiming to overcome limitations imposed by reliance on pre-determined chemical formulas.

title: Shared SFT Lessons Across Alignment, Model Organisms, and Toy Models
summary: This research explores shared lessons in supervised fine-tuning (SFT) across AI alignment, model organisms, and toy models, investigating whether training techniques can transfer between these distinct research areas.

title: Dynamic Parameterization Is Not Dynamic Inference
summary: This paper clarifies the concepts of dynamic parameterization and dynamic inference in AI models, distinguishing between coefficient variation, input-dependent coefficient assignment, and conditional execution to prevent misinterpretations regarding computational savings.

title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation
summary: This research introduces "Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation," a novel method for transferring capabilities across large language models by aligning a student model with a teacher's token-level distribution during the student's own rollouts.

title: Between Gradient and Natural Gradient: A Continuum of LoRA Initializations
summary: This paper explores different initialization schemes for Low-rank adaptation (LoRA), a fine-tuning technique for large pretrained models, to optimize its performance, focusing on a continuum between gradient and natural gradient approaches.

title: Early Verdicts, Better Budgets: Sequential Adaptive Rollout Allocation for Compute-Efficient RLVR
summary: This research introduces "Sequential Adaptive Rollout Allocation," a method designed to improve the compute efficiency of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) by optimizing rollout generation and addressing issues with saturated prompt groups.

title: FloDR: An invertible dimensionality reduction method based on a normalising flow
summary: This paper presents "FloDR," a novel invertible dimensionality reduction method based on normalizing flows, designed to provide more accurate and interpretable two-dimensional embeddings of high-dimensional data.

title: Learning Implicit Causal World Models from Multi-Agent Demonstrations
summary: This research explores a method for learning implicit causal world models from multi-agent demonstrations, addressing the challenge of distinguishing statistical correlations from causal mechanisms in model-based reinforcement learning.

title: RAGuard: A Layered Defense Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems Against Data Poisoning
summary: This paper introduces "RAGuard," a layered defense framework designed to protect Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems from factual corpus-poisoning attacks, which maliciously manipulate retrieved evidence to mislead large language models.

title: Automorphism-Induced Non-Canonicity in Top-k Explanations of Graph Neural Networks
summary: This research highlights an "automorphism-induced non-canonicity" issue in gradient-based Graph Neural Network explainers, where permutation equivariance leads to invariant and potentially problematic attribution scores for chemically equivalent parts of a molecule.

title: Post-Training at the Edge of Detectability: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper proposes a game-theoretic approach to reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning for language models, aiming to optimize performance on target tasks while effectively limiting model drift from a reference policy.

title: ClockRoPE: Random Fourier Rotations for Temporal Routine Modeling
summary: This paper introduces "ClockRoPE," a novel extension of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) using random Fourier rotations, designed to improve temporal routine modeling in transformer-based large language models beyond the limitations of RoPE's log-linear frequency schedule.

title: Q-Steer: Action-Value Guidance for Molecular Policy Optimization
summary: This paper presents "Q-Steer," a novel method providing action-value guidance for molecular policy optimization, designed to overcome the challenges of delayed feedback in oracle-limited molecular generation tasks.

title: Flow Map Learning via Nongradient Vector Flow
summary: This paper proposes "Flow Map Learning via Nongradient Vector Flow," a new method to improve the inference efficiency of diffusion and flow-based models by directly learning the flow maps along the ODE trajectory, thereby reducing sampling overhead.

title: Examining the Efficacy of Graph Neural Network Message-Passing in Regression Contexts
summary: This research examines the effectiveness of message-passing techniques within Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) when applied to various regression contexts, such as predicting properties of molecules or analyzing media networks.

title: SCOUT: Per-Context Reset Curricula for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents "SCOUT," a method utilizing "Per-Context Reset Curricula" to enhance sparse-reward reinforcement learning by starting training rollouts from easier intermediate states, thereby improving task stage reachability.

title: Existence-Field Diffusion Model for Spatial Point Processes with Variable Cardinality
summary: This research introduces an "Existence-Field Diffusion Model" for the generative modeling of spatial point processes, capable of handling variable cardinality and complex spatial configurations.

title: DHRCL:Training Code LLMs with Dense Hierarchical Rewards and Curriculum Learning
summary: This paper presents "DHRCL" (Dense Hierarchical Rewards and Curriculum Learning), a novel post-training paradigm for code-oriented large language models that utilizes richer reward signals and curriculum learning to improve performance.

title: Neural Architecture Search for Traffic Prediction: A Survey of Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: This paper provides a survey of methods, challenges, and future directions for Neural Architecture Search (NAS) applied to traffic prediction, a crucial task in intelligent transportation systems.

title: Learning Dynamic User Personas from Implicit Interaction Streams via Iterative Refinement
summary: This research proposes a method for learning dynamic user personas from implicit interaction streams through iterative refinement, aiming to personalize large language models (LLMs) more effectively for individual users.

title: Conformal Changepoint Localization and Root Cause Analysis with Corrupted Observations
summary: This paper presents a method for "Conformal Changepoint Localization and Root Cause Analysis" designed to detect statistical behavior changes in engineered systems and identify their responsible components, even with corrupted observations.

title: From Conceptual Hydrologic Models to Conceptually Interpretable Neural Networks: A Snow-Water Mass-Conserving-Perceptron Framework for Discovering Catchment-Scale Precipitation-Storage-Runoff Representations
summary: This paper introduces the Mass-Conserving Perceptron (MCP) framework, reformulating conceptual hydrologic models as physically constrained, interpretable neural networks. It develops and evaluates a snow-water MCP network across 513 CAMELS-US basins.

title: From Interface to Inference: Eliciting Any-Order Inference from Any-Order Models
summary: This research explores eliciting "any-order inference" from autoregressive language models for non-causal discrete reasoning tasks like code generation. It addresses the challenge of enabling these models to move between high-level structure and local details.

title: Collaborative Weighting with Pessimistic Critic for Mitigating Overestimation in Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes "Collaborative Weighting with Pessimistic Critic" to mitigate overestimation in deep off-policy reinforcement learning algorithms for continuous control. The method addresses issues with noisy targets and non-stationary optimization.

title: HiFloat4 Format for End-To-End Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces the HiFloat4 Format for the first end-to-end FP4 reinforcement learning post-training of large language models, operating at 4-bit precision. The study investigates sources of degradation in FP4 RL for both rollout and training policies.

title: The Art of Not Forgetting A Local Learning Architecture for Continual Learning
summary: This paper introduces Cognitive Memory Primitive (CMP), a continual-learning architecture that uses a two-tier competitive memory to represent and store inputs as sparse relational codes. It learns through local updates without end-to-end backpropagation.

title: AgentGFM: A Graph Foundation Model with Node-Agent Information-Flow Control
summary: This paper introduces AgentGFM, a Graph Foundation Model designed to learn transferable knowledge from multi-domain graphs and adapt to unseen scenarios. It focuses on the role of node-agent information-flow control in enhancing the transferability of topological patterns.

title: From Tokens to Watt-hours: Analytical Energy Estimation for LLM Inference on Modern GPUs
summary: This research presents a method for analytical energy estimation of large language model (LLM) inference on modern GPUs. It aims to address the growing environmental footprint of deployed AI systems by providing a way to estimate operational energy consumption.

title: Simultaneous Coverage and Efficiency Guarantee in Online Conformal Prediction
summary: This paper addresses limitations in adaptive conformal inference (ACI), the standard approach for online conformal prediction under distribution shift. It aims to provide simultaneous coverage and efficiency guarantees for online conformal prediction methods.

title: Benchmarking ConvLSTM for One-Day-Ahead IMDAA Rainfall-Field Prediction across Four Indian Cities
summary: This study benchmarks Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Networks (ConvLSTMs) for one-day-ahead rainfall-field prediction across four Indian cities using IMDAA data. It investigates the efficacy of convolutional recurrence for precipitation forecasting.

title: Uncertainty-Guided LLM Semantic Augmentation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
summary: This research proposes uncertainty-guided LLM semantic augmentation to improve the estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects, particularly for the conditional average treatment effect (CATE). This method is applicable to targeted interventions in fields like personalized medicine.

title: FedWeave: Rethinking the Unit of Specialization in Heterogeneous Federated MoE-LoRA
summary: This paper introduces FedWeave, a new approach for Federated MoE-LoRA that rethinks the unit of specialization for LLMs in federated learning. It aims to mitigate cross-task interference and gradient conflicts arising from task heterogeneity across clients.

title: Enhancing Automated Machine Learning via Homogeneous Train-Test Splitting Methods
summary: This research proposes enhancing Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) by introducing homogeneous train-test splitting methods. It addresses the limitations of standard random splitting for more accurate model evaluation.

title: RAG-HAR+: Towards Cost-Efficient LLM-Based Human Activity Recognition for Edge Deployment
summary: This paper introduces RAG-HAR+, an LLM-based system for cost-efficient Human Activity Recognition (HAR) from wearable sensors, optimized for edge deployment. It aims to overcome limitations of existing deep learning HAR approaches by leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

title: AIGen: Automating AI Bill of Materials Generation Through Hybrid MLOps Integration
summary: This paper introduces AIGen, a system that automates the generation of an AI Bill of Materials through hybrid MLOps integration. AIGen aims to support the responsible development and deployment of AI systems by rigorously documenting their constituent artifacts.

title: Efficient Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization for Risk-Aware AutoRL
summary: This research proposes efficient heteroscedastic Bayesian optimization for risk-aware automated reinforcement learning (AutoRL). The method addresses the stochastic nature of RL outcomes by optimizing both expected performance and variability under different hyperparameter configurations.

title: Universality and Approximation Rates of Graph Neural Networks with Random Features
summary: This paper investigates the universality and approximation rates of message-passing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) enhanced with random node features. It establishes a novel universality result focusing on permutation-equivariant neural networks.

title: Mixture-of-experts for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors
summary: This study applies a Mixture-of-experts model for online handwriting trajectory reconstruction using data from IMU sensors in a digital pen. The goal is to accurately reconstruct handwriting on any surface for human-computer interaction.

title: PowerAtlas: Towards Electricity-Computing Co-Scheduling for Power Systems
summary: This paper introduces PowerAtlas, a system for coordinated electricity-computing co-scheduling to manage the increasing energy demands of AI workloads in data centers. It addresses the challenge of integrating large-scale, flexible data center loads into power systems.

title: Domain adaptation for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors
summary: This study focuses on using domain adaptation techniques for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors in digital pens. It aims to improve the accuracy of preserving a digital trajectory of handwriting on various surfaces.

title: CalTwin: Towards Calibrated, Shift-Robust Medical World Models via Fisher-Information Regularisation
summary: This paper introduces CalTwin, a method to develop calibrated and shift-robust Medical World Models using Fisher-Information Regularisation. These models aim to learn patient or organ physiology to support tasks from diagnosis to digital-twin treatment planning.

title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution
summary: Introduces SkillRise, an agentic reinforcement learning method for large language model agents to evolve skills across related tasks, addressing limitations of current approaches that treat tasks independently.

title: FedTopo: Relation-Level Topology Sharing for Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning
summary: Presents FedTopo, a method for relation-level topology sharing in federated learning that addresses challenges of model heterogeneity by enabling better transfer of global knowledge across diverse local architectures.

title: Forecasting Trajectory-Level Safety Risks in Black-Box Multi-Turn Interactions
summary: Focuses on forecasting trajectory-level safety risks in multi-turn interactions for autonomous LLM agents, emphasizing the need to understand how malicious intent unfolds over long sequences beyond pointwise risk assessment.

title: Budget-Aware LLM Discovery via Cost-Calibrated Frontier Utility
summary: Introduces a method for budget-aware LLM discovery that considers the cost of search actions, such as prompt length and retries, to optimize scientific and algorithmic discovery processes.

title: Kairos: Numerically Robust News Recommendation under Item Cold-Start via Cholesky-based LinUCB
summary: Proposes Kairos, a numerically robust news recommendation system that addresses the item cold-start problem in regional markets using a Cholesky-based LinUCB approach.

title: Thinking Under Uncertainty: Evidence Use and Information-Seeking in Language Models
summary: Investigates how large language models utilize available evidence and engage in information-seeking during inference-time thinking, distinguishing these responses to understand their impact on decision-making.

title: TREA-Net: A Transferable Residual Epidemiological Adaptation Network for Dengue Incidence Forecasting
summary: Presents TREA-Net, a transferable residual epidemiological adaptation network designed for accurate multi-week dengue incidence forecasting, especially useful for new surveillance systems with limited historical data.

title: Amortized Moment Matching for Visual Generation
summary: Proposes amortized moment matching, a novel method utilizing neural networks to learn data moments as distributional training signals, applying it to visual generation by casting diffusion denoisers through polynomial projections.

title: Británie sází na drony a AI. Chystá největší armádní reformu, čelí ale tvrdé kritice
summary: The UK plans a major military reform leveraging drones and AI to save costs and address manpower shortages, but the strategy is facing significant criticism.

title: Large-Scale ChatBot Validation Through Customer Digital Twin Simulations
summary: Presents a methodology for large-scale validation of LLM-based chatbots, particularly for regulated domains, by employing customer digital twin simulations.

title: Do Methods Support the Claims? Intra-Paper Verification for Peer Review
summary: Explores the use of large language models to assist peer review by performing intra-paper verification, assessing whether a paper's claimed contributions are supported by its described methods.

title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues
summary: Introduces DuplexGen, a system for the adaptive synthesis of human-AI turn-taking dialogues, addressing the limitation of current models in adapting turn-taking behaviors to different contexts.

title: Choosing Where and How to Moderate: End-to-End Trade-offs in Filter Placement and Response Rewriting
summary: Examines the strategic choices in deploying content moderation classifiers, including filter placement and response rewriting, and evaluates their end-to-end impact on customer outcomes rather than just component accuracy.

title: Characterizing Human-Likeness in AI Generated Poetry: A Zero-shot Classification Study
summary: Conducts a zero-shot classification study to characterize the human-likeness of AI-generated poetry, addressing the growing indistinguishability between human and generative AI text and its implications.

title: Steering Instruction Hierarchies at Inference Time
summary: Introduces V-Steer, a training-free inference-time method that enforces instruction hierarchies in large language models to ensure higher-priority inputs, like system prompts, override conflicting lower-priority instructions.

title: Evaluating Prompt Scope and Demonstration Similarity in Local LLM Machine Translation
summary: Evaluates the behavior of large language models in machine translation across various prompt scopes and demonstration similarities, exploring how users might ask for translations beyond single sentences.

title: AgentGUI: An Interface for Observing and Steering Long-Running AI Agents
summary: Introduces AgentGUI, a user-friendly, locally hosted graphical user interface designed to provide human oversight and steering capabilities for complex, long-running AI agents.

title: When Synthetic Users Fail: A Cross-Domain Benchmark of LLM-Simulated Human Survey Responses
summary: Investigates the validity of using large language models as synthetic users for simulating human survey responses, introducing an evaluation framework to determine when this substitution is reliable or fails.

title: Symphony of Bias: Exploring Gender Associations with Musical Instruments in Multimodal LLMs
summary: Explores gender bias in large language models by analyzing their associations with musical instruments, raising concerns about the models' potential to perpetuate social stereotypes.

title: Diagnosing Fine-Grained Inconsistency Classification in Financial Disclosure Text
summary: This research focuses on using AI to diagnose and classify fine-grained inconsistencies in financial disclosure texts, aiming to identify different types of conflicts within numerical claims, temporal statements, and policy commitments.

title: (Im)Paired Programming: Coding Agents Improve Productivity but Harm Understanding
summary: This study investigates how coding agents, while improving developer productivity, may negatively impact users' understanding by shifting from code writing to prompting and reviewing, potentially impeding oversight and learning.

title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment
summary: This research explores the phenomenon of broad misalignment in fine-tuned language models, proposing an interpretable account where misalignment emerges as a shift in "personality" within the Big Five framework.

title: Knowledge before Reasoning: EC-Reason-Bench, a Training-Free Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM Enzyme Classification
summary: This paper introduces EC-Reason-Bench, a new training-free diagnostic benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' capabilities in hierarchical enzyme classification, highlighting their current limitations in predicting complete EC numbers.

title: Voice Memory for Agentic Speech Recognition
summary: This paper introduces "Voice Memory," an inference-only scheme for agentic speech recognition where a corrector reads a per-domain memory file to make decisions on utterances, and an optimizer asynchronously revises this memory.

title: Mergeable Model-Side Aggregation States for Long-Context Language Models
summary: This research addresses a limitation of long-context language models, their unreliable performance in non-additive, set-based aggregation, by proposing mergeable model-side aggregation states to improve their capability with large context lengths.

title: ForgetBench: Benchmarking Forgetting Dynamics of Long-Term Parametric Memory in Language Models
summary: This paper introduces ForgetBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the forgetting dynamics of long-term parametric memory in large language models, addressing the lack of understanding regarding their knowledge retention under repeated updates.

title: CMT-RAG: Complementary Memory Traces for Multi-turn Multi-hop RAG
summary: This paper introduces CMT-RAG, a system using Complementary Memory Traces to enhance multi-turn, multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by improving how conversational memory is represented and recovered.

title: Which RAG Paradigm Wins at Scale? A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms
summary: This study presents a controlled corpus-scaling evaluation to compare various Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paradigms, including lexical, dense, and agentic search, to clarify their accuracy-cost scaling at different corpus sizes.

title: Where Detectors Fail: Closing the Tail-Domain Gap with Expert-Guided Mutual Distillation
summary: This research proposes Expert-Guided Mutual Distillation as a method to improve the cross-domain generalization of multimodal fake news detectors, addressing their tendency to rely on unreliable evidence and domain-specific shortcuts.

title: WikiLoop: Jointly Learning to Build and Navigate Agent-Native Wikis with Downstream Feedback
summary: This paper presents WikiLoop, a feedback-coupled framework that enables agents to jointly learn how to build and navigate agent-native wikis, integrating knowledge-base construction and querying with downstream feedback.

title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes
summary: This research revisits lossy verification schemes in Speculative Decoding, analyzing their mechanisms, trade-offs, and failure modes to improve the efficiency of large language model inference.

title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability
summary: This paper examines filesystem-based memory for LLM agents, where long-term information is stored and managed as a directory tree of markdown files, discussing its organization, evolution, and sustainability.

title: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains
summary: This research investigates "constitutional midtraining," a method of inserting principled, values-based content during model training to achieve more durable alignment, addressing the shallowness of post-training alignment.

title: Automated Multilabel Mpox Research Classification with Explainable Transformer Models
summary: This paper presents an automated multilabel classification system for Mpox research, utilizing explainable transformer models to categorize scientific literature related to the ongoing public health issue.

title: AtmosERC: Modeling Dialogue-Level Affective Atmosphere for Emotion Recognition in Conversation
summary: This paper introduces AtmosERC, a method for Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) that models dialogue-level affective atmosphere to enhance emotion prediction, addressing the heterogeneity of global context in dialogues.

title: Phoneme- vs. Character-Level Targets and Selective State-Space Models for Intracortical Brain-to-Text
summary: This research explores design axes for intracortical brain-to-text systems, comparing the performance of selective state-space models (Mamba) against recurrent decoders and analyzing the impact of phoneme- versus character-level output targets.

title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model
summary: This paper introduces Metis, a Memory Foundation Model designed to internalize agent memory capabilities directly into foundation models, contrasting with current external module-based memory implementations for AI agents.

title: Relation Geometry in Semantic Space of Language Models
summary: This research investigates the extent to which knowledge about semantic relations is represented in the geometry of semantic spaces generated by language models, focusing on the vector representations of words.

title: Enhancing Generative Information Extraction with Two-step Validation: A Product Attribute Use Case
summary: This paper proposes a method to enhance generative information extraction using large language models through two-step validation, demonstrated with a product attribute extraction use case.

title: When Does Span-Guided Detoxification Help? Human Preferences and Evaluator Diagnostics in a Controlled Comparison
summary: This paper presents an exploratory comparison of span-guided and unguided detoxification methods for language models, evaluating human preferences and diagnostic metrics on a mixed-source English dataset.

title: From Found to Designed: Concepts as a Design Axis for Large Language Models
summary: This paper explores the implicit representation of concepts in large language models and proposes a shift towards designing more explicit, structured, and compositional concept-level structures within LLMs.

title: Language Models are not Equally Robust to Non-Canonical Tokenization across Languages
summary: This research investigates the robustness of language models to non-canonical tokenization across languages, exploring the impact of variations in tokenization beyond the standard deterministic sequences.

title: From Representations to Behaviors: Exploring the Person-Situation-Behavior Triad in LLMs
summary: This paper explores the "person-situation-behavior triad" in large language models, examining how personality-related behaviors and traits are represented and expressed within these systems.

title: SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces SERPO, a novel method for self-evolving rubric policy optimization that enables language models to adapt at inference time without labeled feedback, particularly for open-ended generation tasks.

title: DIRECT: Direct Decoding for Efficient and Aligned Sequence Labeling with Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes DIRECT, a framework designed to improve the efficiency and domain alignment of large language model-based approaches for sequence labeling tasks through training-time optimization.

title: Dual-Path LLM Reasoning for Multimodal Few-Shot Knowledge Graph Completion
summary: This research introduces a Dual-Path LLM Reasoning method for multimodal few-shot knowledge graph completion, aiming to infer missing facts in knowledge graphs with limited data.

title: Latent-IM: Latent Interaction Management for Speech LLMs
summary: This paper introduces Latent-IM, a method for managing latent interactions within speech-enabled large language models, contrasting it with traditional dialogue system architectures where dialogue management was explicit.

title: Same Evidence, Different Target: Decoding How Diagnostic Evidence Bears on Causal Questions from Language-Model States
summary: This research paper investigates how diagnostic evidence informs causal questions from language model states, exploring how different claims and contexts influence the interpretation of evidence.

title: Credit Cards, Confusion, Computation, and Consequences: What Can We Uncover About Language Model Reasoning?
summary: This paper introduces CreditCardQA, a new financial literacy benchmark dataset derived from real credit card agreements, designed to evaluate the numerical reasoning capabilities of large language models.

title: Generation or Judgement? A Paradigm Perspective on LLM-Based Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction in Conversation
summary: This research explores different large language model-based paradigms for emotion-cause pair extraction in conversation, analyzing approaches ranging from generating complete pair sets to judging individual candidates.

title: TREK: A Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit for LLM Agents in Complex Trip Planning
summary: This paper introduces TREK, a Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit designed to stress test and evaluate tool-using large language model agents in complex trip planning scenarios.

title: OptimismBench: Forecasting Bias and the Alignment Effect in Language Model Judgment
summary: This paper introduces OptimismBench, a new benchmark designed to detect and measure forecasting bias and the alignment effect in the probability judgments made by large language models.

title: Evaluating Regional Bias in LLMs From Abstract Stereotype to Concrete Social Decision-Making
summary: This research focuses on evaluating regional bias in large language models, examining how it manifests from abstract stereotypes to concrete social decision-making and proposing a method for its assessment.

title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search
summary: This paper presents DenseOn and LateOn, fully open dense and late-interaction retrieval models, and an open end-to-end recipe for training them for multilingual, long-context, and code search applications.

title: Pangram 4 Technical Report
summary: This technical report presents Pangram 4, the latest deep-learning-based AI-text classification model from Pangram Labs, detailing its performance metrics including an AUROC of 0.9916.

title: APEX-Accounting
summary: This paper introduces APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark developed by Mercor in partnership with Ramp, designed to assess the ability of large language models to perform accounting tasks.

title: Mental World Modeling
summary: This paper explores the concept of Mental World Modeling, proposing an expansion of existing world models to include hidden mental states for a deeper understanding of human behavior, planning, and action.

title: Identifying Implicit Bias in LLM-based Chat AI Toward People with Intellectual Disabilities
summary: This research investigates and aims to identify and measure implicit bias present in large language model-based chat AI models toward individuals with intellectual disabilities.

title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale
summary: This paper introduces GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent designed to discover novel prompt injection attacks against frontier large language models, used to evaluate and improve system robustness.

title: Probing the Origins of Reasoning Performance: Representational Quality for Mathematical Problem-Solving in RL vs. SFT Fine-Tuned Models
summary: This research paper investigates the representational quality for mathematical problem-solving in large reasoning models trained via reinforcement learning (RL) versus supervised fine-tuning (SFT). It aims to uncover the mechanistic basis for RL's observed advantage in these tasks.

title: Cognitive Convergence: Deep Similarities Between Large Language Models and Human Cognition
summary: This paper argues that there are deep similarities between large language models and human cognition, challenging the view that LLMs are fundamentally alien intelligences. It proposes a different framing for understanding their cognitive operations.

title: Position: Evaluation Scores Are Perishable Knowledge Claims
summary: This position paper argues that evaluation scores for language models are perishable knowledge claims due to how aggregation of multiple signals like automated metrics, LLM-as-judge ratings, and human assessments can inflate confidence. It critically examines current evaluation methodologies.

title: The Confounder Trap: Treatment-Encoding Representations in Causal Inference with Text
summary: This research addresses the challenge of estimating causal effects of linguistic properties from observational text due to confounders. It discusses issues with existing approaches that learn representations from the full text.

title: Aligning LLM-Simulated and Human Examinees for Psychometric Calibration: A Cognitive Diagnostic Profiling Approach
summary: This research proposes Cognitive Diagnostic Profiling (CDP), a zero-shot approach, to align large language model (LLM) simulated examinees with human responses for psychometric calibration in educational testing. It aims to address the issue of LLMs being too accurate and uniform for realistic simulations.

title: Knowledge-guided Disentanglement with Atomic Actions for Action Recognition
summary: This research introduces a method for action recognition in complex scenes by using knowledge-guided disentanglement with atomic actions. It addresses the limitation of holistic representations in capturing subtle interactions and fine-grained semantics.

title: Weight and Height Estimation from a Single Human Image Captured in the Wild
summary: This research focuses on estimating a person's weight and height from a single image captured in uncontrolled environments. It addresses the importance of these physical characteristics as indicators of health and daily life routines.

title: TraceCLIP: Recovering Local Semantics from Patch-to-CLS Contributions
summary: This research introduces TraceCLIP, a method for recovering local semantics from patch-to-CLS contributions to enhance dense vision-language understanding. It builds upon CLIP to improve object localization, region recognition, and open-vocabulary semantic segmentation.

title: DVPSFormer: Efficient Online Depth-aware Video Panoptic Segmentation for Autonomous Driving
summary: This research introduces DVPSFormer, an efficient online depth-aware video panoptic segmentation method designed for autonomous driving. It aims to provide a holistic understanding of dynamic environments by simultaneously estimating metric depth, semantic segmentation, and instance trajectories.

title: A Picture Says Thousands of Words - Harnessing Dermal Exposure Data from Images through Hybrid Deep Learning for Enhanced Safety Assessment
summary: This study developed a hybrid deep learning computer vision method to quantify exposed skin from images for dermal exposure assessment. It uses Mask R-CNN and a color-based algorithm to enhance safety assessments.

title: Rad-JEPA 3D: Radiology Joint-Embedding Predictive Model for 3D Computed Tomography
summary: This research introduces Rad-JEPA 3D, a radiology joint-embedding predictive model for 3D computed tomography, focused on self-supervised pretraining for medical image analysis. It aims to improve volumetric encoders to preserve spatial and geometric structure for downstream reasoning.

title: WildShadowRemover: In-the-Wild Video Shadow Removal via Detail-Preserving Video Diffusion Models
summary: This research presents WildShadowRemover, a method for in-the-wild video shadow removal using detail-preserving video diffusion models. It addresses the challenges of complex illumination and diverse shadow appearances in unconstrained real-world scenarios.

title: Where Physics Meets Privacy: Federated PINNs for Privacy-Preserving Brain Tumor Biomechanical Modeling
summary: This research proposes using federated Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for privacy-preserving brain tumor biomechanical modeling. It aims to analyze tumor growth and tissue displacement while addressing privacy concerns with deep learning models.

title: Lag-aware cross-hand alignment for dual-hand action segmentation
summary: This research introduces Lag-Aware Cross-Hand Alignment (LACA), a lightweight module that explicitly estimates and accounts for time-varying delays in coordinated hand transitions during dual-hand action segmentation. It aims to improve the alignment of left- and right-hand representations.

title: Spline-Based Boundary Representations for Sparse View Reconstruction and Simulation Using Isogeometric Analysis
summary: This research explores spline-based boundary representations for sparse view reconstruction and simulation using Isogeometric Analysis. It aims to recover 3D geometry from images in a format well-suited for numerical simulation frameworks.

title: LumaGuide: Distribution Shaping for Training-Free HDR Generation in Diffusion Models
summary: This research introduces LumaGuide, a training-free framework for distribution shaping in diffusion models to enable high dynamic range (HDR) content generation. It addresses the limitations of pretrained diffusion models constrained by statistical biases of their training data.

title: Lightweight Image Classification of Raptor Species for Edge Devices: Rare-Species Dataset Expansion via Video Frame Extraction, Knowledge Distillation, and TensorRT Deployment
summary: This research investigates lightweight raptor-species classification for real-time edge deployment in wind-turbine collision mitigation. It uses video frame extraction for dataset expansion, knowledge distillation from DINOv2-L to smaller models, and TensorRT for deployment.

title: Comparing the Performance of Foundation Model Derived Embeddings with Traditional Approaches for Distant Metastasis Prediction in Head and Neck Cancer
summary: This research compares the performance of foundation model-derived embeddings with traditional machine learning approaches for predicting distant metastasis in head and neck cancer. It aims to improve early prediction for timely interventions.

title: HeteroPROPMT: A Real-time and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception Framework
summary: This research proposes HeteroPROPMT, a real-time and privacy-preserving heterogeneous collaborative perception framework designed to improve autonomous systems' awareness of their surroundings. It addresses challenges arising from diverse sensors and models among collaborating vehicles.

title: Eddeep: a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in diffusion MRI
summary: This research introduces Eddeep, a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in diffusion MRI (dMRI). It aims to mitigate geometric distortions that can cause between-volume misalignment and bias downstream analyses.

title: MoSAIC: Aligned Intervention Supervision for Part-Local Motion Style Transfer
summary: This paper introduces MoSAIC, a method for part-local motion style transfer that allows editing character motion by transferring gestures or gaits from reference motions while preserving other aspects.

title: Seeing or Knowing? Visual Context Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates the visual context sensitivity of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), exploring their failures on vision-centric tasks when visual evidence contradicts pretrained knowledge.

title: Zero-Fi: Zero-Shot Wi-Fi-Based Human Activity Recognition via Contrastive Signal-Language Alignment
summary: Zero-Fi is presented as a novel method for zero-shot Wi-Fi-based human activity recognition, utilizing contrastive signal-language alignment to recognize unseen activities without labeled Wi-Fi samples.

title: Registration-Grounded Spectral Fusion for Unregistered WLI/NBI Endoscopic Lesion Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes a registration-grounded spectral fusion method for segmenting endoscopic lesions from White-light imaging (WLI) and Narrow-Band Imaging (NBI), addressing challenges posed by spatially misaligned images.

title: Do Unified Multimodal Models Think in One Space? A Lens Through Cross-Branch Steering
summary: This research explores whether unified multimodal models (UMMs) possess a shared, transferable semantic space for both understanding and generation, using cross-branch steering as a lens for investigation.

title: FAS-R1: A Unified Multi-Task MLLM for Reasoning Face Anti-Spoofing
summary: FAS-R1 is introduced as a unified multi-task Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed for reasoning-based face anti-spoofing, providing not only decisions but also attack semantics and image-grounded evidence.

title: Interpretable Image-Level Acne Severity Grading via EfficientNet-B0 Transfer Learning and Grad-CAM
summary: This study demonstrates interpretable image-level acne severity grading using EfficientNet-B0 transfer learning and Grad-CAM, aiming to provide accurate and consistent assessments for clinical use.

title: Semantic-Aware Temporal Adaptation for UAV Anti-UAV Tracking
summary: This paper presents a method for semantic-aware temporal adaptation designed for UAV Anti-UAV tracking, focusing on localizing adversarial drones from a moving observer UAV.

title: EgoSafe: A First-Person Mobile-Captured Benchmark for Visual Safety Understanding
summary: EgoSafe is introduced as a first-person mobile-captured benchmark dataset specifically designed for evaluating visual safety understanding and causal reasoning capabilities in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).

title: CineWeaver: Training-Free Reference-Controllable Multi-Shot Long Video Generation for Cinematic Storytelling
summary: CineWeaver is a new training-free method for reference-controllable multi-shot long video generation, enabling cinematic storytelling by addressing the challenges of fine-grained control and extended temporal horizons in text-to-video diffusion models.

title: TPCD: Tone-Pressure Contrastive Decoding and the Label-Free Gating Bottleneck in Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Tone-Pressure Contrastive Decoding (TPCD) to address the issue of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) making unsupported commitments under high-pressure prompts, exploring the label-free gating bottleneck.

title: From Spatial Semantics to Temporal Context: Leveraging Gaze Trajectory for Weakly Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This research proposes leveraging gaze trajectory for weakly supervised medical image segmentation, transitioning from spatial semantics to temporal context to reduce annotation effort while improving accuracy.

title: MedARC: Training-Free Adaptive Redundancy Compression of Visual Tokens for 3D Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: MedARC presents a training-free adaptive redundancy compression method for visual tokens in 3D Medical Vision-Language Models, aiming to efficiently process voluminous 3D medical images.

title: Representation Trajectories Matters: Complementary Evidence for OOD Detection and Image Classification
summary: This paper investigates how representation trajectories within vision models provide complementary evidence that can improve out-of-distribution (OOD) detection and image classification, even on shifted data.

title: Classification of Disease from Lungs X-ray Images using VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet50 Models
summary: This study investigates the use of VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models for classifying diseases from lung X-ray images, aiming for early and accurate detection of respiratory conditions.

title: Level, Sharpness, and Corpus: Why Zero-Shot OOD Detector Rankings Do Not Transfer
summary: This research demonstrates that zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detector rankings often do not transfer across different domains, challenging the assumption that top-ranked detectors will perform consistently in new deployments.

title: R-SLPR: Region-based Small-to-Large Point-cloud Registration with Contrastive Learning
summary: R-SLPR introduces a region-based small-to-large point-cloud registration method utilizing contrastive learning, addressing the challenge of aligning partial point clouds with limited geometric cues in 3D robotic perception.

title: SpatialQ: Understanding 3D Gaussian Splatting Scene Quality via Visual-based MLLM
summary: SpatialQ is proposed as a method to understand the quality of 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes using a visual-based Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM), addressing the demand for reliable quality assessment of 3D reconstructions.

title: Decoupled Visual Processing: Efficient Multimodal Adaptation via Modality-Specific Transformer Substitution
summary: This paper presents a method for decoupled visual processing, enabling efficient multimodal adaptation in MLLMs through modality-specific transformer substitution, reducing computational costs for visual instruction tuning.

title: JEPADepth: Masked Predictive Representation Learning for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
summary: JEPADepth is a new self-supervised monocular depth estimation framework that incorporates masked predictive representation learning as a complementary training objective, moving beyond traditional photometric reconstruction losses.

title: Understanding Knowledge Transfer Mechanism in Heterogeneous MLLM Fusion: A Simple Linear Approach
summary: This paper explores a simple linear approach for understanding knowledge transfer mechanisms when fusing heterogeneous multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in a training-free manner.

title: FakeIDet3-DB: Refining Digital Attacks and Patch Extraction for Secure ID Benchmarking
summary: This introduces FakeIDet3-DB, a new benchmark designed to refine digital attacks and patch extraction methods for securely evaluating identity document (ID) authentication against generative AI manipulations.

title: FPSGen: Flexible Point Cloud Scene Generation with BEV-Supported Transport Flows
summary: This paper presents FPSGen, a flexible point cloud scene generation method that uses BEV-supported transport flows to create outdoor scenes, extending beyond LiDAR-conditioned completion.

title: Genie Sim PanoWorld: An Infinite Indoor 3D World Generation Pipeline via Panoramic Scene Modeling and Simulation
summary: This introduces Genie Sim PanoWorld, a pipeline for generating high-fidelity, infinitely navigable indoor 3D scenes from a single 360-degree panorama without requiring per-scene optimization or multi-view capture.

title: Anchoring and Steering Diffusion: Enhancing the Faithfulness of Text-to-Image Generation at Inference Time
summary: This work proposes a method for Anchoring and Steering Diffusion to enhance the faithfulness of text-to-image generation during inference, improving alignment with complex compositional prompts.

title: Physically Real-time Infrared Attack against Optical Flow Estimation Networks
summary: This research details a physically real-time infrared attack method targeting Optical Flow Estimation Networks (OFENs), which are crucial for applications like autonomous driving and motion detection.

title: Visko Orbis 1.0: A Live Model for Real-Time Interactive Long Video Generation
summary: This presents Visko Orbis 1.0, a Live Model designed for real-time, interactive long-video generation, supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, and video continuation with immediate prompt updates.

title: Sequence-SOD: Bio-inspired Sequence-aware Spiking ObjectDetection for Event Cameras
summary: This paper introduces Sequence-SOD, a bio-inspired sequence-aware spiking object detection method developed for event cameras, utilizing Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for high temporal resolution.

title: TPD: Temporal Prior Decoupling for Text-to-Video Diffusion Models
summary: This introduces TPD (Temporal Prior Decoupling), a method designed to improve the temporal coherence of text-to-video diffusion models, especially for scenes with emerging new events on persistent backgrounds.

title: FreeShadow: Training-Free Shadow Removal via Illumination Transfer and Selective Content Preservation in Diffusion Models
summary: This presents FreeShadow, a training-free shadow removal method that uses diffusion models for illumination transfer and selective content preservation, aiming to overcome generalization limitations of existing techniques.

title: CASIAL: Geometric Distortion Robust Image Watermarking
summary: This work introduces CASIAL, a deep learning-based image watermarking technique that demonstrates strong robustness against geometric distortions like cropping or masking, which are common failure modes for existing methods.

title: Online Handwriting Trajectory Reconstruction from Kinematic Sensors using Temporal Convolutional Network
summary: This research focuses on reconstructing online handwriting trajectories from kinematic sensors using a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), enabling digital pens to accurately capture handwritten input.

title: Dual Inversion for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: From Both Prompt and Noise Perspectives
summary: This paper proposes Dual Inversion for text-to-image diffusion models, improving prompt inversion by considering both prompt and noise perspectives to generate desired target images without extensive engineering.

title: Multimodal fusion of visual and morphometric features for avian bone classification
summary: This study presents a proof-of-concept multimodal AI framework that fuses visual and morphometric features for the classification of avian skeletal remains, addressing a gap in zooarcheological applications.

title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation
summary: This introduces StatePlay, a state-aware game world model designed to generate visually realistic and interactive environments that are consistent with explicit game mechanics and player actions.

title: Long-Tailed 3D Point Cloud Dataset Distillation
summary: This research explores Long-Tailed 3D Point Cloud Dataset Distillation, a method to compress large 3D datasets into smaller synthetic sets while preserving training utility and addressing distributional challenges.

title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?
summary: This paper, titled 'See2Think,' investigates whether multimodal large language models genuinely utilize intermediate visual states like sketches and annotations during their reasoning processes.

title: PRISM-Net: Patient-specific reference-guided inter-breast symmetry matching for three-class breast DCE-MRI classification
summary: This work introduces PRISM-Net, an AI method for patient-specific reference-guided inter-breast symmetry matching, used in three-class breast DCE-MRI classification for broader diagnostic scopes.

title: DistillAlign: Coordinating Mode Covering and Mode Seeking in Autoregressive Video Distillation
summary: This presents DistillAlign, a method for coordinating mode covering and mode seeking in autoregressive video distillation, aiming to improve existing multi-stage pipelines.

title: Ripple: Real-Time Streaming Audio-Video Generation With Cross-Modal Recurrent Memory
summary: This introduces Ripple, a new model for real-time streaming audio-video generation that leverages cross-modal recurrent memory to achieve high quality and low latency for long-form content.

title: Towards Trustworthy Embodied Intelligence: A Systems Framework and Graded Trustworthiness Levels
summary: This paper proposes a systems framework and graded trustworthiness levels for embodied intelligence, which integrates perception, decision-making, control, and physical interaction, aiming to ensure safety and prevent harm.

title: Embodied Agents Take Control: Minimal-Interface Zero-Shot Agents Rival Industrial-Scale Policies in Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: This research investigates agentic embodied control, where minimal-interface zero-shot agents perform vision-and-language navigation by sustaining a decision-making loop involving perception, action, verification, and self-correction.

title: MoMo: Dial Motion Mode in Robot Manipulation with Spatiotemporal Action Tokenization
summary: This work introduces 'MoMo' for robot manipulation, which uses spatiotemporal action tokenization to allow robots to adapt their motion modes and execution-level variations to diverse tasks and interaction settings.

title: Reinforcement Learning on Cost-Constrained Quadrupedal Hardware
summary: This paper addresses challenges in deploying learned control policies on low-cost quadrupedal robots, focusing on transport latencies and noisy motor feedback that create a sim-to-real gap.

title: RLMM-Flow: A Flow-based Mobile Manipulation Framework with Latent-Space Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work presents RLMM-Flow, a framework for mobile manipulation that uses latent-space reinforcement learning and flow-based generative policies to generate whole-body actions for goal reaching and collision avoidance.

title: Explicit Kinematic Guidance from Analytic Concepts for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research introduces explicit kinematic guidance from analytic concepts to enhance Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, improving their spatial awareness and adaptability for complex, high-precision robot manipulation tasks by incorporating 3D physical world information.

title: Speech2Grasp: Data-Efficient Transfer of Text-Conditioned Grasp Detection to Speech in Humanoid Robots
summary: This paper investigates Speech2Grasp, a method for data-efficient transfer of text-conditioned grasp detection to speech in humanoid robots, enabling multi-modal understanding for natural human interaction.

title: ContactFlow: A video action conditioning that transfers across embodiments
summary: This research presents ContactFlow, a video action conditioning method for robot planning that improves world models by capturing physical constraints, particularly contact, and enabling transfer across different robot embodiments.

title: Enfold: Folding World-Generator Computation into Predictive Representations for Efficient Embodied Control
summary: This paper introduces Enfold, a method that integrates world-generator computation into predictive representations for efficient embodied control, aiming to leverage the reusable computation that constructs a future rather than just its output.

title: Vision-TL-Action: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Visual Observations and Temporal Logic
summary: This work presents Vision-TL-Action, a neuro-symbolic approach for trajectory generation for long-horizon robotic tasks, leveraging visual observations and temporal logic to overcome limitations in perception-to-symbol binding.

title: CheckVLA: Execution-Time Verification with Action-Conditioned World Model for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces CheckVLA, an execution-time verification method using an action-conditioned world model to ensure the correctness of long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks executed by Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies.

title: Risk-Aware Motion Planning with Learned Trajectory Primitives and Probabilistic Safety Assessment
summary: This paper proposes a risk-aware motion planning framework for safe and efficient urban autonomous driving, utilizing learned trajectory primitives and probabilistic safety assessment for collision avoidance and trajectory optimization.

title: Route by Kinematics, Act by Observation: Kinematics-Supervised Expert Routing in MoE-Augmented VLA
summary: This research improves MoE-augmented Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for manipulation tasks by introducing kinematics-supervised expert routing, addressing the challenge of kinematic heterogeneity and signal unavailability during inference.

title: Practice Makes Policies: Bootstrapping and Consolidating Robotic Capabilities from Zero Human Demonstrations
summary: This work explores bootstrapping and consolidating robotic capabilities for general-purpose manipulation from zero human demonstrations, enabling robots to learn diverse skills and improve over time in open-world environments.

title: From Uncertainty to Determinism: Coarse-to-Fine Visual Floorplan Localization without Ray Matching
summary: This paper addresses visual floorplan localization for indoor navigation by proposing a coarse-to-fine method that overcomes challenges like cross-modal information asymmetry and repetitive layouts without ray matching.

title: NeoRacer: An Open, Standardized 1:12 Scale Autonomous Race Car for Benchmarking and Education
summary: This paper presents NeoRacer, an open, standardized 1:12 scale autonomous race car designed as a platform for benchmarking and education in autonomous systems research.

title: Dense Soft Weighting for Radar Ego-Velocity Estimation
summary: This research focuses on dense soft weighting for radar ego-velocity estimation, a crucial technique for state estimation in visually degraded environments where camera and LiDAR systems may be unreliable for autonomous vehicles.

title: SymmGrid: Super-Scaling On-Robot Learning with Parallelized Symmetries and Egocentric-Exocentric Visual Perception
summary: This paper introduces SymmGrid, a trajectory-level augmentation framework for super-scaling on-robot reinforcement learning by leveraging parallelized symmetries and egocentric-exocentric visual perception to reduce training times for physical robots.

title: RL$^2$-VLA: Adaptive RL Latent Compositional Steering with Test-Time Scaling for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research introduces RL$^2$-VLA, an adaptive reinforcement learning approach with latent compositional steering and test-time scaling, designed to improve the performance of Vision-Language-Action models on challenging and out-of-domain visuomotor tasks.

title: Controlled Experiments on Lane Changing by Transitional Autonomous Vehicle: Dataset and Behavioral Insights
summary: This paper presents the NC-tALC dataset and analysis from controlled experiments on lane changing behavior by transitional autonomous vehicles (tAVs), quantifying lead-lag gap evolution and providing behavioral insights.

title: DLAM: Distributional Latent Actions with Temporal Constraints
summary: This paper introduces DLAM, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to learn robot actions from scarce labeled data by leveraging abundant action-free videos through latent action models.

title: StructureGS: Structure-aware Gaussian Splatting for Articulated Object Reconstruction
summary: This item presents StructureGS, a novel method based on Gaussian Splatting for reconstructing articulated objects with multiple movable parts, addressing challenges in disentangling geometry, appearance, and motion.

title: From Passive Video to Editable Experience: Physically Grounded Experience Synthesis for Embodied Intelligence
summary: This item introduces Pegasus, a low-resource framework for embodied AI that bridges the embodiment gap, allowing robots to learn from human manipulation videos despite differences in morphology and hardware.

title: Temporally Centered SIGReg Improves Multi-Task LeWorldModel Learning: From Analysis to Method
summary: This research details how Temporally Centered SIGReg improves Multi-Task LeWorldModel learning, enhancing stable end-to-end world-model learning from pixels by preventing representation collapse.

title: What Can Latent World Models Know? Physical Parameter Identifiability in Multimodal Predictive Representations
summary: This research investigates the extent to which latent world models internalize environmental physics, identifying which physical quantities are represented and the factors influencing this knowledge in multimodal predictive representations.

title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?
summary: This work introduces HumanCLAW, a system designed to evaluate whether vision-language models can effectively control a physical robot body, addressing the challenge of distinguishing VLM decision errors from motor control failures.

title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
summary: This item presents TurboVLA, a real-time vision-language-action model capable of operating at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with less than 1 GB of VRAM, offering an efficient alternative to LLM-centric VLA pathways for robot actions.

title: PolygMap: A Perceptive Locomotion Framework for Humanoid Robot Stair Climbing
summary: This paper presents PolygMap, a perception-based locomotion planning framework that enables humanoid robots to accurately perceive and climb stairs in unknown environments, emulating human walking capabilities.

title: Can Context Bridge the Reality Gap? Sim-to-Real Transfer of Context-Aware Policies
summary: This research explores whether context-aware policies can bridge the sim-to-real gap in reinforcement learning for robotics, addressing the challenge of transferring policies trained in simulation to real-world environments.

title: Visibility-Aware Cooperative Tracking with Decentralized LiDAR-Based Aerial Swarms
summary: This paper describes a system for visibility-aware cooperative tracking using decentralized LiDAR-based aerial swarms, enhancing autonomous aerial tracking capabilities for applications like surveillance and inspection.

title: LLM-Grounded Dynamic Task Planning with Hierarchical Temporal Logic for Human-Aware Multi-Robot Handover
summary: This research introduces LLM-Grounded Dynamic Task Planning with Hierarchical Temporal Logic, a framework that enhances large language model-generated plans for multi-robot handover tasks to ensure kinematic feasibility and efficiency.

title: TiPToP: A Modular Open-Vocabulary Robot Manipulation System That Plans
summary: This item introduces TiPToP, a modular open-vocabulary robot manipulation system that integrates pretrained foundation models with a GPU-accelerated Task and Motion Planner to solve tasks directly from images and natural language without specific robot training data.

title: SG-CoT: An Ambiguity-Aware Robotic Planning Framework using Scene Graph Representations
summary: This paper presents SG-CoT, an ambiguity-aware robotic planning framework that uses scene graph representations to enable large language models to iteratively query and clarify ambiguities in environmental understanding for robotic tasks.

title: PACE: Phase-Aware Chunk Execution for Robot Policies with Action Chunking
summary: This item introduces PACE (Phase-Aware Chunk Execution), a method designed to improve the deployment and local motion continuity of robot policies that utilize action chunking, especially those based on vision-language-action and diffusion models.

title: VEGA: Learning Navigation VLAs from In-the-Wild Egocentric Video with Geometric Trajectory Supervision
summary: This item introduces VEGA, an approach for training navigation Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models from unlabeled, in-the-wild egocentric videos, using geometric trajectory supervision to learn from internet-scale data.

title: Invariant Kalman filtering for extended pose estimation in multi-IMU articulated rigid-body systems
summary: This research explores invariant Kalman filtering for extended pose estimation in multi-IMU articulated rigid-body systems, addressing a key challenge in robotics and human motion analysis for accurate orientation, velocity, and position tracking.

title: StairMaster: Learning to Conquer Risky Hollow Stairs for Agile Quadrupedal Robots
summary: This paper proposes StairMaster, a novel three-stage reinforcement learning framework that enables agile quadrupedal robots to safely and stably navigate challenging hollow stairs, mitigating risks of leg trapping and depth sensing issues.
