summary: This research introduces AgenticCANN, a system for automated Ascend C operator generation using knowledge-augmented agentic evolution, aimed at optimizing NPU inference performance despite requiring deep hardware expertise.

title: UrbanDS: A Graph-Guided LLM Multi-Agent System for Data-Intensive Urban Tasks
summary: This paper presents UrbanDS, a graph-guided LLM multi-agent system designed to automate data-intensive urban tasks by discovering and leveraging relevant information from large-scale data.

title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM
summary: This research conducts a causal audit of latent multi-agent LLM systems to investigate whether latent communication channels effectively transmit task-relevant information between agents.

title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation
summary: This research presents a three-class detection framework to distinguish AI agents operating under browser automation from humans and traditional bots, addressing the limitations of binary bot detectors.

title: Belief-Guided Decision Making with Uncertainty Gating in the Game of Go
summary: This paper proposes belief-guided decision making with uncertainty gating in the game of Go, aiming to improve performance on consumer-grade hardware by reducing reliance on intensive Monte Carlo Tree Search.

title: Setoka: A Benchmark for Hierarchical User Understanding in Personalized Agents over Heterogeneous Data
summary: This paper introduces Setoka, a new benchmark designed to evaluate hierarchical user understanding in personalized agents that process heterogeneous data, focusing on their ability to infer abstract personal characteristics.

title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
summary: This paper proposes an on-policy distillation method for large language model (LLM) safety to mitigate the vulnerability of fine-tuning to malicious data providers. It aims to prevent LLMs from retaining professional skills while violating human values.

title: AgentMap: Joint Equivalence and Subsumption Discovery for Ontology Matching
summary: This paper introduces AgentMap, a novel approach for ontology matching that simultaneously discovers both equivalence and subsumption mappings. It addresses the limitation of existing systems that typically only identify one type of semantic correspondence.

title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
summary: This research paper explores the potential for large language model (LLM)-assisted language use to lead to linguistic monoculture. It warns that widespread reliance on shared LLMs may reduce population-level linguistic variation despite improving clarity.

title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
summary: This paper introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon office-suite tasks. It focuses on assessing agents' ability to complete workflows efficiently and at a reasonable cost.

title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
summary: This paper addresses partner capability estimation for task-agnostic adaptation in ad-hoc teamwork among autonomous agents. It aims to improve collaboration by allowing agents to work effectively with diverse partners beyond fixed tasks.

title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
summary: This paper investigates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended AI research, presenting early evidence from two case studies. It examines the feasibility of agents automating research tasks, which is crucial for forecasting future AI progress.

title: A Methodology for Designing Knowledge-Driven Missions for Robots
summary: This paper proposes a methodology for integrating knowledge graphs into ROS 2 systems to enhance the efficiency and intelligence of autonomous robotic missions. It aims to improve how robots plan and execute tasks using structured knowledge.

title: Predict before you train: Scaling Laws for particle physics foundation models
summary: This paper explores scaling laws for particle physics foundation models to predict performance before extensive training, addressing the high cost of developing large machine learning models in the field. The goal is to estimate the return on scaling different model architectures.

title: Archetypes or ability? Clustering for modelling student mathematical competence
summary: This paper explores the validity of assumptions in personalized learning systems regarding mathematical competence by applying clustering techniques to model student abilities. It investigates whether student abilities are better understood as archetypes or discrete, sequentially acquired skills.

title: The Age of AI Agents Demands A New Scientific Paradigm To Sustain Trustworthy Science
summary: This paper argues that the rise of autonomous AI research agents necessitates a new scientific paradigm to ensure trustworthy science. It highlights a widening verification gap as AI systems generate hypotheses and discoveries beyond human oversight.

title: The Easy Trap: Why LLMs Underestimate Misconception-Driven Difficulty
summary: This study investigates why large language models (LLMs) underestimate misconception-driven difficulty when estimating item difficulty in educational assessments. It examines the alignment between LLM-generated ratings and learners' actual experience of difficulty.

title: The Human Utility Factor: A Computable Welfare Metric That Reframes AI Governance as a Constrained Optimisation Problem
summary: This paper proposes the "Human Utility Factor," a computable welfare metric that reframes AI governance as a constrained optimization problem. It argues that existing frameworks overlook quantitative constraints on macro-socioeconomic stability, potentially leading to unintended consequences.

title: AI Security Priorities: A Field-Wide Agenda
summary: This paper presents a prioritized agenda for advancing AI security, addressing the widening gap between AI adoption and security readiness in critical economic, governmental, and national security functions. The agenda is informed by interviews with field leaders.

title: SimpleWikiSearch: A Clean Offline Wikipedia Environment for Agentic Search
summary: This paper introduces SimpleWikiSearch, a clean offline Wikipedia environment designed for evaluating large language model (LLM)-based agentic search systems. It provides a standardized environment to assess agent performance, considering factors like data snapshot and retrieval.

title: GuidedRAG: Semantic Steering of Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This work proposes GuidedRAG, a novel extension to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that incorporates a dedicated selection stage and semantic steering during retrieval. It aims to improve RAG systems by enhancing the precision and relevance of information retrieved.

title: IFCMemoryBench: Evaluating Long-Term Memory of LLM-Based Agents in BIM Information Retrieval
summary: This item introduces IFCMemoryBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the long-term memory capabilities of LLM-based agents in BIM information retrieval, going beyond conversational recall.

title: IDP AutoOpt: Agent-Driven Optimization of Document Processing Pipeline Configurations
summary: This item presents IDP AutoOpt, an autonomous LLM agent engineered to discover optimal configurations for intelligent document processing (IDP) pipelines, reducing manual tuning efforts.

title: FinCacheServe: Dependency-Consistent Answer Reuse for Cost-Efficient RAG Serving over Mutable Enterprise Documents
summary: This item describes FinCacheServe, a system designed for cost-efficient RAG serving over mutable enterprise documents by enabling dependency-consistent answer reuse and managing response caches.

title: A Reference-Free Score for Detecting Silent Reasoning Failures in Large Language Models
summary: This item proposes a novel reference-free score for accurately detecting silent reasoning failures in Large Language Models, which addresses limitations of traditional final-answer based evaluations.

title: (EC)2: Event-Centric Explainability for Cybersecurity Through Multi-Agent LLM Investigations
summary: This item presents (EC)2, an event-centric explainability framework for cybersecurity that uses multi-agent LLM investigations to provide contextual and actionable understanding for anomaly detection.

title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability
summary: This research explores the use of recursive transformers as surrogate models for simulating semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability in engineering design, addressing challenges with small, low-dimensional datasets.

title: Regularizing modality contribution drift in multimodal continual learning
summary: This research investigates methods for regularizing modality contribution drift in multimodal continual learning, aiming to mitigate forgetting and improve knowledge preservation from multimodal data.

title: DoTime: A Synthetic Benchmark Generator for Interventional and Counterfactual Time Series
summary: This item introduces DoTime, a new open and synthetic benchmark generator specifically designed for interventional and counterfactual causal inference over time series, addressing limitations in existing benchmarks.

title: Beyond KV Reconstruction: Functional Reconstruction for MLA Draft Models in Speculative Decoding
summary: This item explores functional reconstruction for MLA draft models in speculative decoding, focusing on optimizing memory management by replacing the growing key-value (KV) cache with compact latent states for long-context LLM inference.

title: RLPF: Reinforcement Learning from Performance Feedback for Code Generation
summary: This item introduces RLPF, a method for training code generation agents using reinforcement learning from performance feedback, enabling them to prefer faster and more efficient correct implementations.

title: SDO: Structure-Aware Data Organization for Efficient LLM Post-Training
summary: This research presents SDO, a method for Structure-Aware Data Organization aimed at improving the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of Large Language Model post-training by optimizing data organization.

title: Flat Score, Amplified Failures: How the Error Budget Masks Damage in Quantized LLM Agents
summary: This item evaluates how post-training quantization to 4-bit weights impacts multi-turn, tool-calling LLM agents, revealing amplified failures on the $\tau^2$-bench despite claims of near-lossless performance.

title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
summary: This theoretical research proposes a driven-nucleation rate law to explain the kinetics of training in language models, detailing the emergence of capabilities, plasticity loss, and circuit control.

title: TIER-MoE: Trust-Informed Expert Routing via Conditional Modality Risk for Multimodal Fusion in Biomedical Classification
summary: This item introduces TIER-MoE, a method for Trust-Informed Expert Routing that leverages Conditional Modality Risk for enhanced multimodal fusion in biomedical classification tasks.

title: EvoCause: LLM-Guided Evolution of Causal Graphs for Root Cause Analysis
summary: This research introduces EvoCause, an LLM-guided method for evolving causal graphs to perform root cause analysis in telecommunication, cloud, and microservice systems. It aims to identify the initiating alarms in correlated alarm cascades.

title: THGFM: Dual-Branch Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Fusion Model
summary: This paper presents the THGFM, a dual-branch temporal heterogeneous graph fusion model designed for learning on dynamic relational systems. It addresses the challenges of jointly modeling cross-type structural heterogeneity and temporal dynamics in such graphs.

title: Position, Not Provenance: Separating Reasoning Mediation from Sycophancy in Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: This research introduces CoT-Mediate, a behavioral framework to investigate whether chain-of-thought reasoning in medical vision-language models causally influences predictions or merely demonstrates sycophancy. It aims to separate reasoning mediation from sycophancy by perturbing clinically meaningful attributes.

title: ZUNA1.1: A more flexible EEG foundation model for Denoising and Super-resolution
summary: ZUNA1.1 is introduced as a 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder, functioning as a flexible EEG foundation model for signal denoising and super-resolution. It can reconstruct variable-length EEG sequences with arbitrary channels and scalp locations.

title: Modeling Decisions in Blockchain Analytics: A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of Tree-Based vs. Sequential Models
summary: This research evaluates different AI models, including tree-based and sequential models, for detecting Sybil bots on Ethereum by treating blockchain activity as a quasi-linguistic sequence. It focuses on the computational expense and effectiveness of these models.

title: Compression-Based Behavioral Similarity for Open-World Sybil Discovery on Ethereum
summary: This paper proposes a novel method for open-world Sybil discovery on Ethereum by leveraging compression-based behavioral similarity among blockchain actors. It builds upon machine learning algorithms to detect attackers who imitate legitimate users.

title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation
summary: This research introduces "Explorative Modeling," proposing a third pretraining axis to enable end-to-end training and generation for generative models, addressing limitations of current generative modeling approaches.

title: The Convergence Behavior of Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise
summary: This paper establishes the first convergence guarantees for the plain vector-form Adam optimizer when subjected to heavy-tailed stochastic noise. It provides insights into its behavior beyond bounded-variance nonconvex optimization.

title: FunL2O: LLM-Guided Feature Function Design for Learning to Optimize
summary: This research presents FunL2O, a method that employs LLMs to guide the design of feature functions for Learning-to-optimize (L2O) pipelines. It aims to accelerate repeated optimization by improving how problem instances are mapped to input features.

title: ECG-InterpBench: Benchmarking the Interpretability of ECG Foundation Models with Matched-Scale Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This paper introduces ECG-InterpBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the interpretability of electrocardiogram (ECG) foundation models. It uses matched-scale sparse autoencoders to assess whether internal representations can be clinically interpreted and reproduced.

title: Context-Informed Ship Trajectory Prediction via Conditional Attention
summary: This research proposes a method for context-informed ship trajectory prediction using conditional attention, enhancing Transformer-based architectures. It aims to improve long-term forecasting horizons for maritime safety and autonomous navigation by incorporating environmental context.

title: Good Rankers, Bad Objectives: Bilinear Contrastive Critics under Expressive Policy Search
summary: This research investigates the behavior of bilinear contrastive critics used as objectives in AI systems for tasks like best-of-K selection and critic-guided generation. It highlights how unbounded scores can lead to inflated off-support values, questioning their safety as maximizable objectives.

title: SE(3)-MeanFlow: Few-Step Protein Backbone Generation on Lie Groups
summary: This research introduces SE(3)-MeanFlow, a new generative modeling method for few-step protein backbone generation on Lie Groups. It aims to improve de novo protein design by providing a more efficient alternative to existing diffusion and flow-matching models.

title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Channel Modeling in Low-SNR Regimes
summary: This research proposes a neural network-assisted CLEAN algorithm to improve multipath parameter estimation in low-SNR wireless communication systems. It addresses the computational challenges of traditional methods while maintaining high-resolution parameter extraction.

title: FADEx: Feature Attribution and Distortion-based Explanation of Dimensionality Reduction
summary: This research introduces FADEx (Feature Attribution and Distortion-based Explanation), a method designed to explain opaque non-linear dimensionality reduction techniques. It aims to clarify how these transformations reduce complexity in latent spaces and assist in model interpretation.

title: Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring
summary: This research introduces Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring, a new method to modify graph topology and alleviate the "over-squashing" problem in Graph Neural Networks. It aims to improve long-range information propagation in GNNs.

title: Latent States in Neural Networks: Recovering the Temporal Structure of Drifting Data from Model Weights
summary: This research investigates whether discrete temporal regimes in drifting data streams are recoverable from the weights of neural networks trained on them. It uses a Hidden Markov Model to analyze the chronological trajectory of model weights.

title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation
summary: This research presents NEXUS, a lightweight foundation model for collider physics that leverages pre-trained learning for multi-domain adaptation to out-of-domain scientific datasets. It uses a fully connected autoencoder model with approximately 3 million parameters.

title: Sparsity Induced Identifiability in Matrix Tri-Factorisation
summary: This research explores sparsity-induced identifiability in matrix tri-factorisation, a fundamental machine learning tool for exploiting low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional data. It provides insights into interpretable representation learning and dimensionality reduction.

title: Expanding Data-Agnostic Pivotal Instances Selection Models with Proximity Trees and Ensemble Learning
summary: This research explores expanding data-agnostic pivotal instances selection models by integrating proximity trees and ensemble learning. It aims to improve the interpretability of machine learning tools in complex decision-making processes.

title: Latent-Kernel Discrete Flow Maps for Few-Step Generation
summary: This paper introduces latent-kernel discrete flow maps, a new method for discrete diffusion and flow-matching models to improve few-step text generation by factoring transitions across positions.

title: When Does Explicit View Routing Work? A Controlled Study of Multi-View Graph-Text Alignment
summary: This study investigates when explicit view routing is effective for multi-view graph-text alignment, where graph-text retrieval typically maps a graph and its description to a single embedding.

title: Subtract or Replay? Exact Deletion from Language-Model Memory
summary: This research explores methods for exact deletion from persistent language-model memory, distinguishing between removing addressable influence and rebuilding for influence transformed by later writes in recurrent states.

title: Memory Efficient Tabular Foundation Models
summary: This paper examines memory efficiency and practical deployment considerations for Tabular Foundation Models like TabPFN, which are noted for their performance in in-context tabular machine learning tasks.

title: Recognition and Label-Free Adaptation Across Recording Sessions in Surface-EMG Gesture Decoding
summary: This study addresses the challenge of maintaining recognition accuracy in surface-EMG gesture decoding across different recording sessions, proposing methods for label-free adaptation when electrode placement or conditions change.

title: Policy Gradient Steering: Interventions from Behavioral Objectives
summary: This paper introduces Policy Gradient Steering, a new method that uses behavioral objectives to enable interventions and dynamically change large language models' behavior during inference, addressing limitations of existing activation steering methods.

title: MUGEN: A Unified Framework for Efficient Motion Understanding and Generation
summary: MUGEN is introduced as a unified framework for efficient motion understanding and generation, aiming to create physical AI systems that can interpret, produce, and communicate human behavior by grounding motion in language.

title: Prox: Training-Free FFN Activation Sparsity via Approximate Intermediate-Channel Salience in LLMs
summary: Prox proposes a training-free method to achieve FFN activation sparsity in large language models, aiming to reduce memory traffic and computation during LLM inference by using approximate intermediate-channel salience.

title: Compliance2LoRA: On-Demand Safety Alignment on Arbitrary Policy Subsets via Hypernetwork-Generated LoRA Adapters
summary: Compliance2LoRA is a method proposed for on-demand safety alignment and personalization of large reasoning models, allowing for varying levels of policy compliance on arbitrary subsets via hypernetwork-generated LoRA adapters.

title: Back from the Future: Key-Value Cache Management by Counter-Causal Surprise
summary: This paper explores key-value cache management for large language models, including compression and eviction strategies, to alleviate computational demands during output generation.

title: Kalman Meets Curriculum: Efficient Dynamic Prompt Selection for Adaptive RL Finetuning
summary: This research introduces a method combining Kalman filtering and curriculum learning for efficient dynamic prompt selection, enhancing reinforcement learning finetuning of large language models by adapting to evolving prompt difficulty.

title: Real-Time Hard Peak Age-of-Information Safety with No-Regret Learning
summary: This paper addresses real-time hard peak Age-of-Information safety for critical IoT systems, such as industrial control and V2X coordination, using no-regret learning to ensure information freshness.

title: Certifying when decision-time information justifies adaptive experimentation
summary: This paper introduces OPAL, a framework that certifies when decision-time information justifies adaptive experimentation, helping to determine if adaptation should be enabled in laboratories that choose measurements during experiments.

title: Evaluation Protocols and Cross-Subject Generalization in EEG Emotion Recognition
summary: This research investigates evaluation protocols and cross-subject generalization in EEG emotion recognition, examining how reported accuracy depends on the complete evaluation procedure and classifier, such as a dynamical graph convolutional neural network.

title: Looped Transformers with Source-Centered State Evolution
summary: This paper introduces Looped Transformers with source-centered state evolution, a novel architecture that reuses the same Transformer block over recurrent depth to increase effective depth at a fixed parameter count.

title: Understanding Submodular Information Measure Based Objectives for Representation Learning: A Variance and Separation Perspective
summary: This paper provides a variance and separation perspective for understanding Submodular Information Measure based objectives, such as those used in the SCORE framework, for representation learning and multimodal learning.

title: FedOGL: Combating Catastrophic Forgetting in Federated Open-World Multimodal Graph Learning
summary: FedOGL is introduced as a framework to combat catastrophic forgetting in federated open-world multimodal graph learning, enabling clients to learn emerging classes from private graph streams while retaining historical categories.

title: Tight Sample Complexity for Low-Rank Adaptation: Matching Bounds and Rank Selection
summary: This paper provides a tight sample complexity analysis for Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a standard mechanism for fine-tuning large pretrained models, and investigates its statistical properties and generalization bounds.

title: Event-Structured Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Differentiable Critical Clearing Boundaries
summary: This paper proposes Event-Structured Physics-Informed Neural Networks for differentiable critical clearing boundaries, aimed at improving transient-stability assessment in power systems by determining the maximum time to clear a fault.

title: NMINE: Normalized Mutual Information Neural Estimation
summary: This paper introduces Normalized Mutual Information Neural Estimation (NMINE), a statistical method for estimating mutual information between continuous and multidimensional random variables from samples. It focuses on capturing both linear and nonlinear dependencies.

title: VESTIGE: A Knowledge-Guided Masking Strategy for Corruption-Aware Fine-Tuning of Genomic Transformers, Validated on Ancient DNA Reconstruction
summary: VESTIGE proposes a knowledge-guided masking strategy for fine-tuning Genomic Transformers, addressing uniform masking limitations when degradation is predictable, and validates it on ancient DNA reconstruction.

title: Towards joint scaling laws with optimal batch size schedules
summary: This research investigates the joint effect of learning rate and batch size on deep learning training dynamics, proposing optimal batch size schedules to improve training efficiency and performance. It analyzes the dynamics through convex optimization.

title: Improving the Robustness/Accuracy Tradeoff Against Adversarial Attacks Using Information Bottleneck Distillation Through Dual Teachers
summary: This paper proposes a method using Information Bottleneck Distillation through Dual Teachers to improve the robustness and accuracy tradeoff of Deep Neural Networks against adversarial attacks. It aims to mitigate the vulnerability of DNNs to malicious inputs.

title: ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation
summary: ROCS (Request-Oriented Compute Sharing) is a proposed modeling and inference paradigm designed to efficiently scale large-scale recommendation models. It addresses production cost constraints by exploiting a unique property for improved feature-interaction and sequence module scaling.

title: DAS-PMVC: A Framework for Partial Multi-View Clustering via Dual Alignment and Structure Enhancement
summary: DAS-PMVC is a new framework for Partial Multi-View Clustering that addresses data misalignment and view asymmetry by employing dual alignment and structure enhancement. It aims to improve clustering performance with incomplete or misaligned multi-view data.

title: Prompt Chaining in Practice: A Case Study in Automated Scholarly Report Generation
summary: This paper introduces and evaluates "Prompt Chaining," a multi-stage prompting method to improve the reliability and quality of automated scholarly report generation. It aims to provide more effective information synthesis for complex tasks compared to single-shot prompting.

title: AI-assisted pre-review of open-source software submissions: an experience report from BOSC 2026
summary: This experience report explores the use of generative AI for pre-reviewing open-source software submissions at conferences, aiming to assist volunteer reviewers with the increasing volume of submissions. It details the application and effectiveness of AI in this specific task.

title: Sympathetic Framing: Evaluating AI Alignment across Sociodemographic Groups
summary: This research evaluates "Sympathetic Framing" to assess how well Large Language Models align with human emotional nuances across different sociodemographic groups. It explores LLMs' understanding of emotional framing and its implications for AI alignment and bias.

title: LayerRAG-Bench: A Cross-Layer Reliability Benchmark for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: LayerRAG-Bench is a new cross-layer reliability benchmark designed to evaluate Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It tests for failures at various layers, including evidence, tool-contract, authorization, and session-state, across multiple enterprise domains.

title: BridgeAlign: Bridging Preference Alignment for Humanities and Social Sciences
summary: BridgeAlign proposes an approach for preference alignment for Large Language Models specifically tailored to the Humanities and Social Sciences. It addresses the challenge of nuanced quality judgments in open-ended domains where objective correctness is less important than subjective quality.

title: HSS-Synth: Humanities and Social Sciences Data Synthesis for LLMs
summary: HSS-Synth introduces a method for synthesizing high-quality, diverse data for Large Language Models in the Humanities and Social Sciences. It aims to overcome the scarcity and cost of data for these open-ended domains, where synthesis is particularly challenging.

title: Same Facts, Different Diagnosis: Measuring and Mitigating Narrative Anchoring in Clinical Language Models
summary: This research identifies "Narrative Anchoring" as a failure mode in clinical language models, where sociolinguistic register influences diagnostic outputs despite identical clinical facts. It aims to measure and mitigate this bias in AI-driven diagnostic reasoning.

title: AHA-Memes: A Fine-Grained Multimodal Benchmark for Understanding Hate in Arabic Memes
summary: AHA-Memes introduces a fine-grained multimodal benchmark specifically designed for understanding hate in Arabic memes. It addresses the underexplored area of hateful meme detection in Arabic by providing a resource for evaluating models' ability to interpret complex multimodal hostility.

title: Benchmarking LLM Competence on Logical Inference over Probability Operators
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking Large Language Model competence in performing logical inference over probability operators, a critical skill for understanding uncertainty in natural language. It aims to evaluate LLMs' capabilities in high-stakes domains like medicine and law.

title: Selecting Open-Weight Language Models for Zero-Shot Intent Classification: A Systematic Evaluation of 41 Models
summary: This paper presents a systematic zero-shot evaluation of 41 open-weight language models for intent classification, providing guidance for practitioners on model selection based on compute, latency, and robustness constraints. It compares models for task-oriented dialogue systems.

title: SkillSmith: Learning to Compose Parametric Skills and Textual Knowledge
summary: SkillSmith introduces a method for agentic systems to learn and compose parametric skills and textual knowledge, enabling Large Language Models to autonomously solve complex problems. It focuses on integrating knowledge synthesis with building skill libraries for recurring sub-goals.

title: Models for minimalist RAG: B1ade 335M Embedding and 1B Parameter Small Language Models
summary: This paper introduces B1ade, an efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture consisting of two purpose-built models: a compact 335M parameter embedding model and a 1B parameter Small Language Model. It challenges assumptions about large-scale pretraining for RAG systems.

title: Belief Coevolution in a Social Network of Generalist and Specialist Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces CoevolveSim, a framework for studying belief coevolution and diffusion within social networks of interacting generalist and specialist Large Language Models. It aims to understand how beliefs form and propagate in multi-agent LLM environments.

title: Training Skills Like Parameters via Self-Supervised Semantic Diffusion
summary: This paper proposes a novel training method, "Self-Supervised Semantic Diffusion," to enable Large Language Models to acquire and apply skills like parameters. It aims to enhance LLM capabilities in specialized, open-ended domains such as creative screenwriting.

title: Beyond Similarity: Grounded Agentic Extraction and Expert-Adjudicated Evaluation of Intertextuality in Classical Chinese Histories
summary: This paper recasts fine-grained intertextuality extraction as an agentic process, moving beyond similarity scores to characterize how and why texts reuse one another.

title: AWARE-FX: An Auditable Knowledge-Guided AI System for Measuring Corporate Foreign-Exchange Hedging Disclosure
summary: This study develops AWARE-FX, an auditable AI/NLP decision-support system, to convert corporate annual report text into traceable foreign-exchange hedging disclosure measurements.

title: DualAnchor: Preserving Language Priors and Improving Lexical Fidelity in Gloss-Free Sign Language Translation
summary: This research proposes DualAnchor to address challenges in LLM-based sign language translation, aiming to preserve language priors and improve lexical fidelity in gloss-free outputs.

title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents
summary: This paper introduces Harness-G, a graph-structured approach to improve reinforcement learning search agents by focusing on retrieval mechanisms rather than just credit signals.

title: From Single- to Cross-Document: Benchmarking Multi-Granularity Event Analysis of Large Language Models
summary: This research benchmarks the capability of large language models for multi-granularity event analysis, evaluating their performance from single- to cross-document contexts.

title: Recall Before You Rank: Similarity-Guided Top-$K$ Reuse for Efficient Long-Context Attention
summary: This paper proposes a similarity-guided Top-K reuse method to enhance the efficiency of long-context attention by optimizing key-value cache access and selection.

title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding
summary: This paper presents train-free self-speculative decoding, an efficiency analysis showing how extending the speculation horizon can accelerate large language model inference.

title: Can LVLMs Uncover the Truth Behind Visual Illusions? An Analysis of Perceptual and Reasoning Capabilities
summary: This study analyzes the perceptual and reasoning capabilities of Large Vision Language Models by evaluating their ability to uncover the truth behind visual illusions.

title: Gradient-free Task-Conditioned Retrieval for On-Device In-Context Learning
summary: This paper proposes a gradient-free task-conditioned retrieval method for on-device in-context learning, optimizing pre-inference context selection from local memories under resource constraints.

title: ChronoMem: Version Control and Semantic Rollback for Large Language Model Agent Memory
summary: ChronoMem introduces version control and semantic rollback for large language model agent memory, addressing the continuous accumulation and overwriting of knowledge in existing systems.

title: Reasoning Consensus: Structural Ensembling of LLM Reasoning via Weighted DAG Aggregation
summary: This paper proposes "Reasoning Consensus," a method to improve large language model reasoning by structurally ensembling chain-of-thought explanations via weighted DAG aggregation.

title: Semantic-Aligned Structural Abstraction for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
summary: This research introduces semantic-aligned structural abstraction to improve multimodal sentiment analysis by integrating natural language with non-verbal modalities based on their structural isomorphism.

title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation
summary: This paper proposes a person-aligned user simulation method for the interactive evaluation of role-playing agents, aiming to improve reliability in measuring their capabilities.

title: AutoSupervision: Closing the Feedback Loop in Scientific Workflows with Grounded Revision Verification
summary: AutoSupervision is an AI system designed to assist scientific research and peer review by providing grounded revision verification, closing the feedback loop in scientific workflows.

title: FinanceHarness: Autonomous Financial Deep Research Framework
summary: FinanceHarness is an autonomous financial deep research framework that leverages LLMs and agentic systems to provide specialized financial analysis.

title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory
summary: This work presents "Memory Decoder at Scale," focusing on a pretrained, parametric long-term memory module designed to scale memory capacity independently in language models.

title: RepBench: Compiling Benchmarks into Capability Representations for Large Language Models
summary: RepBench is introduced as a method for compiling benchmarks into capability representations, enabling more comparable and reproducible measurements of large language models.

title: LEEPS: Latent-Guided Explore-Exploit Prompt Sampling for Efficient RLVR in Large Language Models
summary: LEEPS proposes latent-guided explore-exploit prompt sampling to efficiently improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models through Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).

title: GGC: Selective Query Correction for Reliable Text-to-SPARQL Generation
summary: This paper introduces GGC, a selective query correction method to enhance the reliability of large language models in Text-to-SPARQL generation for knowledge graphs.

title: Challenges in annotations by humans and LLMs: A case study of evaluative language
summary: This paper presents a case study comparing the challenges faced by humans and large language models in annotating evaluative language, analyzing their struggles with complex linguistic phenomena.

title: FinSMART: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Market-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents FinSMART, a method using market-aligned reinforcement learning with post-trained financial large language models (LLMs) for improved financial sentiment analysis in algorithmic trading.

title: Rethinking LLM-Judged Helpfulness as a Pedagogy Signal: A Pre-Registered Audit Across Tutor Models
summary: This study audits how large language models (LLMs) judge helpfulness as a pedagogy signal in tutor models, evaluating if their general rubrics can distinguish direct answers from pedagogical guidance.

title: Can Agents Deceive? Evaluating Reasoning and Deception in ParliamentBench using a Social Deduction Game
summary: This research evaluates the deceptive capabilities of large language models (LLMs) when deployed as agents, using social deduction games to assess reasoning and deception for AI safety.

title: RRM: Experience-Driven Reflective Retrieval Memory for Long-Horizon Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces RRM (Experience-Driven Reflective Retrieval Memory), an improved retrieval mechanism for long-horizon multimodal reasoning in AI agents with long-term memory.

title: Where and When to Commit: Candidate-Aware Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
summary: This research proposes Candidate-Aware Decoding, a method for Diffusion Language Models that enables generation-time early exit to efficiently stop decoding before the full schedule is exhausted.

title: The MADRS Pipeline: Supporting Depression Assessment in Clinical Trials
summary: This paper introduces the MADRS Pipeline, an automated method using AI for text analysis to support depression assessment in clinical trials by detecting the disorder from text samples.

title: Fidelity Is Not Safety: Gently-Compressed LLMs Pass Every Data-Free Quality Guard Yet Invent Procedure Steps in Agentic Execution
summary: This paper reveals a safety concern where gently-compressed LLMs, despite passing quality checks, invent procedural steps during agentic execution, highlighting that fidelity does not equate to safety.

title: Causal Discovery with Inverted Self-attention for Multivariate Time Series
summary: This paper proposes a new method for causal discovery in multivariate time series data, leveraging an inverted self-attention mechanism to address complexities like high dimensionality and nonlinear dependencies.

title: EMBL AI Librarian: Life-Sciences Knowledge Layer for AI Agents
summary: The EMBL AI Librarian provides a crucial life-sciences knowledge layer for AI agents, offering access to extensive literature resources like Europe PMC to support agentic pipelines.

title: Understanding Is Done Early: A Depth Division of Labor in Large Language Models and Its Use for Unbounded-Context Memory
summary: This paper introduces CoMem (Comprehension Memory), a new unbounded-context memory mechanism that leverages the depth division of labor within large language models to store and recall information efficiently.

title: MORFES: A Benchmark for Productive Inflectional Competence in Modern Greek
summary: This paper introduces MORFES (Morphological Open-class Recognition-and-Formation Evaluation Suite), a new benchmark for evaluating the productive inflectional competence of language models in Modern Greek.

title: (Towards) Scalable Reliable Automated Evaluation with Large Language Models
summary: This research explores methods for scalable and reliable automated evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs), addressing challenges in measuring the quality and relevance of their textual outputs.

title: CACHE-UK: A Stability-Aware Memory Editor for Sequentially Updated Quantized LLMs in Finance
summary: This paper introduces CACHE-UK, a stability-aware memory editor designed to maintain the factual accuracy of sequentially updated and quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) in dynamic financial environments.

title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations
summary: This work presents Fairness Pruning, a lightweight structural intervention method to locate and mitigate demographic bias in Large Language Models (LLMs) by analyzing differential activations in GLU-MLP layers.

title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments
summary: This study finds that large language models (LLMs) struggle to accurately simulate human belief updates in controlled environments, questioning their fidelity as proxies for human study participants.

title: Beyond a Single Judge: Simulating Social Persona Panels for Generative UI Evaluation
summary: This research proposes simulating social persona panels for Generative UI evaluation, moving beyond single human or LLM judges to provide more comprehensive and reliable quality assessments.

title: Lightning OPD 2.0: Mitigating Style Bias in Cross-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
summary: This paper introduces Lightning OPD 2.0, an improved on-policy distillation method for large reasoning models that mitigates style bias in cross-teacher scenarios to enhance model performance.

title: Improving Mental Health Screening and Early Risk Detection in Spanish
summary: This paper introduces three new Spanish foundational models designed to improve mental health screening and early risk detection by analyzing long histories of social media posts in Spanish.

title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning
summary: This research identifies and defines 'Salience Bias' in large language models (LLMs), revealing their tendency to over-prioritize explicit conditions during commonsense reasoning tasks.

title: Beyond Sentiment: Structured Information Extraction from Financial News
summary: This research goes beyond simple sentiment analysis by demonstrating structured information extraction from financial news, identifying multiple orthogonal information dimensions like event type and impact scope.

title: Generative AI and linguistic diversity in academic writing and publishing: Perspectives from World Englishes
summary: This article explores how generative AI impacts linguistic diversity and inclusivity in academic writing and publishing, raising questions about the legitimacy of different English variations in scholarly communication.

title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes
summary: This paper examines how AI systems, particularly large language models, reflect and reinforce existing language ideologies and biases within the context of World Englishes.

title: OVEarth-Bench: Evaluating Category Breadth and Query Diversity for Open-Vocabulary Earth Observation
summary: This work introduces OVEarth-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the category breadth and query diversity of open-vocabulary Earth observation systems. It aims to fill gaps in existing benchmarks for localizing geospatial concepts.

title: VETO: Towards Protecting Images From Frontier AI Editing
summary: This paper proposes VETO, a method aimed at protecting images from powerful frontier AI editing models, which have advanced capabilities in extracting, recontextualizing objects, and altering identities in new scenes.

title: Bunraku: Turning a Single Illustration into an Editable Live2D Character
summary: This paper presents Bunraku, a method for turning a single illustration into an editable Live2D character, simplifying the authoring process for 2D character animation in applications like virtual streaming and mobile games.

title: Shared Semantic Codebook Distillation for Unpaired Cross-Modal Medical Classification
summary: This paper introduces Shared Semantic Codebook Distillation, a method for unpaired cross-modal medical classification. It addresses the challenge of transferring diagnostic knowledge between modalities when patient cohorts are different.

title: PanDent: Toward Comprehensive Tooth-Level Structure-Language Consistency in Dental Radiology
summary: This work introduces PanDent, a large-scale, clinically grounded benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate multimodal large language models in dental panoramic radiography. It focuses on achieving tooth-level structure-language consistency.

title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System
summary: This paper introduces VideoCoCo, an agentic dual-engine system utilizing Code-as-CoT for generating physically consistent videos from text prompts. It aims to improve temporal consistency that text-to-video models currently struggle with.

title: IGME: Efficient Chained Method Ensemble for Transferable Semantic Segmentation Attacks
summary: This paper introduces IGME, an efficient chained method ensemble for transferable adversarial attacks on semantic segmentation models. It addresses the computational expense of evaluating such attacks on dense prediction models.

title: ProgFormer: Hierarchical Voxel Diffusion Transformer for Longitudinal Brain MRI Prediction
summary: This paper presents ProgFormer, a hierarchical voxel diffusion transformer model designed for longitudinal brain MRI prediction. It aims to predict future structural MRI changes while preserving global brain structural consistency.

title: Drawing-Recode: Annotation Grounding for Parametric CAD Code Generation from Raster 2D CAD Drawings
summary: This paper introduces Drawing-Recode, a method for annotation grounding that enables parametric CAD code generation from raster 2D CAD drawings. It facilitates part reproduction and manufacturing process automation from legacy designs.

title: Inference-Time Agentic Decision Rules Beat Longer Evolving Search for Multi-Image Medical Reasoning
summary: This paper demonstrates that inference-time agentic decision rules are more effective than longer evolving search strategies for multi-image medical reasoning. It highlights fundamental challenges for medical vision-language agents in aggregating evidence.

title: Objective-Aligned Direct Answer SFT for Robust Multi-Frame Medical VQA
summary: This paper proposes Objective-Aligned Direct Answer SFT for robust multi-frame medical Visual Question Answering. It tests a simpler hypothesis on MedFrameQA, contrasting it with complex adaptation methods for improved reliability.

title: MeshFM: 2D Features Are All You Need for 3D Shape Understanding
summary: This paper presents MeshFM, an efficient feedforward framework for extracting rich features from 3D inputs by distilling 2D features from visual foundation models. The method predicts 3D features directly without inference-time optimization.

title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing
summary: This paper introduces MPIE-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating anatomically plausible multi-person interaction editing in text-to-image and personalized editing models. It addresses major failures seen when synthesizing multiple people in shared actions.

title: MedXplore: Towards Reliable and Unbiased Generalized Category Discovery in Medical Imaging
summary: This paper presents MedXplore, a research effort towards reliable and unbiased generalized category discovery in medical imaging. It aims to overcome limitations of existing deep learning methods reliant on large-scale annotations and closed-world assumptions.

title: 4DHumanDiff: Direct Text-to-4DGS Generation for Consistent 360-Degree Dynamic Humans
summary: This paper introduces 4DHumanDiff, a method for direct text-to-4DGS generation to create consistent 360-degree dynamic human assets. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that often result in incomplete geometry or view-inconsistent renderings.

title: MMOOC: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Out-of-Context Evaluation in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces MMOOC, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating out-of-context performance in multimodal large language models. It aims to assess MLLMs' reliability in refusing out-of-context questions while answering shifted ones.

title: Learning Color Grading, No Photo Sharing: Federated Aesthetic Preference Learning for Personalized Image Enhancement
summary: This paper proposes federated aesthetic preference learning for personalized image enhancement, specifically color grading, without requiring private photo sharing. It addresses learning individual aesthetic tastes from sparse, decentralized feedback.

title: Witness Evidence Portfolios: Single-Prefill Risk Detection for Closed Multimodal Answers
summary: This research proposes a method called "Single-Prefill Risk Detection" to improve the reliable deployment of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by identifying risky or untrustworthy visual answers. It focuses on detecting where visual readouts associated with MLLM confidence scores might be misleading.

title: JigShape: Evaluating Visual-Geometric Reasoning in VLMs through Jigsaw Puzzles
summary: This paper introduces "JigShape," a new benchmark designed to evaluate visual-geometric reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using jigsaw puzzles. Unlike existing benchmarks, JigShape features tab-and-blank interlocking pieces to provide unambiguous ground truth for evaluation.

title: RefineSVG: Visual Feedback-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Image-to-SVG Generation
summary: This research proposes "RefineSVG," a visual feedback-driven reinforcement learning framework that enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to self-correct for high-fidelity image-to-SVG generation. It improves upon existing MLLM-based approaches that rely on single-pass open-loop inference.

title: Calibrate Before Reason: Robust Visual Token Reduction against Semantic Drift in VLMs
summary: This research addresses the efficiency challenge of Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by proposing methods for robust visual token reduction. It aims to reduce inference overhead without causing semantic drift in the model's representation.

title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
summary: This research introduces a new method for reconstructing 3D geometry and kinematic structures of articulated objects from a single rest-state observation. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that require explicit motion data for building interactive digital twins.

title: EgoGVAE: Ego-body Mesh Reconstruction via Guided Variational Autoencoder
summary: This research presents "EgoGVAE," a method for reconstructing the full-body mesh of a person using only head pose information. This task is crucial for applications involving head-mounted devices and smart glasses.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmedical 2026: Architectural Diversity for Concept Detection and Foundation-Model Scaling for Caption Prediction in Medical Image Analysis
summary: This describes the DS@GT submissions to the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 challenge, a long-running benchmark for medical image analysis. It focuses on architectural diversity for concept detection and foundation-model scaling for caption prediction in radiology images.

title: Private Face Recognition Training Dataset Publication via Identity-Decoupled and Geometry-Preserving Face Distillation
summary: This research proposes a method for publishing privacy-sensitive face recognition training datasets by releasing protected proxies instead of original faces. The approach uses identity-decoupled and geometry-preserving face distillation to mitigate privacy risks.

title: CXR-Retrieve: Compositional Text-to-Image Retrieval in Chest Radiography
summary: This research introduces "CXR-Retrieve," a method using vision-language models for compositional text-to-image retrieval in large chest radiography archives. It addresses the difficulty of searching these archives due to free-text reports rather than structured annotations.

title: FDDWAN: A Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Network for Watermarking Attack
summary: This research proposes "FDDWAN" (Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Watermark Attack Network), a new method for invisible watermark removal that aims to overcome limitations of existing techniques. It improves the trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity.

title: LoMeVQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Longitudinal Medical VQA
summary: This paper introduces "LoMeVQA," a comprehensive benchmark designed for Longitudinal Medical Visual Question Answering (VQA). It aims to evaluate models' ability to analyze temporal information from successive medical imaging examinations.

title: SPFM-Net: Semantic-Prior-Guided Frequency-Constrained Mamba for Invisible Watermark Attack
summary: This research introduces "SPFM-Net," a Semantic-Prior-Guided Frequency-Constrained Mamba network for invisible watermark attack. It aims to improve watermark removal effectiveness by capturing long-range dependencies of watermark signals.

title: Hallucinations Leave a Grounding Signature:Verifier-Guided Decoding for Selective Object Correction
summary: This research addresses object hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) by proposing a "Verifier-Guided Decoding" method for selective object correction. It aims to provide reliable object-level grounding diagnostics to mitigate coarse-grained interventions.

title: Thinking Once Is Enough: Intermediate-Layer Evidence Routing for High-Resolution VQA
summary: This research proposes an "Intermediate-Layer Evidence Routing" method to improve high-resolution visual question answering (HR-VQA) by optimizing how multimodal large language models acquire evidence. It suggests that models don't always need to re-inspect images for accurate answers.

title: SAFViT: Spatial Attention Fusion Gating for Vision Transformer-Based Nucleus Segmentation and Classification
summary: This research introduces "SAFViT" (Spatial Attention Fusion Gating), a new Vision Transformer-based architecture for accurate nucleus segmentation and classification in digital pathology. It leverages spatial attention fusion gating to enhance multi-scale feature integration.

title: FeatFix: Reuse What You Verify through Local Exact-Feature Correction for Faster Cached Diffusion Inference
summary: This research proposes "FeatFix," a method to accelerate diffusion models by reusing and verifying cached intermediate features through local exact-feature correction. This aims to reduce the computational intensity of iterative denoising while maintaining image quality.

title: VCP-DCN: Beyond Visual Concealed Property via Depth Collaborative Network for Camouflaged Object Detection
summary: This research introduces "VCP-DCN" (Depth Collaborative Network), a new method for Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) that utilizes depth maps to enhance performance. It aims to better identify and segment objects concealed in complex environments.

title: Benchmarking Foundation and Large Language Models for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This paper focuses on benchmarking Foundation and Large Language Models for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation (FS-MIS). It addresses the challenge of inconsistent evaluation settings across diverse FS-MIS solutions to clarify their relative effectiveness.

title: DECODE: Tackling Representation and Decision Degradation in Continual AI-Generated Image Detection
summary: This research proposes "DECODE" to address representation and decision degradation in continual AI-generated image detection as generative models evolve. It enables detectors to incrementally adapt to new generative domains while preserving previous knowledge.

title: Unifying Adversarially Robust Model Experts in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research addresses the vulnerability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to adversarial attacks by proposing a method to unify adversarially robust model experts. It aims to overcome the specialization of individual fine-tuning strategies to create more robust VLMs.

title: One Patch Is Enough: Reinforcement-Optimized Visual Token Grounding for MLLM-Based Scene Text Spotting
summary: This paper presents a reinforcement-optimized visual token grounding method for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to improve scene text spotting accuracy by reducing noise in previous multi-patch approaches.

title: ARD-REFSM: Enhancing Reflection Symmetry Detection with Asymmetric Denoising and Rotation Equivariance
summary: This research introduces ARD-REFSM, a new method that uses asymmetric denoising and rotation equivariance to enhance reflection symmetry detection, addressing challenges from asymmetric regions and arbitrary pattern orientations.

title: LAST: The Last Query Token Guides Visual Token Pruning for Edge-Cloud Collaborative MLLM Inference
summary: This paper proposes 'LAST,' a method where the last query token guides visual token pruning for edge-cloud collaborative MLLM inference, aiming to reduce cloud-side inference costs by optimizing visual-token sequences.

title: FiRE: Enhancing MLLMs with Fine-Grained Context Learning for Complex Image Retrieval
summary: This study introduces FiRE, a method to enhance Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with fine-grained context learning, improving their performance as universal image retrievers for complex tasks.

title: FootprintNet: State-Transition-Guided Dynamic Footprint Learning for Multi-temporal Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: This research presents FootprintNet, a state-transition-guided dynamic footprint learning method for multi-temporal remote sensing change detection, aiming to better represent dynamic processes over observation periods.

title: Now You Have My Healthy Attention: A U-DiT for Brain-MRI Inpainting
summary: This paper introduces a U-DiT model for brain-MRI inpainting, designed to anatomically complete healthy brain tissue within masked regions, providing a tumor-free reference for medical analysis.

title: ViP-Rig: Visual-Prompted Controllable Rigging
summary: This research presents ViP-Rig, a visual-prompted controllable rigging system that allows artists to easily edit skeletal structures and deformation behaviors based on specific animation requirements.

title: Deep learning-based hierarchical insect classification using camera trap imagery
summary: This study explores deep learning-based hierarchical insect classification using camera trap imagery to enable more efficient and reliable insect biodiversity monitoring.

title: Beyond Classification: Pathology Foundation Models as Detection Encoders for Mitotic Figures
summary: This paper investigates the use of pathology foundation models as detection encoders for mitotic figures, extending their application beyond classification to more complex detection tasks in medical imaging.

title: Split and Drive: Dual-Axis Disentanglement for Real-Time Gaussian Head Avatars
summary: This research introduces a method for real-time Gaussian head avatars using dual-axis disentanglement, aiming to create photorealistic and animatable digital humans from a single image without external tracking.

title: TongueReenact: Geometry-Anchored Tongue Synthesis for Face Reenactment
summary: This paper introduces TongueReenact, the first framework for geometry-anchored tongue synthesis in face reenactment, addressing the common issue of anatomically inconsistent mouth interiors during speech animation.

title: Temporal Concentration from Rollout Errors: Implicit Preference Optimization for Text-to-Video Diffusion
summary: This paper proposes a method for temporal concentration from rollout errors using implicit preference optimization for text-to-video diffusion, aiming to mitigate issues like motion collapse and object flickering.

title: BladeYOLO: Wind Turbine Blade Defect Detection with Limited Annotations and Weak-Saliency Awareness
summary: This research presents BladeYOLO, a wind turbine blade defect detection system designed to work with limited annotations and weak-saliency awareness, addressing the challenges of small, low-contrast defects in real-world inspections.

title: Simulation of Surgical Suturing Using Position-Based Dynamics and the Material Point Method for Robot Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper describes a high-performance simulator for surgical suturing, utilizing Position-Based Dynamics and the Material Point Method to model diverse objects like soft tissue for robot reinforcement learning.

title: Corrigible Assistance in One Round: Pragmatic-Pedagogic Best Response
summary: This paper formalizes 'assistance games' to model human-robot collaboration under asymmetric information, proposing strategies for computing optimal, corrigible assistance in one round.

title: Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via Flow-Matching World Modeling
summary: This research focuses on failure detection for surgical robot imitation policies using flow-matching world modeling, aiming to enhance the safe deployment of autonomous robotic surgery systems.

title: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Behavior-Aligned Representations
summary: This work explores improving cross-embodiment transfer in robot manipulation by leveraging behavior-aligned representations within large-scale imitation learning datasets.

title: A Systems Engineering Framework for Vision-Language-Enabled UAV Triage and Disaster Response
summary: This paper proposes a systems engineering framework for using Vision-Language Models with UAVs for triage and disaster response, enabling responders to interpret large volumes of sensor data.

title: Arm2Air: Cross-Embodiment Skeleton Transfer for 3D Relay Formation
summary: This research presents Arm2Air, a method for cross-embodiment skeleton transfer to optimize 3D relay formation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks in urban environments.

title: LabEvolver: Training-Free Experience Evolution for Safe and Grounded Wet-Lab Agents
summary: This paper introduces LabEvolver, a training-free framework that equips wet-lab agents with episodic memory from execution experience, facilitating adaptive perception, online planning, and safety validation.

title: RedFlow: Redirect Failure into Action-Level Corrections for Flow-matching VLA Policy
summary: This paper introduces RedFlow, a method that uses offline reinforcement learning to correct action-level failures in flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for robotic manipulation, improving robustness during deployment.

title: DexDirect: Direct Kinesthetic Arm Guidance for Efficient Dexterous Demonstration Collection
summary: DexDirect proposes a method using direct kinesthetic arm guidance to efficiently collect dexterous manipulation demonstrations, addressing a major bottleneck in robot learning by offering high precision without costly hardware.

title: RoboBRIDGE: A Modular Framework for Bridging Policies to Robust Real-World Robotic Agents
summary: RoboBRIDGE is a modular framework designed to deploy Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models as robust real-world robotic agents, addressing issues like failure recovery and inconsistent execution for complex manipulation tasks.

title: Learning Social Robot Navigation By Sensing Human Legs
summary: This research explores how robots can improve navigation among pedestrians by learning to interpret 2D LiDAR data, which primarily senses human legs, providing a more accurate understanding of dynamic environments.

title: RaDiVe: Robust 4D Radar Odometry with Distance-Bounded NDT and Velocity-Discrepancy Point Uncertainty
summary: RaDiVe introduces a robust 4D radar odometry framework designed to overcome the challenges of sparse, noisy 4D radar point clouds, enabling better perception and positioning for autonomous systems in adverse weather conditions.

title: When Robots Exchange Meaning: A Demo of Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications for Collaborative Robotics
summary: This demo paper presents a robot-edge semantic communication (SemCom) system for collaborative robotics, focusing on goal-oriented communication where quality is measured by mission execution and environment understanding.

title: SemAnCorr: Semantic Anchored Correspondence for Zero-Shot Manipulation Skill Transfer
summary: SemAnCorr proposes a method for zero-shot manipulation skill transfer in robots, using semantic anchored correspondence to overcome challenges when transferring skills across objects with similar function but different geometry.

title: Machines that know they are aging: a framework for hardware-aware autonomous intelligence
summary: This framework proposes a new approach for autonomous intelligence that accounts for hardware degradation over time, allowing AI systems to adapt to aging components like batteries, sensors, and processors.

title: TEA-AgriVLN: Traversability Estimation Alarm for Agricultural Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: TEA-AgriVLN is a traversability estimation alarm for agricultural Vision-and-Language Navigation, enabling an AI agent to follow natural language instructions to guide a robot through continuous environments by predicting low-level actions.

title: X-NavDP: Generalizing Navigation Diffusion Policy to Novel Behavior and Embodiments with Group Q-score Reweighted Matching
summary: X-NavDP introduces a method to generalize navigation diffusion policies for robots to novel behaviors and embodiments, using group Q-score reweighted matching to improve policy performance in diverse and challenging scenarios.

title: FA-RDP: A Frequency-Adaptive Reactive Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: FA-RDP presents a frequency-adaptive reactive diffusion policy for contact-rich manipulation tasks, allowing robots to handle multimodal actions before contact and then narrow solutions based on geometric and force constraints post-contact.

title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
summary: PAC-MAN is a perception-aware CBF-RL framework designed for whole-body safety in humanoid robots, demonstrating its application in a dodgeball scenario where the humanoid uses onboard sensing for safe interaction.

title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
summary: World Action Planner is a robot planning system designed for generalizable decision-making using action-conditioned world models, addressing the challenge of enabling robots to perform diverse tasks in novel environments.

title: HALO: Heterogeneous Admission through Localized Obligations for Safe Agentic Execution
summary: HALO introduces a mechanism for safe agentic execution in AI systems, allowing for heterogeneous responses to be admitted and processed even if conditions change, rather than rejecting entire responses due to outdated components.

title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
summary: ODEWorld proposes a continuous predictive architecture using physical-time flow for world modeling, addressing the limitations of discrete-time predictions in capturing the continuous dynamics of the physical world within machine learning.

title: Filling the Pareto-Optimal Front for Affordance Segmentation on Embedded Devices Using RGB-D Cameras
summary: This paper proposes methods for affordance segmentation on embedded devices using RGB-D cameras for wearable robots, focusing on hardware-aware neural architecture search to improve robot perception.

title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization
summary: QQWorld presents a method for latent world model regularization using Quantile-Quantile Matching, which improves the quality of learned latent distributions for efficient planning by predicting future states.

title: SharedAssembly: A Data Collection Approach via Shared Tele-Assembly
summary: SharedAssembly introduces a novel data collection approach via shared tele-assembly to gather high-precision demonstrations for training tactile-aware robotic foundation models, overcoming traditional teleoperation barriers.

title: A Three-Stage Offline SDRE-Based Control Framework for Human Motion Reproduction on a Suspended Bipedal Robot
summary: This research details a three-stage offline control framework for human motion reproduction on a suspended bipedal robot, converting captured human movements into executable commands for safe exoskeleton evaluation.

title: A Robust Placeability Metric for Model-Free Unified Pick-and-Place Reasoning
summary: This paper presents a robust placeability metric for model-free unified pick-and-place reasoning, addressing the challenge of reliable manipulation for autonomous robotic systems handling unseen objects in unstructured environments.

title: ARCSnake V2: Mechanical Adaptations For An Amphibious Multi-Domain Screw-Propelled Snake-Like Robot
summary: This paper introduces ARCSnake V2, a screw-propelled snake-like robot with mechanical adaptations designed for amphibious multi-domain exploration in challenging environments like caves and oceans.

title: SUNSET - A Sensor-fUsioN based semantic SegmEnTation exemplar for ROS-based self-adaptation
summary: This research presents SUNSET, a sensor-fusion based semantic segmentation exemplar for ROS-based self-adaptation, addressing the need for robots to adapt to failures in dynamic environments.

title: Relational Scene Graphs for Object Grounding of Natural Language Commands
summary: This research explores using Relational Scene Graphs for object grounding of natural language commands, aiming to improve human-robot interaction by enabling robots to understand and execute complex instructions.

title: Compact Task-Aligned Imitation Learning for Laboratory Automation
summary: This work introduces Compact Task-Aligned Imitation Learning for robotic laboratory automation, aiming to overcome the limitations of large model sizes in generating general robot behaviors from demonstrations.

title: RMBench: Memory-Dependent Robotic Manipulation Benchmark with Insights into Policy Design
summary: This paper presents RMBench, a new benchmark for robotic manipulation that specifically evaluates and provides insights into the memory capabilities of manipulation policies, which often struggle with historical observations.

title: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication for ISAC-Enabled Robotic Obstacle Avoidance
summary: This research investigates a goal-oriented semantic communication framework for ISAC-enabled base stations to efficiently transmit signals for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) obstacle avoidance tasks.

title: SeedPolicy: Horizon Scaling via Self-Evolving Diffusion Policy for Robot Manipulation
summary: This research proposes SeedPolicy, a method using self-evolving diffusion policy for robot manipulation that addresses the degradation of diffusion models when increasing observation horizons for long-horizon tasks.

title: REFINE-DP: Diffusion Policy Fine-tuning for Humanoid Loco-manipulation via Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research presents REFINE-DP, a method for fine-tuning diffusion policies via reinforcement learning to achieve stable and coordinated loco-manipulation for humanoid robots in complex environments.

title: Critic Architecture Matters: Dual vs. Unified Critics for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: This research examines the impact of critic architecture (dual vs. unified critics) in multi-objective reinforcement learning for humanoid loco-manipulation, addressing how to coordinate locomotion and manipulation.

title: A New Human-Likeness and Comfort Index for Robot Movements Along Prescribed Paths
summary: This paper introduces a new human-likeness and comfort index for robot movements, aiming to improve human-robot interaction and robot acceptance by addressing the importance of perceived comfort.

title: Inside Europe's lessons on AI safety as U.S. rules loom
summary: Europe and the United Kingdom are fine-tuning their approach to AI model testing as a deadline looms for the U.S. government to set rules of the road. Why it matters: U.S. allies for years have been grappling with the same AI safety questions the Trump administration now faces. Wherever the U.S. lands in its AI framework, architects of the EU and U.K. approaches say it would be just the start. The big picture: President Trump began his second term by scrapping his predecessor's AI strategy and pursuing an anti-regulatory regime. But as AI models became increasingly powerful fast, the Trump administration has found itself developing an oversight framework and deciding exactly what should be covered. Under Trump's executive order, the administration is due to release its voluntary AI framework by Aug. 1. The Trump administration is weighing a unified pitch from OpenAI and Anthropic to create "an equal playing field" where highly capable models are all covered, regardless of whether they're open- or closed-source, according to one source familiar with the discussions. The EU, meanwhile, has treated AI safety as a sustained technical and policy project for several years. It's a fluid approach to cybersecurity use cases where previous events inform future rules. Zoom in: One lesson from Europe is to start with specific threat scenarios. Researchers begin with historical data on threats such as biological weapons, then measure how much AI increases a bad actor's capabilities and whether that creates a systemic risk to society, CEO and co-founder of AI evaluation firm EquiStamp Chris Canal told Axios. Other key lessons from the EU process include tying benchmarking — testing AI models against standardized evaluations to measure their capabilities and risks — to specific scenarios, such as bioweapons or government database hacks. The EU also emphasizes multiple, independent verifications rather than relying solely on companies' own assessments. Canal worked with the EU and U.K. governments to shape their approaches to AI regulation. Zoom out: The EU commits to getting buy-in from the scientific community, grounding AI risk thresholds in peer-reviewed science before embedding them into policy and pushing researchers to publish their methodologies. By comparison, the U.S. relies mainly on internal or industry-driven standards. Technical experts are also flocking to the private sector, particularly in the U.S. and U.K. What they're saying: "There have been several times where we're working with someone on the [U.K.] government side, and they suddenly put in their two weeks' notice, maybe less, and then they have a great position at OpenAI," Canal said. The bottom line: Governments are beginning to coalesce around cyber risks, but the U.S. and its allies are only beginning to map AI's broader challenges.

title: Publishers are losing Google traffic as AI answers replace links
summary: The way your work shows up in a digital-dominated world is changing lightning fast, starting with the total collapse of Google Search traffic. Why it matters: Google has basically stopped sending people to websites (including our site) for answers and information. Instead, it's using AI to answer them on its platform, in its words. Chartbeat data shared with Axios shows Google Search traffic to publishers fell 34% over the past year. That pain is regressive. Over the past two years, small publishers lost 60% of referrals from search overall, medium publishers 47%, large publishers 22%. This is a gut punch to all of us who operate online because people who search arrive with specific needs and intent, so they tend to be more valuable than a random passer-by from X or Facebook. At the same time, LinkedIn, Reddit and other massive platforms are getting jammed with AI-created content, making it harder to stand out — or decipher real from fake. To that end, Substack announced a partnership last week with AI-detection software Pangram, specifically calling out LinkedIn while arguing that "platforms that reward fakeness will create a race to the bottom." Between the lines: Any smart person who primarily does business online is already anticipating the shift to an LLM, ChatGPT-like world. It starts with GEO — the term for shaping how content shows up inside LLMs like Claude and ChatGPT. This is the modern version of SEO. It's early, and it's a black box. But there's no time to waste. The future: My theory is all of us will need to rethink and reformat our content to meet human AND AI needs. Turns out, our Smart Brevity format — most important point first, context second, information stacked in order of importance, often in bullet form — works wonders with AI. We're among the top publishers surfaced by the leading LLMs, so we're working with companies to see if they can achieve similar results. It's crucial to get ahead of this problem. At Axios, we're already figuring out how we can: Show up inside LLMs now. Improve that standing. Offset reliance on search and open web. Connect with audiences in a post-open-web world. (Direct relationships via things like newsletters and events are a good start.) What's next: The agent wave is coming. Smart publishers have largely stopped treating AI engines as a referral source and now treat them as a distribution layer. Soon, the "customer" reading a website, comparing prices and learning about a product will often be someone's AI agent as the middleman. 📈 If you're a CEO or on a CEO's team: Ask to join Jim's new weekly Axios C-Suite newsletter.

title: How extreme weather is shaping tomorrow's electric grid
summary: A series of dangerous heat waves this summer — including one that has left 17 states under an emergency federal order — are putting the electric grid under an intense real-world stress test. Why it matters: Successive summer heat waves are forcing utilities to rethink how they prepare the grid for longer and more frequent periods of extreme stress. They're raising questions about whether the electric grid can keep pace with surging demand from both climate change and the AI-driven electricity boom. State of play: Heat waves create a double challenge by increasing electricity demand for air-conditioning while reducing the efficiency of some power plants. Zoom in: Texas has become one of the nation's biggest proving grounds for grid modernization since the deadly 2021 winter storm exposed major weaknesses. The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which operates most of the state's grid, has since handled record seasonal demand with the help of rapid battery expansion, mandatory weatherization, improved forecasting and expanded demand response. This month, the Public Utility Commission of Texas approved standards requiring large data centers to disconnect in a controlled way during grid disturbances to help protect grid stability. Yes, but: ERCOT told state lawmakers that statewide electric demand will reach about 175,000 megawatts by 2032 — almost double the record number that was set this month. Between the lines: "Texas has been enormously proactive" in building transmission and adding solar, wind and batteries, retired UC Berkeley electrical engineering professor Sascha von Meier tells Axios. But rapid growth in electricity demand from AI data centers is creating a new challenge, she says. Aidan Tuohy of the Electric Power Research Institute, a nonprofit energy research and development organization, says utilities are shifting from planning for a single peak hour to ensuring they have enough resources to remain reliable throughout prolonged periods of extreme heat. "There isn't one specific resource that's coming up and saving the day or anything like that," says Tuohy, EPRI's director of research and development. "It's a mix, and that diversity is actually a big part of the equation." Zoom out: A growing number of U.S. utilities are linking home batteries, solar panels and EV chargers through software to virtual power plants that can supply electricity or reduce demand during periods of grid stress. "In California, we've had very positive experiences with battery storage and the way that it has performed during extreme peak demand days," von Meier says. She points to a California Independent System Operator study that called batteries "invaluable for reliability" after helping the state avoid rotating outages during a record 2022 heat wave. Tuohy says utilities are increasingly looking at whether large data centers can become flexible grid resources rather than simply new sources of demand. Early results from an EPRI demonstration in Arizona showed a participating AI data center reduced electricity use by 25% over three hours during a simulated peak-demand event. What we're watching: Von Meier expects that five years from now, electric grids will become more agile and flexible, out of necessity. "We may find it no longer realistic to accommodate unlimited demand at uniform reliability across entire interconnections at a reasonable price," she says. "Instead, we will value efficiency, flexible backup options, including storage, self-generation and microgrids, and more active management of electric demand. All the key technologies exist today." The bottom line: Reliability "is going to be won or lost," Tuohy says. "It's not the individual components. It's how they all work together."
